** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2TFKvRBg92qB2mTn4oNeRpi][project thread]]/

Before: =emacsclient -c= against the daemon opens a frame that disappears almost immediately.

After: the client frame stays open and is centered on screen.

=sp-frame.el= adds =sp-frame-recenter= to =after-make-frame-functions= but nothing defines it. The function got lost when =lem-frame-recenter= from lambda-emacs was renamed to the =sp-= prefix. Every frame made through =make-frame= (which is every =emacsclient -c= frame) signals a void-function error. The server then returns the error to the client and deletes the frame it just created. A plain GUI launch never hits this because its initial frame doesn't run that hook.

How: restore the function under its =sp-= name, with the same body as =lem-frame-recenter= in =lambda-emacs-modified/.../lem-setup-frames.el=.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2GSdfx2LDjjW1ejiT3SruTH][project thread]]/

Before: the modules in =.config/emacs-modular/libraries/modules/= existed only as =.el= files, and most had no documentation.

After: =docs/tangles/= has a canonical =sp-*.org= file for each of the 127 modules. Each one holds the module's full source, in order, in =emacs-lisp= blocks, with headings and prose explaining every block. Tangling a doc (=C-c C-v t=) regenerates its module.

*How*

- Each file sets =#+PROPERTY: header-args:emacs-lisp :tangle ../../libraries/modules/<category>/<module>.el :comments no :padline yes :noweb no=, so tangling rewrites the real module file. Nothing tangles unless you run it, because no file sets =auto_tangle=.

- The code was copied by a script, not retyped. Blocks are split only at single blank lines, so =:padline yes= restores each original blank line. Lines starting with =*= or =#+= are comma-escaped. Blocks use =-i= and start at column 0, so indentation survives whatever =org-src-preserve-indentation= is set to.

- 14 modules already had an older doc under the same name, for example =sp-faces.org=. Those older docs are renamed to =<name>-old.org= with their contents unchanged, and the new docs take the plain name.

- =lem-dashboard.el= gets =sp-lem-dashboard.org=.

- Third-party code under =libraries/modules/cloned/= is not included.

- Five modules are empty .el files: =sp-syslinux=, =sp-instant-messenger=, =sp-mail=, =sp-music-comp= and =sp-vulpea-ext-back=. Their docs are literate skeletons with these parts:

  - a file header
  - a Configuration section to fill in
  - a =:tangle no= Sandbox for trying settings
  - a =provide= form

  Tangling one of these writes a valid module that loads, replacing the empty file.

- Commits: there is one commit per module category, then one for the =-old= renames and one for the empty-module skeletons.

*Round-trip check* (Emacs 29.3 / Org 9.6, tangled into a scratch copy and compared with =cmp=)

- 44 modules come back byte-for-byte identical.
- 78 differ only by a final newline. Their =.el= files have no newline at the end, and Org always ends a tangled file with one.
- =sp-org-archive.el= also loses two trailing spaces on its last line.
- All five skeletons tangle to modules that load in =emacs -Q=.

No =.el= file is changed by this PR. Against =main=, 127 files are added and 14 are modified; the modified ones are the canonical names that now hold the new docs.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2CeT7EXLucCBx8drQGW8YWR][project thread]]/

Before: there was no place to track code issues, and working on a dotfiles branch meant checking it out in =~=, which swaps the live config.

After: =M-x sp-org-issues-create-area= creates an "Issues" file as a vulpea-para area (tagged =area=, in the vulpea database), with one heading per repository (dotfiles, vulpea-mcp). =C-c c I= files an issue under a repository, =C-c o a i i= shows an issue board (in progress, next, waiting, open), and =M-x sp-org-issues-start= gives an issue its own git worktree under =~/src/dotfiles-wt/= and opens Magit there. For the dotfiles the worktree is added from the yadm repository itself, so =~= is never touched.

How: the file sets the org-gtd keywords (=TODO NEXT PROG WAIT | DONE CNCL=) with its own =#+todo:= line, and every issue carries =ORG_GTD: Actions=, so a NEXT issue also shows in =org-gtd-engage=. Repository settings (=GIT_DIR=, =WORKTREE_ROOT=, =BASE=) sit on the repository heading and are inherited by the issues. The module requires =sp-vulpea-para= first and appends its capture template and agenda commands, so that module's =setq= cannot wipe them. Closing an issue offers to remove its worktree, and Magit lists untracked files in yadm worktrees (the yadm repo hides them for =~=). =init.el= loads it right after =sp-org-ext=.

The literate source is =docs/tangles/sp-org-issues.org=; it tangles back to the =.el= byte for byte. Tested in batch Emacs with Org and current Magit against a repository laid out like yadm's (vulpea calls stubbed): area creation, capture into an existing and a missing repository heading, both agenda views, starting an issue from the agenda (branch, worktree, PROG), and removing the worktree on DONE.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW29vhgKfRxAMNLbYh7KprHvb][project thread]]/

Before: there was no file tree in the config, so keeping the modules and the docs in =docs/tangles= in view meant switching to dired.

After: pressing =<f9>= opens a treemacs side window rooted at =~/.config/emacs-modular= (=user-emacs-directory=), and pressing it again closes it. Nothing opens at startup.

The tree is rooted at a fixed folder, =sp-treemacs-root=, instead of treemacs' "current project", because the yadm repository's root is =$HOME= and following the project would show the whole home folder.

How: a new module, =libraries/modules/ui/sp-treemacs.el=, installs treemacs through Elpaca (=:ensure t=), binds =<f9>= to =sp-treemacs-toggle=, keeps treemacs' saved workspace in =sp-cache-dir=, and turns on =treemacs-follow-mode=. The toggle is defined in =:config= because it uses the =treemacs-is-path= macro. The module is added to the window management group in =init.el=, after =sp-mini-frame=. Its literate doc, =docs/tangles/sp-treemacs.org=, tangles back to the =.el= byte for byte (checked with =org-babel-tangle-file=), and has a =:tangle no= Sandbox block.

Tested in =emacs -nw -Q= with treemacs from source: =<f9>= is an autoload before first use, the first press adds the root and shows the tree, the second hides it, the third shows it again without adding the root twice.

Before: once =pulse= was loaded, pressing =C-x o= failed with =apply: Wrong number of arguments: #<subr other-window>, 0=.

After: =C-x o= switches windows normally. The line still pulses on window change, and through =pulsar=.

=sp-faces= advised =other-window=, the scroll commands and =recenter-top-bottom= with =pulse-line= using =:after=. Because =pulse-line= is interactive (it's bound to =C-<return>=), nadvice used its empty =(interactive)= spec in place of the advised command's own spec, so =other-window= got no COUNT.

How: this drops the =advice-add= loop from =libraries/modules/ui/sp-faces.el= and from its literate doc =docs/tangles/sp-faces.org=. The doc's prose now says why the advice was removed. Those commands already pulse through =pulsar-pulse-functions= in =sp-windows=. The =C-<return>= binding and the =window-selection-change-functions= hook stay as they are.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2PGHTAG7Ju4Mw8ZC3zoPzju][project thread]]/

Before: discourse-graphs could tell me a claim was contested only through its own dashboards, its status logic was fixed, and the research-question states I had sketched had one catch-all =CONTESTED= state.

After: a new =sp-dg-positions= module draws the positions in a discourse graph the way =sp-vulpea-hierarchy= draws the note hierarchy, with the same kind of interface (=dg-positions-outline=, =dg-positions-graph=, =dg-positions-rankdir=, =dg-positions-graph-file=). It adds one view per status (=dg-positions-status=), a gaps view and a check view. Questions, claims, evidence and sources, the relations between them, the statuses and the gaps are all declared in one readable list, =dg-positions-rules=, so a new relation such as =contests= or =reframes= is one line. A new doc, =docs/tangles/research-question-states.org=, says exactly which state each object should be in; how contested an answer is now lives on the answer, not on the question.

How: the module reads =dg-all-nodes= and =dg-all-relations= from the discourse-graphs database and never writes to a note. =dg-positions-install= copies the declared node types and relations into discourse-graphs' own variables so it parses the new =DG_<RELATION>= properties; run =dg-rebuild-cache= afterwards. The literate doc =docs/tangles/custom/sp-dg-positions.org= is the source and tangles to =libraries/modules/custom/sp-dg-positions.el=; it is loaded from =init.el= after =sp-vulpea-hierarchy=. The doc's nine ERT tests pass in Emacs batch mode, the file byte-compiles without warnings, and the graph was rendered with Graphviz. It has not been run against a real discourse-graphs database.

*Before:* =M-x vulpea-hierarchy-graph= drew every parent/child link in the vault as one Graphviz SVG, which is too large for a big vault. =M-x vulpea-hierarchy-outline= showed the whole tree as Org headings.

*After:* Both commands first ask for a starting note and a depth. =vulpea-hierarchy-graph= opens an interactive graph in the browser: pan, zoom, and click a box to fold it. =vulpea-hierarchy-outline= shows native buttons: TAB or =[+]=/=[-]= expands a note on demand, RET visits it, and =c= picks a new start. The SVG export is kept as =vulpea-hierarchy-svg=. Notes at the last depth show how many children they hide.

*How:* One scope function walks the parent tree from the chosen note to the chosen depth. The browser page is generated HTML with the data embedded as JSON and no external assets. Titles are written with =textContent=, and the JSON escapes =<=, =>= and =&=. The button view reads the full tree from vulpea and expands only the branches you open. Tested on Emacs 29.3 with mock notes (scope, toggling, HTML output, and JavaScript syntax). Not yet run against the real vault database.

- Merged :: 2026-10-20 21:59

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2ApjJf3fNB4nmVud6MqNpBi][project thread]]/

*Before:* =sp-vulpea-hierarchy= knew one relation, =parent=, read from one metadata key (=vulpea-hierarchy-parent-key=).

*After:* =vulpea-hierarchy-relations= declares any number of relations. Each has a label, a colour and a list of sources: a metadata key (=- supports :: [[id:..][..]]=), the inverse of a metadata key (=- children ::= on a parent gives its children their parent edge), or a file property such as =DG_SUPPORTS= (and the inverse of a property). =parent= still builds the tree; =supports=, =opposes=, =informs= and =answers= are declared as defaults, the same names =discourse-graphs= uses. The other relations appear as dashed, labelled, coloured links between two notes that are both in view, in the browser page (with a legend) and in the SVG export. The outlines are unchanged. =vulpea-hierarchy-parent-key= is removed: its value is now the =parent= relation's =(meta "parents")= source.

*How:* =vulpea-hierarchy--edges= reads every source into =(subject relation object)= edges and drops duplicates; =--build= turns =parent= edges into the tree and keeps the rest as =:links=; =--scope= keeps the links whose two ends are in scope. Tested on mock notes with a file property, an inverse key, a repeated key and a comma-separated key, plus a JavaScript syntax check, =dot=, and a headless Chromium screenshot. Property sources have to test every note, because vulpea has no property index. Not run against your real vault, and I did not check how vulpea fills =vulpea-note-properties= there, so please confirm =DG_SUPPORTS= links show up. Stacked on #16 (base is its branch); merge #16 first and GitHub will retarget this one to =main=.

*Before:* every box in the browser graph and the SVG export had the same colour, and a click on a box folded it. The page only knew the part of the tree that Emacs had cut, so it could not move to another note.

*After:* =vulpea-hierarchy-tag-colors= maps a file tag to a colour (defaults for =root=, =idea=, =question=, =claim=, =evidence=, =source=). A note takes the colour of the first of its tags that is listed, drawn as a tint, and the legend lists the tags in view. In the browser, a click on a box recentres the graph on it and remakes the nodes from there. A small ▾ marker folds a branch, =−= and =+= change the depth, and =←= or Backspace goes back to the previous centre. The SVG export uses the same colours.

*How:* the page now embeds the whole tree and runs the depth cut itself (the same breadth-first walk as =vulpea-hierarchy--scope=), so recentring needs no Emacs round trip. For a very large vault this makes the page bigger, since it holds every note of the hierarchy (ids, titles, tags and paths). Tested on mock notes in headless Chromium: tint colours, legend, a recentre, a depth change, back, and a JavaScript syntax check; =dot= accepts the tinted Graphviz source. Not run against your real vault. The literate doc is regenerated and tangles back byte for byte.

The fold marker can never be clicked. It is a ~<text class="fold">~ inside =g.node=, so the later rule =.node text{pointer-events:none}= applies to it. That selector is more specific than =.fold=, and =.fold= sets no =pointer-events= of its own. The marker's click handler never fires, and the click lands on the box instead, which recentres the graph on that box. The fold feature (▾/▸) is therefore dead, and clicking the marker recentres.

Fix by re-enabling pointer events with a selector at least as specific:

#+begin_src css
.node text.fold{pointer-events:all;font:12px system-ui,sans-serif;fill:var(--muted);cursor:pointer}
#+end_src

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2ApjJf3fNB4nmVud6MqNpBi][project thread]]/

Stacked on #17 (which is stacked on #16). Merge in order and GitHub retargets each one.

*Before:* the browser graph put boxes in columns by depth, with parents on the left, and the other relations were drawn as lines between boxes the tree had already placed. There was no way to say where a relation should go.

*After:* each relation in =vulpea-hierarchy-relations= takes a =:direction=: =up=, =down=, =left=, =right=, or an angle in degrees (0 is right, 90 is up, so 45 is up and to the right). It says where the object of the relation is drawn, seen from its subject. Parents now go above their children, siblings sit on one row, and a note with several parents is drawn once and joined to all of them. Defaults: =supports= right, =opposes= left, =informs= 45, =answers= up. The Graphviz default =vulpea-hierarchy-rankdir= is now ="TB"= to match; the SVG export ignores the other directions.

*Backend change (needed for this):* the page's own tidy-tree code could not place a note relative to a note in another branch, so positions now come from the fCoSE force-directed layout, which takes "above/below/left of/right of" rules. The page still does its own drawing. Pros: directions, diagonals and cross-branch rules; multi-parent notes drawn once; deterministic. Cons: about 560 KB of vendored MIT-licensed scripts (=libraries/modules/custom/vendor/vulpea-hierarchy/=, with a README and licences) pasted into each page; heuristic layout that breaks some rules in crowded graphs and is less tidy than a tree; about 0.5 s for 120 boxes; the scripts need manual updates; SVG export has no directions. The full table, and the alternatives I considered (Cytoscape renderer, ELK, d3-force, Graphviz), are in the doc section "Layout backend of the browser page".

*How:* =constraints= turns the tree and each link's direction into relative-placement rules, dropping any rule that would contradict earlier ones; =place= runs fCoSE in a window-less Cytoscape graph; =separate= pushes apart boxes that still overlap. Tested on mock notes in headless Chromium (directions, recentre, depth, back, fold), on a 121-box tree with 25 random links (about 0.5 s, readable but crowded), and =dot= accepts the Graphviz output. Not run against your real vault. The literate doc is regenerated and tangles back byte for byte.

** Description
Stacked on #18 (merge #16, #17, #18 first).

Before: The module was called =sp-vulpea-hierarchy= and only read relations between notes. Node types, the type patterns of a relation, anomaly checks and computed attributes lived in the external =discourse-graphs= package.

After: The module is =sp-relationship-annotator= (=relationship-annotator-*=). Notes can have a type (=DG_TYPE= property, =type= metadata or a file tag), a relation can list the types it should connect, and the browser graph flags other edges with a warning sign. Boxes without a coloured tag take the colour of their type, and an attribute such as =[2]= is shown after the title. =relationship-annotator-review= lists anomalies, claims with gaps and the strength of each answer. The old variable and command names stay as obsolete aliases, so =sp-dg-positions= (#12) keeps reading the rankdir.

The port covers the node types, relation patterns, the anomaly check, the formula language for attributes, argument gaps and answer strength. The formula parser has no global state, takes relation names from the configuration and stops on self-references. The SQLite cache, the websocket UI and node/link creation were not ported; =docs/relationship-annotator-vs-discourse-graphs.org= compares the two and lists what was left out.

How: the discourse layer works on the tree that =--build= returns, with an index of edges standing in for the SQL queries. The literate doc was regenerated and tangles to the .el and .html byte for byte. Tested on mock notes in Emacs 29.3 and headless Chromium, not on a real vault.

Stacked on #20 (which is stacked on #19, #18 and #17). Merge in order and GitHub retargets each one.

*Before:* about thirty modules spelled out =~/notes=, =~/bibliography=, =~/Documents/literature=, =~/src= and the like, so the configuration only worked with one machine's layout and a test run could not be kept away from the real notes. =init.el= ended in a Custom block with a list of =/Users/siainbuletin/notes/...= agenda files, which made =org-agenda= open every one of them. The system modules sat in their own =env/= directory.

*After:*

- A new first module, =sp-paths=, names each location once (=sp-notes-dir=, =sp-documents-dir=, =sp-literature-dir=, =sp-bibliography-dir=, =sp-org-dir=, =sp-src-dir=, =sp-git-dir=, =sp-clones-dir=, =sp-data-home=, =sp-yadm-repo=, =sp-chrome-history-file=) and offers =sp-path= to build a path below one. The modules use these instead of literals. Each location can be overridden from the environment (=SP_NOTES_DIR=, =SP_BIBLIOGRAPHY_DIR=, =SP_DOCUMENTS_DIR=, =SP_ORG_DIR=, =SP_SRC_DIR=, =SP_GIT_DIR=, =SP_CLONES_DIR=, =XDG_DATA_HOME=). Defaults come from =~=, and the Chrome history path has a macOS, Windows and Linux default. This prepares for =sp-syswin= and the Linux module, which are not part of this PR.
- =env/= moves to =base/= (=sp-env=, =sp-exwm=, =sp-macos=, =sp-syslinux=, =sp-syswin=), in =libraries/modules/= and in =docs/tangles/=. The tangle paths, =docs/main.org= and =conditional-loading.org= follow. =sp-env= requires =sp-paths= and explains in its commentary that the =SP_*= overrides are read before the shell environment is imported.
- The whole Custom block at the end of =init.el= (=custom-set-variables= and =custom-set-faces=) is removed, so =sp-vulpea-para= decides which agenda files load. A copy of the removed block is kept outside the repo in case anything in it should come back.

*Behaviour notes:*

- On your Mac every path default resolves to what it was before.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW212AZe9AuXK5zGyitrMyoeN][project thread]]/

Based on =main=. It does not depend on #17 to #20 or #22, which touch other files; the day stamp file simply uses =sp-cache-dir= when it exists.

*Before:* =sp-org-issues= could show the issue board, but nothing told me each morning what to do first across issues and pull requests.

*After:* =M-x sp-org-issues-morning= opens a read-only =*Morning*= Org buffer with one ranked list of the open issues and the open pull requests of the repositories in =sp-org-issues-repos= (plus =sp-org-issues-morning-extra-repos=). It also appears once, on the first Emacs start of each day. Ranking, highest first: failing checks (100), merge conflict (90), changes requested (85), approved and green (80), an issue whose PR is gone (75), waiting for my review (70), then issues by PROG 60, NEXT 50, WAIT 20, TODO 10. Deadlines add up to 30, a waiting PR gains a point a day up to 10, and a PR stacked on another open one loses 15 per level and says "only after #N". An issue and its PR (the =PR= property) are one line. All scores are in =sp-org-issues-morning-scores=. The full rule, the TDD workflow and how to brief Claude for it are in the guide =tdd/tdd-with-claude.md= in the project files.

*How:* pull requests are read with =gh pr list --json= (needs =gh auth login=), one repository after the other without blocking Emacs; without =gh= the list shows the issues and says so, and a repository that fails is named at the top. The code is written test first: 25 ERT tests in the =* Tests= section of the literate doc tangle to =tests/sp-org-issues-test.el=.

Run them with =emacs -Q --batch -l tests/sp-org-issues-test.el -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit= from the folder of =init.el=.

*Tested:* the 25 tests pass in headless Emacs 29.3, including the fetch against a fake =gh= script. I saw them fail before the code existed and broke the stack rule on purpose to check that the right test fails. The doc tangles to the module and to the test file.

*Not tested:* the real =gh= (this session cannot use GitHub's GraphQL API), the real vulpea area lookup, the =*Morning*= window and the startup greeting in the full configuration. Please run =M-x sp-org-issues-morning= on your Mac.

/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW22ykMMYap3WBMUhHviqhAoA][project thread]]/

*Before:* testing a pull request of the Emacs config meant checking its branch out in =~= and restarting Emacs, and a PR could write to the real notes.

*After:* the fish function =emacs-pr N= (in =.config/fish/functions/emacs-pr.fish=) fetches =pull/N/head= through yadm into a detached worktree at =~/src/dotfiles-wt/pr-N= and starts a second Emacs on it with =--init-directory=. That Emacs runs with =HOME= set to a throwaway folder holding an APFS copy of =~/notes=, so the PR cannot change the real notes. All sandboxes share one package cache, cloned from your live =var/elpaca= (with elpaca's absolute build symlinks repointed), so no PR reinstalls packages it already has. =emacs-pr rm N=, =emacs-pr reset= and =emacs-pr reseed= clean up. The new README section "Testing a pull request in a sandbox" documents usage, what it does, what is not isolated, and what to do when something fails.

*How it was checked:* the function passes =fish -n=, and I ran it against a local stand-in for the yadm repository, with stub =emacs= and =cp=, to check the fetch, the worktree creation and re-run, the sandbox home, the cache clone, the symlink repointing and the launch arguments. It was not run with real yadm, Emacs or APFS (this container is Linux), so the first real run on the Mac is the test.

Before: =init.el= ended with Customize-generated =custom-set-variables= and =custom-set-faces= blocks (about 190 lines, mostly a snapshot of =org-agenda-files=), and =sp-fonts= set the default face three times in competing ways.

After: =init.el= has no such blocks. Every setting is in the module that owns it, and =custom-file= points to =var/etc/custom.el= (set in =early-init.el=, never loaded), so Customize can't write into =init.el= again.

| Setting                                                                                                   | Now                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Fonts (=sp-ui-default-font=, =sp-ui-variable-width-font=, =ha-= lists, direct =set-face-attribute= calls) | =sp-fonts= is rebuilt around =fontaine=: one =regular= preset, Aporetic Sans Mono 150 as the default face, Aporetic Serif Mono 120 as variable-pitch (placeholder until the variable fonts are organised) |
| =sia/modeline=                                                                                            | default changed to =doom-modeline= in =sp-choose-modeline= (matches its commentary)                                                                                                                       |
| =bibtex-aux-opt-alist=                                                                                    | =:custom= of =use-package bibtex= in =sp-bibprocess=                                                                                                                                                      |
| =transient-show-menu=, =helm-minibuffer-history-key=                                                      | =:custom= in =sp-base-libraries=                                                                                                                                                                          |
| =org-default=, =org-extra-emphasis*= faces                                                                | =set-face-attribute= in =sp-org-emphasis=                                                                                                                                                                 |
| =custom-safe-themes=                                                                                      | dropped; =sp-themes= already sets it to =t=                                                                                                                                                               |
| =org-agenda-files=                                                                                        | dropped; =sp-org-agenda= sets the directories and =sp-org-node-mem= rebuilds the list after each scan                                                                                                     |
| =package-selected-packages=, =package-vc-selected-packages=                                               | dropped; elpaca does not use them                                                                                                                                                                         |

Docs for the touched modules and =CHANGELOG.org= are updated.

Not verified (no Emacs in the container):

- =fontaine= preset keys and =fontaine-restore-latest-preset= follow its documented API but were not run; the default face is now Aporetic Sans Mono 150 instead of the PT Mono 120 that used to win at the end of startup.
- =M-+=, ~M-=~ and =M--= now change the default face height by one point; =fontaine-set-preset= resets it.
- Until =org-mem= finishes its first scan, the agenda uses =~/notes/area/= and =~/notes/inbox/= instead of the old saved list of about 150 files.
- A theme that defines the Org faces could override the =set-face-attribute= values; the old =custom-set-faces= always took precedence.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW22ykMMYap3WBMUhHviqhAoA?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW22ykMMYap3WBMUhHviqhAoA][project thread]]/

Follow-up to #24 (merged).

*Before:* =emacs-pr= gave all sandboxes one shared =elpaca= folder and one shared notes copy, so only one sandbox could safely run at a time, and a sandbox could only be started from a shell.

*After:*

- Each PR gets its own =var/elpaca=, an APFS clone of a seed that is itself a clone of the live =var/elpaca=, and its own =HOME= with a clone of =~/notes= (=~/.cache/emacs-sandbox/home/pr-N=). Any number of sandboxes can run at once, next to the live Emacs. Only the native-compile cache is still shared, which Emacs supports. =emacs-pr rm N= deletes everything of a PR, =emacs-pr reset N= refreshes its notes, and =emacs-pr reseed= drops the seed.
- A new module, =sp-sandbox=, adds =M-x sp-sandbox-pr= (the number defaults to the =22= or =#22= at point), =sp-sandbox-remove=, =sp-sandbox-reset-notes= and =sp-sandbox-reseed=. They run the fish function in a separate process from the Emacs you are working in and show its output in =*emacs-pr*=.
- The README section "Testing a pull request in a sandbox" describes the new layout and the commands. Chemacs2 is not needed: =--init-directory= already gives each worktree its own packages, and the isolation comes from the per-PR =HOME= and clones, which a Chemacs2 profile would not provide.

*How it was checked:* the function passes =fish -n=. I ran it against a local stand-in for the yadm repository, with stub =emacs= and =cp=, for two PRs, a re-run and =rm=. Each PR's build symlinks pointed into its own =elpaca=, each got its own home, and =rm= removed one without touching the other. The Emacs commands were run in batch against a stub =emacs-pr= (arguments, output buffer, number at point), and =sp-sandbox.org= tangles to =sp-sandbox.el= identically in Emacs 29.3. I did not run any of this with real yadm, Emacs or APFS, so the first real launch on the Mac is the test.

Replaces #22, which GitHub would not reopen after its branch was rebased (#18 to #20 are merged into =main=, so this PR is no longer stacked).

*Before:* about thirty modules spelled out =~/notes=, =~/bibliography=, =~/Documents/literature=, =~/src= and the like, so the configuration only worked with one machine's layout and a test run could not be kept away from the real notes. =init.el= ended in a Custom block with a list of =/Users/siainbuletin/notes/...= agenda files, which made =org-agenda= open every one of them. The system modules sat in their own =env/= directory.

*After:*

- A new first module, =sp-paths=, names each location once (=sp-notes-dir=, =sp-documents-dir=, =sp-literature-dir=, =sp-bibliography-dir=, =sp-org-dir=, =sp-src-dir=, =sp-git-dir=, =sp-clones-dir=, =sp-data-home=, =sp-yadm-repo=, =sp-chrome-history-file=) and offers =sp-path= to build a path below one. The modules use these instead of literals. Each location can be overridden from the environment (=SP_NOTES_DIR=, =SP_BIBLIOGRAPHY_DIR=, =SP_DOCUMENTS_DIR=, =SP_ORG_DIR=, =SP_SRC_DIR=, =SP_GIT_DIR=, =SP_CLONES_DIR=, =XDG_DATA_HOME=). Defaults come from =~=, and the Chrome history path has a macOS, Windows and Linux default.
- =env/= moves to =base/= (=sp-env=, =sp-exwm=, =sp-macos=, =sp-syslinux=, =sp-syswin=), in =libraries/modules/= and in =docs/tangles/=. The tangle paths, =docs/main.org= and =conditional-loading.org= follow. =sp-env= requires =sp-paths= and explains in its commentary that the =SP_*= overrides are read before the shell environment is imported.
- The whole Custom block at the end of =init.el= is removed, so =sp-vulpea-para= decides which agenda files load.

*Behaviour notes:*

- On your Mac every path default resolves to what it was before.
- Removing the Custom block also drops what it set besides the agenda files (fonts, =sia/modeline=, =custom-safe-themes=, =package-selected-packages=, =helm-minibuffer-history-key=, =transient-show-menu=, =bibtex-aux-opt-alist= and the four =org-extra-emphasis= faces). They fall back to defaults until set in a module.

*How:* the literate sources in =docs/tangles/= are edited together with the modules. The branch content is the same as #22 (rebased onto =main= with the merged #20); I did not start the full configuration, so please try a launch on your Mac.

*Before:* no way to turn loose thesis ideas into tasks from Emacs.

*After:* =M-x sp-thesis-dump= opens a buffer for a brain dump. =C-c C-c= sends it to Claude, which returns annotated Org =TODO= tasks (summary, tags, effort, citekeys), a checklist of citekeys to look up (checked by Emacs against the =.bib= files, so "missing" does not depend on what Claude says) and open questions. The answer opens in a review buffer; =C-c C-c= files it under a heading of the task file (created if missing).

*Portable:* =sp-thesis-dump.el= needs only Emacs 28.1, Org 9.5 and the =claude= command. Project variables (task file, heading, bib files, TODO keywords, tags, citation style, citekey style, outline file, language) are prompted for when missing and can be saved in the project's =.dir-locals.el=; =C-u M-x sp-thesis-dump= asks for all again. Machine settings (the =claude= command, =--mcp-config=, =--allowedTools=) are global and never read from =.dir-locals.el=. Copy the one file into the thesis repo's Emacs setup.

*How "org-mcp" is used:* MCP puts the model in the client role, so Emacs cannot send to Claude through an MCP server. Emacs runs =claude -p= in the project directory, and if =sp-thesis-dump-claude-allowed-tools= lists the org-mcp tools, Claude can read the Org files for context. Emacs does the filing. Without MCP the prompt carries the existing headlines, known citekeys and an optional outline file.

*Also:* literate doc =docs/tangles/custom/sp-thesis-dump.org= (tangles the module and a companion Claude Code skill =docs/skills/thesis-brain-dump/SKILL.md= for the same job outside Emacs), =init.el= loads it after =sp-sandbox=, entries in =docs/main.org= and =CHANGELOG.org=.

*Tested:* byte-compiles without warnings on Emacs 29.3; settings, prompting and saving to =.dir-locals.el=, prompt, parsing (including a code fence), rendering, filing under a nested heading and the failure path were run in batch Emacs against a stand-in =claude= script.

*Not tested:* the real =claude -p --output-format json= envelope, reading the prompt from stdin, =--mcp-config=/=--allowedTools=, the org-mcp tool names, the GUI on macOS, and the skill.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW26cs7ZQYxbbiqDNfMZAWuBV][project thread]]/

*Before:* =relationship-annotator-graph= wrote a static HTML file and opened it from disk, so the graph was a snapshot and needed a new run after every edit.

*After:*

- =M-x rel-anno-graph= now opens a live view: a new module =sp-relationship-annotator-live= serves the same page from Emacs on =http://127.0.0.1:8765/=, rendered from the vulpea database on each load. The old static command is =rel-anno-graph-static= (unchanged otherwise, and the SVG export is untouched). Also =rel-anno-live-open=, =-start=, =-stop=, =-refresh=; options =relationship-annotator-live-port= and =-debounce=. =/graph.json= returns the nodes and edges.
- *Shorter command prefix.* All interactive commands use =rel-anno-= (=rel-anno-svg=, =rel-anno-review=, =rel-anno-outline-native=, =rel-anno-outline-vui=, the three outline-buffer commands and the live ones). *The obsolete aliases are removed*, including the old =vulpea-hierarchy-*= ones, so the old command names no longer work; nothing else in the repo used them. Variables and internal functions keep the long prefix.
- *No polling.* An open page holds a Server-Sent Events stream. Emacs watches the folder of =vulpea-db-location= with =file-notify=, waits until it is idle (debounced), cuts the tree for each open page and compares a SHA-1 of the data with the one the page was rendered from. Only a different hash sends a message, so editing a note that is not in the graph reloads nothing. A page that reconnects after a drop is compared the same way, so changes made meanwhile are not lost.
- On a reload the page restores the note it was recentred on, pan, zoom and folded branches (kept in =sessionStorage=).

*How:* a small server on =make-network-process=, bound to 127.0.0.1 (not configurable), GET only, rejecting any =Host= header that is not localhost with this port. I did not use =simple-httpd= (one global server rooted at =/var/www=, all interfaces by default). On =vulpea-graph=: the analysis found no rendering code to reuse (metrics and lists only), so only its neighbour-walk idea applies, already done by =relationship-annotator--scope=; I did not read =vulpea-graph-ui=. Literate doc in =docs/tangles/custom/sp-relationship-annotator-live.org=; the annotator doc and =docs/main.org= are updated; =init.el= loads the module after =sp-relationship-annotator=; =CHANGELOG.org= entries added.

*Tested* (Emacs 29.3, in a container, real annotator code with stubbed vulpea/vui and three fake notes): the modules tangle from their docs and byte-compile. A batch Emacs served =/=, =/graph.json=, =/favicon.ico=, 404, 403 (wrong Host or port), 405 (POST). With an event stream open: a db file touch without a data change sent nothing; a title change plus a touch sent =changed=; a stale =since= hash on connect and =-refresh= sent it; a closed stream was dropped; stop closed everything. Headless Chromium on a live server: the page drew, a recentre plus pan and zoom survived a data-triggered reload, no JS errors.

*Not tested:* real vulpea (whether =vulpea-db-autosync-mode= writes =vulpea-db-location= or its =-wal= soon after a save, and that name being right on your version), your vault and its size (a check builds the tree in Emacs while idle), macOS file notification (fsevents/kqueue), the idle timer in an interactive Emacs (batch has none; the test used a plain timer), the outline buffer keys and the vui outline (not run), =browse-url= with your browser. If the watch cannot start, a message says so and =rel-anno-live-refresh= remains.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2PrmYxQzcZ3Bkjp14GNgEA7][project thread]]/

*Before:* clicking a box in the =relationship-annotator-graph= page did nothing. The page called =setPointerCapture= on the =svg= at every =pointerdown=, so the browser sent the following =click= to the =svg= and never to the box, and =recentre= was never called.

*After:* a click on a box recentres the graph on it: the box becomes the centre and its own children and other relations are drawn (within the =relationship-annotator-embed-depth= levels the page holds). The pointer is captured only once a press has moved more than 4 pixels, so plain clicks reach the box and drags still pan. Boxes can also be reached with Tab and recentre on Enter or Space (the keyboard path ignores the stale =dragged= flag, which stays true after a drag until the next press).

*How:* three edits in =sp-relationship-annotator.html= (pointer capture moved into =pointermove=, =tabindex=/=role= and a =keydown= handler on boxes, a focus outline). The literate doc =docs/tangles/custom/sp-relationship-annotator.org= has the same code and its prose and line numbers are updated; its HTML blocks tangle to exactly the new file (checked by script). =CHANGELOG.org= has an entry.

*Overlap:* the thread "Live localhost graph view" is adding a localhost view of the same graph and may touch the same page template. This change is small and only touches the box click handling, drag code and one CSS line, so a conflict should be easy to resolve.

*Tested:* reproduced the bug and the fix in headless Chromium with the real template and vendored libraries and a small made-up tree: a mouse click on a box recentres (broken before, works after), a drag pans without recentring, and Tab/Enter recentres, also after a drag.

*Not tested:* Emacs could not be installed in the container, so =relationship-annotator-graph= itself, the real vault and Sia's browser were not run, and I added no ERT test (the changed code is JavaScript in the page; the repo has no test setup for modules). Not changed: the native buffer outline (=relationship-annotator-outline-native=), where RET on a title visits the note and =c= re-scopes by prompting. If "the buffer" meant that view, tell me and I'll make a click or RET there recentre on the note.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2LyHQi7b6T67FotQ1nucEdp][project thread]]/

*Before:* the live relationship graph (=sp-relationship-annotator-live=, on =127.0.0.1=) could only be opened in an outside browser.

*After:* a new module =sp-embr= (=libraries/modules/custom/=, loaded in =lem--late-modules= after the live module) adds two more viewers and a comparison, all showing the same live page:

- =M-x rel-anno-live-embr=: [[https://github.com/emacs-os/embr.el][embr.el]], a headless Chromium whose CDP screencast frames are drawn in a buffer. Needs Emacs 30.1, Python 3.10 and a Chromium it downloads (=M-x embr-install-or-update-chromium=); upstream says macOS is "Unknown".
- =M-x rel-anno-live-xwidget=: Emacs's own =xwidget-webkit=, a native WebKit view (needs xwidgets; =sp-md= already uses them).
- =M-x rel-anno-live-compare=: embr on the left, xwidget on the right.
- =rel-anno-live= / =rel-anno-graph= are unchanged and still open the normal browser. Each new command asks for the note and depth the same way (and shares the remembered ones), starts the server if needed and uses the live module's URL and port, so there is no separate host/port setting. A viewer that is unusable or errors falls back to =sp-embr-fallback-function= (=browse-url=). =sp-embr-open= and =sp-embr-open-xwidget= take any URL.
- Elpaca installs embr from GitHub (recipe from its README), only on Emacs 30+. Literate doc =docs/tangles/custom/sp-embr.org= has a checklist of what to compare (pan/zoom smoothness, CPU and memory, rendering, input, live reload); entries in =docs/main.org= and =CHANGELOG.org=.

*Brought up to date:* =main= is merged in (including the renamed =rel-anno-= commands, the moved late-module list and the removal of the academic block from =init.el=); one conflict in =init.el= resolved by dropping the old block and adding =sp-embr= to =lem--late-modules=. A merge of =main= that was pushed to the branch in the meantime is merged too.

*Tested:* Emacs 29.3 in a container: the module tangles from the doc, byte-compiles without warnings, and the three commands were run in batch against stubs of the live module (scope, server start and URL), with the =browse-url= fallback and the two-window layout.

*Not tested:* embr itself (Emacs 29 is below its 30.1 minimum), the Elpaca recipe, the Chromium install, =xwidget-webkit-browse-url= and the side-by-side layout with real xwidgets (a new session is assumed to display in the selected window), the real live module, anything on macOS.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2XeAdUCvg6CzkNNnvnLZg74][project thread]]/

*Before:* three Vulpea table modules (=sp-vulpea-dblock=, =sp-vulpea-vui-table=, =sp-vulpea-table-views=) that had to be required in order, with positional saved views, =vui= as the only interactive renderer, and a few bugs (sorting by title did nothing, =|= in a cell broke the Org table, editing a heading's row rewrote the file's top meta, inline tables left the note modified after a save).

*After:* =sp-vulpea-table= is the one entry point (=sp-vulpea-ext= requires only it) and loads six parts around one query description, a plist:

- =-core=: spec, one =vulpea-db-query= predicate (tags all/any/none, directories, TODO states, links, meta key/value, parent, level, title regexp), cells, sorting, writing meta back, refresh broadcast.
- =-menu=: a transient menu (=C-c w T=) showing each setting's value beside its key; open, preview count, insert as =vulpea-table= block, save/load/delete views.
- =-views=: saved views as spec plists; the first version's file is converted when read.
- =-org=: the =vulpea-table= dynamic block (title links, escaped cells) and a read-only Org buffer renderer.
- =-exc=: a renderer that draws the table with [[https://github.com/yibie/grid-table][exc]] (needs Emacs 29.1 and ETAF): frozen header, meta columns editable in place and written to the note, =C-c o= / =C-c q= / =C-c C-u=.
- =-vui=: the old vui table and inline tables, ported to specs, kept as the fallback.
- =sp-vulpea-table-renderer= is =auto= (exc, then vui, then org), =exc=, =vui= or =org=. Old =sia-vulpea-*= commands remain as obsolete aliases.

Packages come from =use-package= with Elpaca =:ensure= recipes (ecss, ebox, etaf with =:files ("*.el" "lisp/*.el")=, and exc from =yibie/grid-table=, the only address that resolved). exc is not part of emacs-taf; it is built on it.

Docs: one literate doc =docs/tangles/funct/sp-vulpea-table.org= writes all seven files (tangles back identical) and replaces the three old docs; =docs/main.org= module tree and =CHANGELOG.org= updated; the requires in the =sp-vulpea-ext= and =sp-vulpea-grouped-backlinks= docs follow.

*Tested* (container, Emacs 29.3, real Vulpea database of 3 then 1000 notes, no display): every filter, sorting, the dynamic block, view save/load and old-format conversion, writing meta back (and refusing a heading note), the Org, vui and exc renderers, in-place editing and the read-only guards in exc, the menu's commands with prompts stubbed, byte-compile. Opening 1000 notes, uncompiled: exc about 2.1 s, vui 2.8 s, Org 2.9 s.

*Not tested:* the menu on screen, tables in a graphical frame, mouse use, vui field editing, inline tables, Elpaca building ETAF and exc (the recipes are untested), the Transient version on your Mac, anything on your real notes or macOS. A step-by-step plan for comparing exc and vui is in the project files (=renderer-test-plan.md=).

*Before:* =org-ql= was installed in =sp-org-base=, and =org-super-agenda=, which =org-ql= requires, a few modules later in =sp-org-agenda=. Elpaca queued it as a dependency first and warned =org-super-agenda previously queued as dependency of: (org-ql)=. =emr= (in =sp-prog-misc=) had the same problem with =paredit=, installed by =sp-lisp= further down the list. Every module loaded during startup.

*After:*

- =org-ql= moves to =sp-org-agenda=, right after =org-super-agenda= (=.el= and the literate doc).
- =sp-lisp= loads before =sp-prog-misc=.
- Twelve leaf modules (=sp-academic=, =sp-dgraphs=, =sp-relationship-annotator=, =sp-notes=, =sp-semantic=, =sp-dyn-graph=, =sp-sandbox=, =sp-vcontrol=, =sp-magit-style=, =sp-terminal=, =sp-eshell=, =sp-ai=) are in =lem--late-modules= and load 0.5 s after Emacs first goes idle once Elpaca has finished its queues. =sp-defer-late-modules= = =nil= loads them with the rest. No other module requires them.
- =docs/load-order.org= (linked from =docs/main.org=) has two Graphviz graphs (rendered SVGs beside it), the table of requirements behind each arrow, and a checklist for placing a new module. CHANGELOG entry added under a "Startup and module load order" set.

*Checked:* Emacs 29.3 reads =init.el= and the changed modules; the module list is the same set as before; the late-module functions ran against stubs (twelve modules required in order, queues processed). The requirements come from the =Package-Requires= headers of =org-ql=, =org-super-agenda=, =emr=, =org-ref=, =org-gtd=, =org-node=, =code-review=, =vulpea-ui=, =treemacs=, =claude-code=, =gptel-agent= and others, read from GitHub.

*Not checked:* a real startup. Elpaca cannot reach MELPA from the container, so I have not seen the warning disappear, nor that the late modules install and configure their packages after init (I read =elpaca.el=, which suggests they do once =elpaca-process-queues= is called). Keys defined only in late modules (for example =C-M-g= for magit) work from about a second after startup. Duplicate explicit declarations (=hl-todo=, =org-autolist=, =elisp-demos=, =company=) are left alone.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW21jZfxe5AmskoMP3AYBnVbr][project thread]]/

Stacked on #48, which is stacked on #45. Merge in that order; GitHub retargets each PR as its base merges.

Before: the splash colours were two fixed greys chosen for dark or light backgrounds, plus the box face.

After: a small framework of colour roles.

- A role (=art=, =banner=, =footer=, =accent-1..3=) takes its colour from a face of the current theme (=shadow=, =font-lock-keyword-face=, ...) mixed towards the default background, so the lambda stays quiet and the accents stay vivid in any theme. =sp-splash-palette-roles= says which theme face, attribute and mix each role uses, so adding a role is one line.
- =sp-splash-palettes= lets you choose colours for a particular theme by hand; roles not listed are still derived.
- The menu boxes are coloured with the accent faces in turn (=sp-splash-accent-faces=), so each block has its own colour.
- The splash is recoloured and redrawn when a theme is enabled or disabled (=enable-theme-functions=, =disable-theme-functions=; switch off with =sp-splash-palette-follow-theme=). =sp-splash-apply-palette= and =sp-splash-show-palette= do it and show it by hand.
- =sp-splash.org= has a new "Colour palette" section and tangles to the same text as the =.el=; CHANGELOG entry added.

Checked in headless Emacs 29.3 with faces set by hand: the roles came out as derived colours, a per-theme override won, the three boxes got the three accent faces, and enabling a test theme with a red =shadow= recoloured the art. Not checked: how the derived colours look on your real themes; tune the mix values in =sp-splash-palette-roles= if the art is too faint or too strong.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW21mXvibxgZ5NzrmRV92h1on][project thread]]/

*Before:* checkbox lists under a =Tasks= heading in the vault are invisible to the agenda and org-gtd, and TODO-like words (=DOING=, =WAITING=, =STARTED=, ...) that are not declared in =init.el= or in the file are plain text to Org.

*After:* new module =sp-org-normalise= (=libraries/modules/custom/=, literate doc =docs/tangles/custom/sp-org-normalise.org=, listed in =docs/main.org=, loaded from =init.el= after =sp-org-issues=).

- =M-x sp-org-normalise-inventory=: every keyword-like heading word with heading and file counts, how many files do not recognise it, and what the mapping table does with it.
- =M-x sp-org-normalise-preview=: report buffer of proposed changes per file; =RET= visits a change. Writes nothing.
- =M-x sp-org-normalise-run=: the preview, then per file yes / no / choose each change / quit. Buffers are left modified and unsaved (=sp-org-normalise-save-after-apply= to change).
- Checkbox items under a =Tasks= heading become child headings: =[ ]= TODO, =[X]= DONE, =[-]= PROG. Nested lines stay in the body. A checklist under a heading that already has a keyword is left alone.
- =sp-org-normalise-keyword-map= (editable) rewrites =DOING=, =WAITING=, =CANCELLED=, ... to the org-gtd set; words not in it are only reported. A =#+todo:= line is proposed for files that would otherwise use an unknown keyword; files with their own sequence are only noted.
- Code blocks and drawers are never read. All =defcustom=s are in the group =sp-org-normalise=. No external packages.

*Checked* (headless Emacs 29.3, container only, fake vault in a temp directory): 24 ERT tests in =tests/sp-org-normalise-test.el= (tangled from the doc), plus a manual run of inventory, preview and apply on a small fake vault. The tests started red and were fixed (case-folding of the keyword regexp; undeclared words wrongly triggering a =#+todo:= line).

*Not checked:* the interactive prompts (=read-char-choice=, =y-or-n-p=) and the report buffer in a real Emacs, and anything on the real vault, TRAMP or Windows paths. The default map rewrites =DOING= and =WAITING=, which =sp-org-taskman-extra= currently sets globally; remove them from the map if you want to keep those.

Run it with =emacs -Q --batch -L libraries/modules/custom -l tests/sp-org-normalise-test.el -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit= from the =init.el= folder.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2Ncux17Yj6ANSAph5xngrN3][project thread]]/

Modelled on Obsidian's [[https://github.com/mdelobelle/obsidian_supercharged_links][Supercharged Links]].

**** What it does
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what-it-does
:END:
- *=sp-tag-emoji=* (=libraries/modules/custom/=): =sp-tag-emoji-rules= maps a tag, or a list of tags that must all be present, to =:emoji= and/or =:face= (and =:position= prefix/suffix for links). =sp-tag-emoji-mode= shows the tags of the heading at point, or the file's =#+filetags:=, as emoji in the modeline (or header line), and decorates =id:= links with the emoji and face of the tags of their note, read from the vulpea db. A combination rule uses up its tags, so =("@writing" "deep")= replaces the two single emoji. =sp-tag-emoji-check-rules= lists rule tags missing from =org-tag-alist=, so that stays the single tag registry.
- *=sp-emoji-font=* (=libraries/modules/ui/=): prepends the first installed colour emoji family (Apple Color Emoji, then Noto Color Emoji, ...) to the =emoji= fontset. On Linux, =sp-emoji-font-file= or =M-x sp-emoji-font-install= installs an Apple Color Emoji =.ttf= into =~/.local/share/fonts/sp-emoji/=. The font is not bundled (Apple's licence).
- Literate docs in =docs/tangles/custom/sp-tag-emoji.org= and =docs/tangles/ui/sp-emoji-font.org=; =init.el=, =docs/main.org= and CHANGELOG follow.

**** Checked (Emacs 29.3, headless, container)
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: checked-emacs-293-headless-container
:END:
Both docs tangle; the rules, the combo logic, the heading/file/both sources, inheritance, the modeline string, the header-line placement, the link overlays and face (with a fake tag lookup), turning the mode off, and picking the font from a faked font list.

**** Not checked
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-checked
:END:
How the emoji render in a graphical frame, whether lambda-line prints =global-mode-string= (use =sp-tag-emoji-placement= = =header-line= if not), the vulpea lookup against a real database, and the Linux font install with a real TTF. The Apple =.ttc= shipped with macOS does not work on Linux; a CBDT-format =.ttf= is needed.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2HrSnCzQDTcWT2ugso36vjb][project thread]]/

Stacked on #59 (it rewrites the header of =sp-org-lint=); retarget to =main= after #59 merges.

*Before:* notes written with Org's default behaviour end in a =Footnotes= heading, but this setup keeps each definition at the end of the text of the heading that cites it (=org-footnote-section= is nil; =sp-vulpea-split= copies definitions per heading).

*After:* =M-x sp-org-lint-footnotes= in =sp-org-lint= (docs: =docs/tangles/funct/sp-org-lint.org=, "Sectional footnotes").

- *Async:* the files of the vulpea database are read by a second headless Emacs (=make-process=), one at a time; a report buffer fills in as results arrive. Emacs stays usable.
- *Preview first:* the scan changes nothing. =a= in the report applies, after a yes/no question.
- *What moves:* each definition in a =Footnotes= heading goes to the end of the own text of the heading that contains its reference (same section meaning as =sp-split--fn-section=). Cited from several sections: every section gets a copy, later ones with a suffixed label (=smith-2=), as in =sp-vulpea-split=. An emptied =Footnotes= heading is removed; one with other content stays.
- *Reported, never deleted:* orphan definitions, dangling references, and conflicts (label defined twice, cited from the footnotes heading itself, cited only from another footnote).
- *Safety:* every file is copied to =sp-org-lint-fn-backup-directory= (per-run folder) before being written; a file that changed since the preview, is open with unsaved edits, has CRLFs, or fails the post-check (reference count, dangling set and definition count) is skipped. Written via temp file and rename. Open unmodified buffers are reverted and vulpea is asked to re-read the files when idle.
- =C-u= asks for a folder instead of using the vulpea database. No external packages.

*Checked* (headless Emacs 29.3, container only, fake vault in a temp directory): 11 ERT tests in =tests/sp-org-lint-test.el= (tangled from the doc), including a real run of the worker process: scan, apply, backup content, and a file changed after the preview. A 300-file fake vault scans in about 2 s in the worker. The =.el= byte-compiles without warnings.

*Not checked:* a real Emacs session with the report buffer on screen, the vulpea database query (=vulpea-db-query=; not loaded here, the folder fallback was used), macOS, TRAMP, and the real vault. Run the preview on the vault and read it before pressing =a=.

Implements the proposal from the thread's analysis doc. Reasons and alternatives are in =adr/0009-one-agenda-owner-per-setting.org= and =adr/0010-phase-out-denote.org=.

*Agenda*

- =sp-vulpea-para= turns on =vulpea-para-agenda-mode=: it owns =org-agenda-files=, filters =cemetery= notes (=sp-vulpea-para-agenda-note-p=, tested), and keeps =inbox.org= always listed. The three other =org-agenda-files= settings are gone.
- The =org-mem= agenda hook is removed from =sp-org-node-mem=; the old code is kept in ADR 0009.
- New =sp-org-keywords= is the only setter of =org-todo-keywords= (one constant per use) and gives =vulpea-para-done-keywords=. Its doc has a use-case table with empty columns to fill in, and the removed Workflow Status settings.
- =sp-agenda-views= assigns =org-agenda-custom-commands= once (PARA, native and issue views) and holds every agenda key; =sp-org-issues=, =sp-org-base= and =sp-org-taskman-extra= point to it. Commands that restrict the files bind =vulpea-para-agenda-inhibit-files-update=.
- =org-agenda-prefix-format= is one alist in =sp-org-agenda=.
- The =sp-denote= agenda hooks are removed; Denote is to be phased out (ADR 0010).

*Capture*

- =sp-org-capture= assigns =org-capture-templates= once (t, i, p, I, n, l); the only inbox is =~/notes/inbox.org=.

*Load order*: =sp-org-keywords= after =sp-org-base=; =sp-org-capture= and =sp-agenda-views= last (=init.el=, both lists; =sp-org-ext= no longer requires them). =docs/load-order-modules.svg= is redrawn.

*Not done / to check*

- Nothing was run with the real packages. Run vulpea-para's backfill once so existing files get the =agenda= tag.
- =C-c d c= (org-gtd capture) is unbound; =C-c d p= still processes org-gtd's own inbox.
- Dashboard/splash link and org-ql in the agenda were left out as asked.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2XXKDQ5Dp5crxRdWfcttAXb][project thread]]/

New module =sp-merge-pick= (=libraries/modules/prog/=, doc in =docs/tangles/prog/sp-merge-pick.org=, which tangles to the module byte for byte).

*Flow*

1. =C-x C-SPC g m= opens a graph log of all branches (unicode lane glyphs, Magit's colours). In the yadm repo start from =M-x yadm=.
2. =C-c v i= marks the commit at point as INTO, =C-c v f= another as FROM. Both lines are highlighted and labelled.
3. =C-c v p= previews the merge in memory with =git merge-tree --write-tree= and lists conflicting files; =RET= on one opens a three-way Ediff (INTO, FROM, merge base). =C-c v d= shows what FROM adds, =C-c v e= picks any file for the same Ediff.
4. =C-c v n= starts a =--no-commit= merge (after asking, and after offering to check out INTO's branch if the worktree is clean). Then resolve with Magit =e=, Smerge or =M=, commit with =c c=, or abort with =m a=.

Only step 4 changes the worktree. Nothing commits.

*Wiring*: module added to the late list in =init.el=; =sp-keys= autoloads =sp-merge-pick-log= on =m= in =lem+vc-keys= (code and doc); =load-order.org= lists the module; CHANGELOG set "Reviewing merges in Magit".

*Tested* in headless Emacs 29.3 with Magit from Oct 2026 on a small repo with a conflict: log buffer, marks and overlays, glyph display properties, the preview and conflict list, the file buffers handed to Ediff (Ediff call stubbed), the no-commit merge including checking out INTO's branch, and the byte-compile (clean).

*Not tested*: the Ediff session itself, colours and glyph widths in a real GUI or TTY, =C-c v= on the yadm repo, git older than 2.38 (the preview needs it). =docs/load-order-modules.svg= is not redrawn.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2Y1zBiwrAYWiD24zS6xVdwc][project thread]]/

Fixes the errors seen when starting Emacs from =main=, and audits the other =use-package= forms.

*Root causes*

- =Cannot load goto-last-change / rainbow-mode / treemacs-nerd-icons / org-contrib / openwith=, and =ns-auto-titlebar/:init=: these forms had no =:ensure=. Elpaca's =use-package= support installs nothing by default; =elpaca-use-package-by-default= in =init.el= does not exist in current Elpaca (checked in its source). The =locate-library= guards removed in #61 used to hide this.
- =Failed to parse package consult-snapfile ... sp-path=: =use-package= reads a list given to =:load-path= as a list of paths and evaluates each symbol as a variable. The path now goes through the constant =sp-consult-snapfile-dir=.
- =which-key loaded before Elpaca activation=: the raw =(which-key-mode 1)= in =sp-keys= autoloaded the built-in package early. Removed; the existing =use-package which-key= enables the mode. The stray =(which-key-mode +1)= =:custom= entry is removed too.

*Audit (second commit)*

- All other third-party =use-package= forms without =:ensure= now have =:ensure t= (about 70). =inheritenv= used =:straight=, which this config does not use; =org-focus-hud= gets =(:host github :repo "SSD2019/org-focus-hud")=.
- Left alone: =tramp=, =pulse=, =org= (built-in), =exwm= (module not loaded), =excali= (local checkout), =citar-org-node= (=:vc=).
- Reordered so Elpaca does not queue a dependency first: =company= before =company-quickhelp=, =go-mode= before the Go helpers, =auctex= before =auctex-latexmk= and =company-auctex=.

Module docs in =docs/tangles/= are updated and their code blocks match the =.el= files. CHANGELOG: one entry in "Startup and module load order" (after #61), and a duplicated =Fixed= entry removed.

*Not tested* (no Emacs here): nothing was loaded or byte-compiled. =use-package= and Elpaca behaviour was read from their sources. I could not reach MELPA or GNU ELPA from the container, so I assumed the package names (for example =go-complete=, =dot-mode=, =pcomplete-extension=) exist there; an unknown name will show up as an Elpaca error on first start. Please start Emacs and check =*Messages*= and =M-x elpaca-log=.

*Stacked on #72* (merge #72 first; GitHub then retargets this to =main=). Both touch the =sp-org-ext= require, =docs/main.org= and the CHANGELOG.

*Before:* the table family (PR #43) was named after Vulpea, though it is a personal module for querying a collection of notes.

*After:* files and features are =sp-collection-query-tables= (seven files in =libraries/modules/funct/=, doc =docs/tangles/funct/sp-collection-query-tables.org=); every symbol (function, command, setting, customize group) uses the short prefix *=sp-collec-query-=*. The doc has a section, "Names: why the prefix is =sp-collec-query-=", explaining it: /collec/ is /collection/ (the set of notes a query runs against), /query/ is the spec, and /tables/ is dropped because every renderer shows a table; the long form reached 45 characters. It deliberately breaks the "prefix = feature name" habit, so =sp-collec-query-menu= is the command and =sp-collection-query-tables-menu= the file that defines it.

*User-facing renames* (no aliases for the old =sp-vulpea-table-= names):

- Settings: =sp-vulpea-table-{renderer, install-exc, refresh-delay, link-titles, views-file, exc-column-widths}= → =sp-collec-query-…=.
- Commands: =…-menu=, =-open=, =-open-view=, =-view-save=, =-view-delete=, =-insert-dblock=, =-inline-toggle=, =-inline-mount=, =-inline-unmount=, =-refresh-all= → =sp-collec-query-…=. Key bindings (=C-c w T/v/V/t=) are unchanged. A =setq= of an old setting name in your config must be renamed.
- Dynamic block: =#+BEGIN: collection-query-table= for new blocks; =vulpea-table= still updates in existing notes.
- Saved views file: =sp-collection-query-tables-views.el= in =user-emacs-directory=; while it does not exist the old =sp-vulpea-table-views.el= is read, so saved views carry over.
- Buffer names (=*query-table: …*=) and the mode lighter changed. The feature =sp-vulpea-table= no longer exists; =require 'sp-collection-query-tables=.

Also corrects a line in the table doc left stale by #72, and updates the one use in =sp-vulpea-grouped-backlinks= (=sp-collec-query-select-note=).

*Checked* (Emacs, container): the doc tangles to the seven files, parens check passes. *Not checked:* loading the modules with vulpea/exc/vui/transient, the menu on screen, a real start with Elpaca. Try the menu, a saved view and an old =vulpea-table= block once.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia*/

*Before:* =sp-dashboard-public-conditions= was empty, the privacy mode only changed on =P=/=g=, and TODO lines were not clickable by default.

*After:*

- =sp-dashboard-condition-focus= is the default condition. True while =sp-dashboard-focus-flag-file= exists (a macOS Shortcuts automation can =touch=/=rm= it when a Focus turns on/off), or while macOS lists a Focus as on in =~/Library/DoNotDisturb/DB/Assertions.json=. =sp-dashboard-focus-modes= limits it to some Focus modes.
- =M-x sp-dashboard-public-facing-mode=: global minor mode, lighter = Public=, forces public mode (private entries hidden) over the other settings.
- The dashboard remembers whether it was drawn as public. A timer (=sp-dashboard-public-check-interval=, 30 s) and file watches on the two Focus files compare that to the current status while the buffer exists, and toggling the mode does so too. A visible Dashboard is redrawn in its window; a hidden one is killed, so it never comes back showing entries it should now hide.
- =sp-dashboard-agenda-todos-clickable= is now =t=: =RET= or a click on a TODO visits the entry (each TODO is a =TAB= stop).
- Doc and CHANGELOG updated; the doc tangles to the =.el=.

*Checked* (Emacs 29.3, headless): flag file on/off redraws and hides/shows the private entry; the minor mode forces and releases public; the Assertions parser and the mode filter work on a made-up file; clicking a TODO opens its Org file at the entry. *Not checked:* macOS itself. The real =Assertions.json= layout and whether Emacs can read it (it may need Full Disk Access) are from memory, so the flag-file route is the reliable one.

- =sp-vulpea-base=: =vulpea-db-sync-scan-on-enable= is nil, so enabling =vulpea-db-autosync-mode= no longer scans the vault at startup (the database, save hook and watchers still work; an empty database is still scanned). =sp-vulpea-scan-once= runs =vulpea-db-sync-full-scan= two idle seconds after the first tracked note is opened, then removes itself. =M-x vulpea-db-sync-full-scan= still works by hand.
- The literate docs (=sp-dashboard.org=, =sp-vulpea.org=) are updated with the code.

*Not tested:* no Emacs in this environment, so none of this was run. =vulpea-db-sync-scan-on-enable= and =vulpea-db-sync-tracked-file-p= come from reading vulpea's source on GitHub; check they exist in the installed version.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2YUwbTNFP92MbconEgCJZPM][project thread]]/

*Before:* in many modules the options of a package sat in top-level =setq= forms just before or after its =use-package=.

*After:* in 14 modules those options are =:custom= entries of the package's =use-package=, in the =.org= docs (canonical) and in the tangled =.el=. Attached comments and trailing comments moved with their setting. The doc text says where each option now lives (bullets, no leftover sections for removed code blocks).

| Module              | Package          | Moved                                     |
|---------------------+------------------+-------------------------------------------|
| sp-denote           | denote           | =denote-directory=, =denote-save-buffers= |
| sp-consult-snapfile | consult-snapfile | 3 options                                 |
| sp-citations        | citar            | =citar-library-file-extensions=           |
| sp-litnotes         | citar-denote     | 4 options                                 |
| sp-bibprocess       | bibtex           | 6 =bibtex-autokey-*=                      |
| sp-org-node-mem     | org-node         | 2 options                                 |
| sp-org-refile       | org-refile       | 3 options                                 |
| sp-vulpea-ext       | vulpea-capf      | 3 options                                 |
| sp-vulpea-ui        | vulpea-ui        | 13 options                                |
| sp-dired            | dirvish          | =dirvish-preview-buffers-max-count=       |
| sp-graphs           | discourse-graphs | 10 =dg-*= options                         |
| sp-org-agenda       | org-agenda       | 14 =org-agenda-*= options                 |
| sp-org-base         | org              | 3 options                                 |
| sp-fonts            | lin              | =lin-face=, =lin-mode-hooks=              |

*Behaviour that changes (check these):*

- =:custom= uses =customize-set-variable=, so a variable with a =:set= function now runs it; =setq= did not. I did not read the installed packages' source to see which have one.
- =:custom= runs before =:init= and =:config=. For =discourse-graphs= the =dg-*= options used to be set after =discourse-graphs-mode= was turned on; =citar-denote= and =org-node= likewise enable their mode after the options now.
- =sp-org-refile=, =sp-consult-snapfile= and =sp-vulpea-ui= have =:after=, so their options now apply once that package has loaded, not at module load.
- =sp-org-agenda= sets =org-agenda-tags-column= twice (0, then =org-tags-column=), as before; the last one wins.
- =sp-citations=: the existing =:custom= already holds a =(when …)= and a =(setq citar-notes-paths …)= form, which =use-package= reads as variables named =when= and =setq= (the doc already says so). The new entry was added after them and is a normal one.

*Not tested:* no Emacs here, so nothing was loaded or byte-compiled. What I did run: a Python check that every changed =.el= has the same bracket balance as before, and a Python tangler that shows each doc tangles to its =.el= (the same 15 pre-existing mismatches, such as =sp-icons= and =sp-themes=, before and after). =python3 tools/set-defcustom-group.py --check= fails on =main= too, for =sp-collection-query-tables{,-org,-views}.el=; I did not touch those.

*Conflicts:* rebased onto =main= with #85 (merged), clean. #79 also adds a line under "Open pull requests" in =CHANGELOG.org=, next to mine; keep both lines. No other open PR touches these files.

*Not moved* (built-in features, settings of a package declared elsewhere, order-sensitive ones, unloaded modules) is listed in the thread.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW23eddj9am1nebvkG14YLgqW][project thread]]/

​#85 started =cursor-intangible-mode= from an idle timer, but the echo-area error still appeared constantly. This removes the mode.

*Why the error cannot be suppressed*

- The mode puts =cursor-sensor--move-to-tangible= on =pre-redisplay-functions=. It calls =cursor-sensor-tangible-pos=, which returns nil when it finds no tangible position, then does arithmetic on nil: =(wrong-type-argument number-or-marker-p nil)= (Sia's backtrace).
- Redisplay runs the hook inside =with-demoted-errors=, so the error is caught and printed in C-level redisplay before any handler of ours runs. =condition-case=, =debug-on-error= and =warning-suppress-types= cannot reach it. Advising the function would mean patching Emacs's own code.
- It repeats because redisplay runs the hook every time, for as long as the condition holds.
- Edge cases where the mode would work: a buffer that is never erased, never redrawn and always has a button. The dashboard redraws on every window-state change (=sp-dashboard-refresh=), and the buttons come and go with the privacy mode and agenda boxes, so it cannot meet that. A guard that makes it safe would have to run before redisplay, which is the same hook.

*Changes* (=sp-dashboard.el=, =sp-dashboard.org=, =CHANGELOG.org=)

- =sp-dashboard--isolate-menu= no longer marks text =cursor-intangible= or starts the mode; =sp-dashboard--enable-intangible= is removed. The keymap overlay stays: =TAB= / =S-TAB= already step through the buttons (wrapping), and the commands that move point are bound to =ignore=, so point only rests on a button.
- =sp-dashboard-focus-face= has =:extend nil=.
- =global-hl-line-mode= is turned off in the dashboard buffer: =(setq-local hl-line-mode -1)= does not disable it, and =prog/sp-prog-misc.el= turns the global mode on. This is the likely cause of the whole-line highlight, since the focus overlay covers only the button text; not verified.

*Not tested:* no Emacs in this environment, so none of it was run.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW22f6Y1Nv4WY5KWBa3A7g69G][project thread]]/

Follows the design note merged in #80.

*Before:* themes came from Elpaca packages (modus, ef, doric, lambda, catppuccin); =sp-load-theme= disabled every theme and reset the mode line /before/ asking, so quitting the prompt left the bright default theme; several modules loaded themes on their own.

*After:*

- =libraries/themes/=: =lib/= (engines on =load-path=), =active/= (the 7 themes in use: =ef-dream=, =ef-day=, =ef-melissa-light=, =lambda-light=, =lambda-light-faded=, =lambda-dark-faded=, =doric-fire=), =library/= (the other 72, one folder per package, for trying out), =sp/= (own themes, empty). README with upstream commits. No Elpaca for themes; =easy-theme-preview= stays. No LICENSE added.
- =sp-themes=: four families in =sp-theme-families= (hard light, faded light, faded dark, hard dark). =sp-load-theme= is the single entry: grouped prompt (families first, then =library=), no confirmation (=custom-safe-themes= set in code plus =load-theme= advice, nothing for =custom.el=), applies optional =sp-theme-palette-overrides= (Ef/Modus only), then disables the previous themes only /after/ the new one loaded (=sp-theme-disable-others=, nil = stack). =T= loads a family. =sp-theme-appearance-themes= / =sp-theme-load-appearance= replace the hard-coded themes in =sp-macos= and the toggle; =sp-theme-dark-p= replaces the =lambda-dark= check in =sp-dashboard=.
- Removed: =lem-dashboard.el= and its doc, =libraries/sp-archived-configs.el= (last commit linked in =sp-helper-funct.org=), =sp-disable-all-themes=, dead Modus options (=-prompts=, =-completions=, =-org-blocks=, =-disable-other-themes=) and duplicates.
- New =docs/architecture/modus-faces-outside-global-system.org=: Modus mechanisms and the 1,237 faces a Doric-style global face system would not cover.

*Checked* (Emacs 29.3 in a 256-colour terminal): all 7 themes and all 72 library themes load, exactly one enabled after each =sp-load-theme=; family lookup and =sp-theme-dark-p= right for all 7; override applied (=ef-day= cursor); toggle switches light/dark. The three edited modules were tangled from their docs. *Not checked:* macOS appearance hook, GUI, a full startup of the whole configuration.

*Decisions for review:* =ef-dream= is the only =hard-dark= theme and =doric-fire= sits in =faded-dark= (near-identical backgrounds, edit =sp-theme-families=). I read "remove the disabling step" as "never disable before loading"; set =sp-theme-disable-others= to nil to stack as literally asked, but faces then mix. The old =ADR 0011= still says =lem-dashboard='s module stays; left as history. =sp-kill-and-archive-region= still writes to its own file in =sp-setup-dir=.
