** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW26wAfLRRbhSQHUmjT3byNkC][project thread]]/

Cleans up plain-BibTeX handling in the academic modules (=sp-academic.org= is canonical; the =.el= files were tangled from it).

*Citation keys: =smithjones-2017-atten-all=.* Your settings: year length 4, =-= between name, year and title words, 2 title words (stretch 1) of at most 5 letters. Your later edit in the =.el= (first two authors, ignore list gains "Is", "the", "a") is kept and the doc now matches it; "On" and "on" are also ignored; keys are lower case and ASCII (=Müller= → =muller=). Before, the options were set twice with different values and =biblio= entries kept whatever the service returned. Now:

- all =bibtex-autokey-*= options live in one =use-package bibtex= block in =sp-bibprocess=;
- =biblio-bibtex-use-autokey= gives inserted entries the same key;
- =bibtex-search-entry-globally= + =bibtex-files= check keys across all registered files.

*One folder option.* =sp-bibliography-dir= (in =sp-paths=) is the only one and now defaults to =~/Documents/bibliography=. =sp-bibtex-dir= (a copy of it) and the unused =sp-bibliography= are removed, no aliases. =sp-org-export= read =sp-bibliography= for pandoc; =sp-cite-to-org= / =sp-cite-to-markdown= now pass one =--bibliography= flag per registered =.bib= file. Existing =.bib= files must move to the new folder (or set =SP_BIBLIOGRAPHY_DIR=).

*One bibliography list.* =sp-bibtex-register= also sets =org-ref-default-bibliography=, =bibtex-completion-bibliography= and =bibtex-files= (previously a hard-coded list of seven files in =sp-academic=, =master.bib= only for org-ref). The file regexp is fixed.

*Citar fixes* (both were bugs):

- =citar-bibliography= / =org-cite-global-bibliography= were set from =sp-bibliography= (nil), so Citar loaded with an empty bibliography. They now use =sp-bibtex-files=.
- =citar-library-paths= was commented out; it is now =sp-literature-dir=. The extensions and separator moved to =sp-citations=; the =(setq citar-library-file-extensions nil)= it overrode is gone.
- The =citar-symbols= =when= form and the =citar-notes-paths= =setq= sat inside =:custom= and never applied; they moved to =:config= / a proper entry (notes path falls back to =sp-notes-dir=).

*Also:* removed the verbatim repeated block in =sp-bibprocess=; the =defcustom=s in =sp-academic= come before the =require=s; =citar-org-node= uses an Elpaca recipe instead of =:vc=; =H-b= moved into the =bibtex= block. The doc has "Citation keys" and "Settings worth knowing" sections.

*Checked* (Emacs 29.3, batch): the key function (=smithjones-2017-atten-all=, =hegel-1807-phanom-geist=, =mullerjones-2020-origin-species=); =sp-bibtex-register= and =sp--pandoc-bibliography-args= on a temp directory; the edited files read without errors; docs tangle to the =.el= byte for byte (own tangler). =tools/set-defcustom-group.py --check= only reports =sp-collection-query-tables*.el=, which this PR does not touch. *Not run:* the whole configuration, Citar/org-cite with real =.bib= files, =biblio= insertion, pandoc, the Elpaca recipe for =citar-org-node=.

*Overlap:* #87 also moves the three =defcustom=s to the top of =sp-academic= and will conflict in that hunk.

That run caught that =bibtex-set-field= does not exist, so the field is edited with =bibtex-search-forward-field=. *Not run:* anything over the network (CrossRef, Google Scholar, =org-ref= DOI and PDF fetch), Elpaca installing =biblio-gscholar=, loading the whole configuration. I also expect =org-ref= to clean the new DOI entry with =bibtex-clean-entry= (so it gets the #90 key) but did not confirm it; check the first key you get.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia*/

*Before:* the lambda sat behind the left of the same area as the banner and boxes, the footer was centred under the lambda 15 lines above the bottom, and the lambda never changed size with the display.

*After:*

- *Two columns:* the lambda (=sp-dashboard-side-layer=) is the left column, centred in the window's height; the banner, title and boxes share the right column. The two are centred in the window together, =sp-dashboard-column-gap= apart. Offsets in =sp-dashboard-art-layers= now default to 0 and are relative to these places (offsets set in your config keep their number but not their old meaning).
- *Footer* centred in the window, two lines from the bottom (=sp-dashboard-footer-layer= is nil by default).
- *Lambda as SVG* (=sp-dashboard-side-as-svg=): each art line becomes =<text>= runs stretched to the character grid, and the image is cut into one slice per buffer line, so line heights are untouched. =sp-dashboard-side-scale= (=auto=, a number, or nil) sets the size; =auto= picks the largest factor within =sp-dashboard-side-scale-limits= at which the lambda fills =sp-dashboard-side-fill= of the window height and of the room left of the other column. A bigger window or display therefore gives a bigger lambda, while *all text stays at its normal size* (no font scaling any more).
- Without a graphical frame or SVG support, the plain text lambda is used. In a window too narrow for both columns the lambda is left out.
- Doc and CHANGELOG updated; the doc tangles to the =.el=.

*Checked:* Emacs 29.3 headless: banner ink, box corners and title share edges and centre at 200, 160 and 120 columns; footer centred on the last lines; =TAB=, privacy, Focus and clicking a TODO still work. In a real GUI Emacs under a virtual X display (DejaVu Sans Mono): the lambda renders complete, aligned to the grid, with no line gaps, at 190x58 and 240x70 frames (scale 1.15 and 1.38). *Not checked:* a Mac or 4K display, or other fonts.

- Merge commit :: [[https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/commit/7f05a4a617745aa13d42624eba1cbd2c48a295a1][7f05a4a617]]

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW22f6Y1Nv4WY5KWBa3A7g69G][project thread]]/

Follows #89 (vendored themes).

*Before:* only third-party themes; the Modus mechanisms a palette cannot hold (headings, mixed fonts, variable-pitch UI) existed only for Ef/Modus; theme names and light/dark were known from a hand-kept list; the macOS appearance code lived in =sp-macos=.

*After:*

- New module =sp-theme-engine= (+ doc) and two themes in =libraries/themes/sp/=, =sp-dark= and =sp-light=, three lines each.
  - *Flavors* (=sp-theme-flavors=): 12 base colours per flavor, =catppuccin-set-color=-style (=sp-theme-set-color=, reloads). Dark is a simplified =ef-dream=; light uses the matching =ef-day= colours (my choice, with a teal cyan). These are the only hex codes.
  - The 26 Doric palette keys are *derived by blending*, and the faces come from =doric-themes-define-theme=, so Doric's bundles define about 1,300 faces.
  - *Semantic mappings* (=sp-theme-mappings=): Modus-style roles (=bg-region=, =fg-heading-1=, =err=, ...) -> palette keys, overridable per flavor (=sp-theme-set-mapping=); =sp-theme-mapped-faces= are written against roles.
  - *Semantic face names* (=sp-urgent=, =sp-crucial=, =sp-focus=, =sp-strong=, =sp-meek=, ...), per-flavor overridable.
  - *Ported Modus mechanisms:* =sp-theme-headings=, =sp-theme-mixed-fonts=, =sp-theme-variable-pitch-ui=. Bold and italic are Doric's bundles, so they have no option.
- =sp-themes=: *registry* reading every theme file the same way (name, background, description, package, family); the prompt is grouped by family and annotated from it. *=sp-theme-auto-mode=* is the one switch for light/dark (macOS setting, falling back to time of day via =sp-theme-day-hours=; also syncs new frames for daemons). =sp-macos= now only turns it on (its own detection and daemon hook are removed).
- Removed the colour-blind themes (4 Modus, 2 Ef) from the library.
- 19 ERT tests (=tests/sp-theme-engine-test.el=, =tests/sp-themes-test.el=).

*Checked* (Emacs 29.3; GUI-like checks in a 256-colour terminal): all 19 tests pass; all 75 themes load and the registry background matches the real background of every one; =sp-dark= and =sp-light= give the mapped colours, heading heights and merged attributes (e.g. =org-code= keeps its Doric colour and gains =fixed-pitch=); =set-color= and =set-mapping= reload; auto-mode with the time source switches and cleans up. *Not checked:* macOS (appearance hook, =defaults read=), a GUI, a full startup of the configuration.

*Notes for review:* the defaults still load =ef-dream= / =lambda-light-faded= for dark/light; set =sp-theme-appearance-themes= to =sp-dark= / =sp-light= to switch. =sp-dark= and =sp-light= are last in their families. Emacs keeps every =custom-theme-set-faces= call of a theme as its own record and enables the oldest, so the engine merges into and drops the older record (explained in the doc). The Modus engine file still contains the colour-blind palettes (vendored unchanged).

** Description
Follows #97 (merged).

*Before:* =sp-theme-auto-mode= could only read the macOS appearance (or the time of day); =sp-syswin= and =sp-syslinux= were not loaded, and =sp-syslinux= was empty.

*After:*

- =sp-themes=: =sp-theme-platform= (macos / windows / linux) and three alists naming the function per platform: =sp-theme-system-providers= (reads light/dark), =sp-theme-system-watchers= (calls back on change, returns an unwatch function) and =sp-theme-ambient-providers=. A source with no answer, an error or nonsense falls back to the time of day. Where there is no watcher, the timer polls.
- =sp-macos=: =sp-macos-appearance= (moved from =sp-themes=) and =sp-macos-watch-appearance=.
- =sp-syswin=: =sp-syswin-appearance= reads the registry value =AppsUseLightTheme= with =reg query=; no watcher, so it is polled.
- =sp-syslinux=: =sp-syslinux-appearance= tries the freedesktop portal (=gdbus=), then =gsettings=, then the KDE colour scheme; =sp-syslinux-watch-appearance= listens to the portal's =SettingChanged= signal with Emacs' =dbus=.
- Each of the three modules turns =sp-theme-auto-mode= on for its own platform, and =init.el= now loads =sp-syswin= and =sp-syslinux=.
- *macOS room light:* with =sp-theme-auto-source= set to =ambient=, the lux from =sp-macos-light-sensor-command= picks a family, in this order from the brightest room: =faded-light=, =hard-light=, =faded-dark=, =hard-dark= (=sp-macos-ambient-levels=, default 150 / 60 / 15 / 0 lux), and loads the first theme of that family. =sp-macos-ambient-margin= (25%) keeps it from flickering at a boundary. Checked every 60 s (=sp-theme-ambient-interval=).
- 13 new ERT tests (providers, ambient, watcher, parsers, levels with hysteresis); all 40 tests pass on Emacs 29.3.

*Not checked:* anything on macOS, Windows or a Linux desktop (only the parsing of what they print, and the dispatch, are tested). macOS has no command line tool for the ambient light sensor, so there is no default =sp-macos-light-sensor-command=: it needs a command of your own that prints lux; without one, =ambient= follows the time of day. The default source is still =system=.

*Judgement call:* I read "faded light, hard light, faded dark, hard dark, in this order" as brightest room first. If you meant another order, reorder =sp-macos-ambient-levels=.

*Before:* startup reports =[FAILED] sp-env (void-function exec-path-from-shell-copy-env)=. =sp-env.el= had a second, top-level =dolist= (added in ee21b24 for =GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=) calling =exec-path-from-shell-copy-env= outside the =use-package= form. *Not tested:* nothing was run (no Emacs in the container). On fish, =exec-path-from-shell= is unchanged; if a startup warning about the shell appears, it is separate from this error.

** Description
*Before:* after =sp-load-theme= to a theme with another background, white borders stayed around the buffers. =sp-windows= painted the window dividers, the fringe and (indirectly) the frame border with the default background *once, when the module loaded*, so they kept the colour of the theme loaded at startup. Most themes (Doric included) also give =internal-border= no background, and Emacs does not repaint a frame's border when a face changes.

*After:* =sp-windows-blend-borders= paints the three divider faces, =fringe=, =internal-border= and =child-frame-border= with the current default background and redraws the graphic frames. It runs at load, from =sp-after-load-theme-hook=, and for each new graphic frame (a daemon that started without a frame has no background to read yet). Values like =unspecified-bg= (terminal frames) are skipped.

*Checked* (Emacs 29.3, no GUI available): with the default background stubbed to two colours in turn, all five faces follow it. *Not checked:* a real graphic frame, so please confirm on your Mac that the borders now follow =sp-load-theme=. If a border is still white, it is probably the =spacious-padding= faces, and I would look there next.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW25gNRrBAMuP7KHa4qEqWBeG][project thread]]/

*Before:* =sp-clean-whitespace= (the command asked about as =sp-remove-whitespace=) ran from the global =before-save-hook=. =sp-backups= saves modified buffers after 5 s idle (=lem-full-auto-save=, plus =auto-save-visited-mode=), and those saves run the same hook. In the middle of writing, the cleanup stripped the space just typed at the end of a line and collapsed blank lines around point, which in Org moved text and broke words.

*After:* the hook calls =sp-clean-whitespace-before-save=, which skips the cleanup in the modes of the new option =sp-clean-whitespace-autosave-skip-modes= (default =(org-mode)=, derived modes included) unless the save was explicit (=this-command= is =save-buffer=, =save-some-buffers= or =write-file=). Set it to =nil= to restore the old behaviour. =M-x sp-clean-whitespace= is unchanged. Module doc and CHANGELOG updated.

*Not tested:* nothing was run (no Emacs in the container). Saves from other commands (e.g. Magit's save prompt) count as non-explicit in Org buffers.

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
- *Registry:* =sp-org-tag-registry.el= holds the note tags in =org-tag-persistent-alist=. The task tags stay in =org-tag-alist= (=sp-org-taskman-extra=).
- *=M-x sp-org-tag-add=:* inserts a tag above a marker line in the registry file, saves it and runs =load-file=, so it works without restarting. It asks first if the tag is close to a registered one (typo guard).
- *=M-x sp-org-tag-lint=:* scans the vault (vulpea db, else =~/notes=) and reports unregistered tags in =#+filetags:= and on headings, with the likely typo, plus notes with no =#+filetags:= (for =sp-tag-emoji=). =RET= visits, =a= registers, =g= reruns. =sp-org-tag-lint-buffer= does one file.
- *=sp-org-create-note-and-link=* and *wikilink conversion:* both ask for at least one note tag (unknown ones can be registered on the spot) and write =#+filetags:=.
- *=sp-split-leave-parents=:* binds =org-use-tag-inheritance= to the new =sp-split-inherit-tags= (nil), only while it runs.

**** Notes
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: notes
:END:
- The registry file is data, not tangled from a doc, because the command edits it. It is documented in =docs/tangles/funct/sp-org-tag-lint.org=.

Follow-up to #60 (merged).

**** What changes
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what-changes
:END:
- With =sp-tag-emoji-mode= on, =vulpea-select-describe-fn= is =sp-tag-emoji-describe-note=: the emoji of the note's tags, then the title (=vulpea-select=, =vulpea-find=, =vulpea-insert=). It depends on the note alone, so vulpea's candidate cache stays valid; the previous value (now =vulpea-select-describe-outline-full= from =sp-vulpea-base=) is restored when the mode is turned off.
- =sp-select-note= is my own selector (same keywords as =vulpea-select=) built on =vulpea-select-from=: the tags in a column at the right edge (=(space :align-to (- right N))=, =N= a fraction of the frame width), small and dimmed, still matchable.
- =sp-insert-note= is =vulpea-insert= with the same emoji and tag column; the link text stays the plain title.
- Both bypass vulpea's candidate cache while they run (the column width is not a property of the note).
- *Callers now use them*, for one look everywhere: =sp-org-create-note-and-link= (its "insert existing" branch) and the wikilink conversion, =sp-tab-inbox=, =sp-move-region-to-heading=, the graph start note in =sp-graphs=, and =sp-collec-query-select-note= (which also no longer confuses same-titled notes). Each of those modules now requires =sp-tag-emoji=.
- Rules can opt out of the selector with =:select nil=. =sp-tag-emoji-select-visit= is not part of this PR.
- Docs and CHANGELOG follow.

**** Worth checking
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: worth-checking
:END:
=sp-org-create-note-and-link= used to call =vulpea-insert= with two positional functions. Upstream =vulpea-insert= takes keywords (=:filter-fn=, =:create-fn=), so the call now uses keywords; if your installed vulpea still has the positional signature, that call needs to go back.

:END:
Candidate strings with a stubbed =vulpea-select-from= and fake notes, =sp-insert-note= calling a stubbed =vulpea-insert= with the emoji describe function and the cache off, mode on/off restoring the describe function; every changed =.el= reads and balances, and each tangles from its doc.

The look in a real minibuffer (Vertico / mini-frame), the callers with a real vulpea database, and the real =vulpea-insert= signature (read from upstream source, not your installed copy).

A design record only (=adr/0020-tag-families.org=, status /proposed/, plus its row in =adr/README.org= and a CHANGELOG line). No code changes.

*Decision proposed:* families of note tags are one alist, =sp-org-tag-families=, of =(FAMILY TAG…)= lists, which is the shape of Org's own =org-tag-groups-alist=. =org-tag-persistent-alist= (#105) is derived from it as Org group tags (=:startgrouptag= ... =:endgrouptag=), so a tag search on a family finds its members. The record also lists the alternatives (raw group-tag syntax, plists, structs, nested names, vulpea properties, symbol plists), the consequences for =sp-org-tag-lint=, =sp-tag-emoji= and the prompts, and two open questions (family names, whether a tag in no family is refused).

*Checked* (Emacs 29.3, headless): the family list converted to the group-tag form and =org-tag-alist-to-groups= returned the same families (a =("group" . ?g)= member kept its key); in an Org buffer a =+music= match found a heading tagged =album=. *Not checked:* the converter and lookup functions (sketched in the record only), nested families, org-ql / vulpea behaviour with group tags, the completion grouping.

**** What changes
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what-changes
:END:
- =sp-org-tag-families=: the families of note tags as a list of =(FAMILY TAG…)=, in the shape ADR 0020 proposes, with the six families from the ADR (structure, who, music, software, literature, inquiry). =sp-org-tag-family-of= returns a tag's families.
- =sp-tag-emoji-family-colors= gives each family one of Notion's ten tag colours; =sp-tag-emoji-palette= holds the pairs, a tinted background with dark text on a light theme, a muted background with light text on a dark theme (read from the frame's =background-mode= every time the selector draws).
- In =sp-select-note= and =sp-insert-note= the tags in the right-hand column are now chips: the name with a space on each side on the family's background. A tag in no family, or a family with no colour, gets Notion's default grey. Chips that do not fit the column become an ellipsis. Tags are still matchable (=deep=, no =#= now).

**** Not done
:PROPERTIES:

:END:
=sp-org-tag-registry.el= does not use =sp-org-tag-families= yet: =org-tag-persistent-alist= is still the flat list, so the two are kept in step by hand until ADR 0020 is decided. Nested families are not followed. This PR is not blocked on the ADR, but it takes its shape for granted.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia*/

*Problem:* in Sia's Emacs the box titles and entries could not be walked: =keycast-log-mode= showed =TAB= and =<right>= running =sp-dashboard-next-button= and =sp-dashboard-enter-box=, but nothing moved.

*Likely cause (not reproduced):* =sp-dashboard-refresh= was on =window-state-change-hook= and =window-configuration-change-hook=, and it kills and redraws the Dashboard every time they run. Those hooks also run for reasons other than a resize (a key logger, the mode line, a message). A redraw puts point back on the first title and out of any box, so each key press is undone at once.

*Change:*

- The hooks now call =sp-dashboard--refresh-on-resize=, which redraws only when the pixel size of the window or the font differs from the last draw (=sp-dashboard--drawn-geometry=, set when the mode starts). =sp-dashboard-refresh= itself is unchanged for the other callers (=g=, art moves, privacy changes).
- The width of the larger box titles is read with =window-font-width= instead of =string-pixel-width=, so nothing is measured in a temporary buffer on each draw.
- Doc and CHANGELOG updated.

*Checked:* Emacs 29.3 headless: running both window hooks after TAB and =<right>= keeps point and the box; a real resize still redraws. Graphical Emacs 29.3 on a virtual display with a window manager and real Tab, S-Tab, Right and Left key presses (xdotool), through the real startup hooks and =sp-set-window-margins=: everything works, titles stay aligned. *Not checked:* Sia's Emacs (31, Mac), real nerd-icons, keycast. I could not reproduce the failure here, so this may not be the whole cause.

*What changes*

  - *Header line* in nano's blocky style: a block with =RW= (writable, muted), =RO= (read-only, warning colour) or =**= (modified, error colour; =--= for a dedicated window), then the path of the file in bold and the project name at the right edge. Other windows get a muted block and path. Colours come from the theme (=warning=, =error=, =shadow=, inverted). The project name is cached per buffer.
  - *Divider* between the text of the buffer and the mode line: a thin overline in the =shadow= colour on =mode-line=, =mode-line-inactive= and the lambda-line faces, set again after each theme load (=sp-nano-style-divider= turns it off). The mode line itself stays whole (nano shrinks its own to the divider; not done here, as you asked for a real mode line).
- The header code that was in =sp-lambda-modeline= (and Prot's path construct) is replaced by this module.
- =sp-mini-frame=: =M-x= (=sp-mini-frame-nano-commands=) opens at the bottom as in =nano-minibuffer= (full width, 5 lines, 12 px fringes, no border, background moved 8% from the theme's, a half-height blank line above the prompt). Other prompts keep the centred frame and dimming.
- Docs, docs index and CHANGELOG updated; the docs tangle to the =.el= files.

*Interpretation to confirm:* I read "the =M-x= menu beautification" as nano's =mini-frame= styling in =nano-minibuffer.el=. If you meant =nano-command-x= (a prompt drawn in the header line, in =nano-command.el=), say so and I will add that instead.

- Order: window number, major mode (nerd-icons, boxed), word count (text buffers) or line:column (code), keycast (key boxed, command next to it, last command kept, fixed width), minor-mode count (button: click for menu, right-click for =describe-mode=). Tags and branch stay at the right.

- Lambda uses the layout only in text and prog buffers (via advice on =lambda-line-compose=); Prot loses its own buffer-name, major-mode, minor-modes and keycast segments in favour of the shared ones.

From nano only the text styling and boxes: inverted bold prompt with a box, one-pixel border, and a dotted line (=sp-mini-frame-divider-char=) under the input in the divider colour. /Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2GZfKdKaJ3ZDytUsAiWfF6L][project thread]]/

*Cause:* =olivetti-mode= centres and narrows text by setting window margins. =sp-set-window-margins= in =sp-frame= runs on the global =window-configuration-change-hook= (and at startup and for new frames) and sets a 2/2 margin on every window. The global hook runs after Olivetti's buffer-local one, so it overwrote Olivetti's margins and the text ran to the window edge instead of the 80-column body.

*Fix:* =sp-set-window-margins= now skips windows whose buffer has =olivetti-mode= on (checked with =bound-and-true-p=, so it is safe before Olivetti loads). Doc (=docs/tangles/ui/sp-frame.org=) and CHANGELOG updated.

*Not changed, worth knowing:* =sp-writedesk= sets =olivetti-minimum-body=, which is not an Olivetti variable (it is =olivetti-minimum-body-width=), so that line does nothing. If you fix its name, 100 > 80 would widen the body to 100 columns, so I left it for you to decide.

*Not tested:* no Emacs in the container; please check an Org buffer after =M-x eval-buffer= of =sp-frame.el= or a restart.

- *Centred* horizontally (as before) and vertically for its largest size: =top= is computed in pixels as (parent height - largest frame height) / 2; the frame grows downward from there.
- *Padding of 4 pixels* (=sp-mini-frame-padding=) in the frame's own background colour; =sp-mini-frame-border-color= gives it a colour for an outline. The border faces are now set on every showing (mini-frame sets them only when it makes the frame). =M-x= loses its one-pixel foreground border because the border is now the padding.

*Not tested* (no Emacs in the container; =.el= paren-checked only): the height fitting with Vertico's candidate overlay (=vertico-resize=), the vertical centring on a real display, and the padding colour after a theme change. ** Description
/Requested by *Sia*/

*Reported:* the text in the =M-x= mini-frame blends into the background and shows only where highlighted; and =ESC= / =C-g= in it blocks everything.

*Likely cause of the invisible text (not confirmed):* since #115 =M-x= takes the colours =mini-frame= computes from the /frame parameters/ of the parent frame. After a theme is loaded later (=sp-load-theme=) those parameters still hold the first frame's colours, while the text is drawn with the theme's =default= face. Result: a background computed from the old colours with the new text colour on it.

*Change:* =sp-mini-frame--colors= reads the text colour and the background from the =default= face of the selected frame; the background is the text colour mixed in by =sp-mini-frame-contrast= (0.08, as before #115). Both are passed as frame parameters. The =M-x= prompt block uses =:inverse-video= and no colour lookup. The prompt styling hook now reports an error in the echo area instead of aborting the prompt.

*Not fixed, not understood yet:* =ESC= / =C-g= blocking everything. I could not find a cause in the code; it might be input focus not returning to the main frame after the child frame is hidden, or =mini-frame-resize t= (from #119) during the exit. I have asked for details in the thread.

*Not tested:* nothing was run in Emacs.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW28jYkTEHaVRbSbZqCYEwELz][project thread]]/

*Reported:* since the vulpea scan was deferred, Emacs hangs for 10+ seconds after init while vulpea reindexes and the dashboard agenda entries fill in, with silent gaps in the echo area.

*Likely cause (read from the code, not measured):* =sp-vulpea-scan-once= ran =vulpea-db-sync-full-scan=, which lists, cleans up and checks dir-locals in the foreground of Emacs; the dashboard's reading of the agenda files visited a vault file and so started that scan; and each of the four dashboard boxes re-read every agenda file.

*Changes*

- =sp-vulpea-base=: removed =sp-vulpea-scan-once= and its =find-file-hook=. =vulpea-db-autosync-mode= starts from a 5s idle timer after start-up (=sp-vulpea-start-autosync=) with =vulpea-db-sync-scan-on-enable= set to ='background=: files are listed in a subprocess and the queue parses only changed files. Opening a note no longer starts a scan.
- =sp-dashboard=: the entries of a list of agenda files are read once per draw (=sp-dashboard--read-entries=, cached only during =sp-dashboard--insert-boxes=), and the boxes filter/sort a copy. Until =org-agenda-files= is set (=sp-dashboard-agenda-ready=) the boxes show "loading agenda files..."; =sp-dashboard-refresh-agendas= redraws the Dashboard when the files are set, if it is the selected buffer.
- =sp-vulpea-para=: the agenda-files refresh sets the ready flag and prints messages with the count and time. Autosync start and dashboard reads print their time too.
- Docs (=sp-vulpea.org=, =sp-dashboard.org=) and CHANGELOG updated; =.el= files edited in step with the docs.

*Not tested:* nothing was run; there is no Emacs in the container and vulpea is not installed. Parens checked only. Profiling steps are in =profiling/vulpea-startup-profiling.md= in the project files. If it still hangs, the profiler will show where.

* PR #125: ✨ Import a short colour palette as an sp theme
:PROPERTIES:
:PR_NUMBER: 125
:URL: https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/pull/125
:STATE: open
:AUTHOR: siainbuletin
:END:
- Link :: [[https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/pull/125][https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/pull/125]]
- State :: open
- Author :: @siainbuletin
- Opened :: 2026-10-26 13:12
- Branch :: =125-palette-import= → =main=
- Labels :: needs-further-testing

** Description
*Before:* a flavor needed twelve hand-picked colours, and the engine only knew =dark= and =light= as flavor names.

*After:*

- =sp-theme-flavor-from-palette COLORS &key variant roles= turns a handful of =#rrggbb= colours into a flavor:
  - the darkest colour (pushed darker) is the background of a dark theme and the lightest (pushed lighter, contrast >= 10) the foreground; the other way round for a light theme;
  - the two most saturated remaining colours are =accent-1= (also the cursor) and =accent-2=, lifted to contrast >= 4.5;
  - the six status hues (red ... cyan) stay recognisable but are not new colours: the usual hue blended 30% towards =accent-1=;
  - =:roles= gives a colour to a job, e.g. =((red . 4) (blue . "#6fa8ff"))= (an index into the palette or a hex).
- =sp-theme-import-palette NAME COLORS= (interactive; accepts a pasted string of colours) registers the flavor, writes =libraries/themes/sp/sp-NAME-theme.el= (three forms, the palette stays in the file) and loads it. Flavors can now carry a =:mode= (=dark=/=light=), so their names are free.
- Example: =sp-wandavision=, from the five colours of [[https://www.color-hex.com/color-palette/111848]] (=#2a3156 #8f8280 #4e5044 #8a4160 #8d2025=), dark: background =#171b2f=, foreground =#cdc7c6=, accents =#b77375= and =#ae7a90=.
- The registry reads the background of such theme files.
- Also: the registry tests expected the Modus themes and a count of 70+, which no longer matches =main= (they failed on =main=); they now match the remaining themes.
- 4 new ERT tests; engine 13 and themes 13 pass on Emacs 29.3.

*Not checked:* how =sp-wandavision= looks in a graphic frame (only that it loads, its colours, and the contrast ratios). The palette is dark and muted, so the accents are lifted a lot to stay readable; try =M-x sp-load-theme= and =sp-theme-set-color= / =:roles= to adjust. It is not in any family yet.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2XYC9n7jY4gV3tnop2oYDSv][project thread]]/

**** Problem
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: problem
:END:
=M-x sp-split-leave-parents= failed with "Autoloading file .../org/org.elc failed to define function sp-split-leave-parents".

**** Cause
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: cause
:END:
In =sp-org-base.el=, =(use-package org :bind (:map org-mode-map ("C-x s t" . sp-split-leave-parents)))= makes use-package autoload the command from =org=, which does not define it. Until =sp-split-leave-parents.el= is loaded (it is only required by =sp-vulpea-ext=), the stub points at the wrong file.

**** Fix
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: fix
:END:
Declare =(autoload 'sp-split-leave-parents "sp-split-leave-parents" nil t)= before the =use-package org= block. use-package only adds its own autoload when the function is not already bound, so the correct one wins and the key binding is unchanged. Doc and CHANGELOG updated.

**** Verification
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: verification
:END:
Not run in Emacs (none in the sandbox). I read the code only; please check =C-x s t= and =M-x sp-split-leave-parents= in a fresh Emacs. If the error persists, =M-x describe-function sp-split-leave-parents= will show which file the stub names.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2XYC9n7jY4gV3tnop2oYDSv][project thread]]/

**** Problem
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: problem
:END:
=C-x t s= reports =vulpea-ui-sidebar-toggle= as undefined. (Separate from #130, which fixed =C-x s t=.)

**** Cause
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: cause
:END:
=sp-vulpea-ui.el= declared =(use-package vulpea-ui ... :after vulpea)= and bound the key with a plain =global-set-key=. =vulpea= is loaded lazily (its own =:bind=), so the =:after= form never ran and =vulpea-ui= was never loaded; a plain =global-set-key= creates no autoload.

**** Fix
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: fix
:END:
Drop =:after vulpea= and bind =C-x t s= with =:bind= in the same =use-package=, which autoloads =vulpea-ui-sidebar-toggle= from =vulpea-ui=. =vulpea-ui= requires =vulpea= itself. Doc and CHANGELOG updated.

**** Verification
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: verification
:END:
Not run in Emacs (none in the sandbox); this is from reading the code. Please check =C-x t s= in a fresh Emacs. If it still says undefined, =M-: (locate-library "vulpea-ui")= shows whether Elpaca installed it.

- Merge commit :: [[https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/commit/0e96addda1710f2e355095ba4adc28b11a673c07][0e96addda1]]

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW257Mdet5dXQHZmdGYA1j39j][project thread]]/

**** Problem
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: problem
:END:
At launch a =*scratch*= window opens beside the Dashboard instead of the Dashboard alone.

**** Likely cause
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: likely-cause
:END:
Since 8e1917b (Oct 23) =tabspaces-mode= starts after init with =tabspaces-session-auto-restore=. On startup it restores the window layout saved at the last exit (=window-state-put=). =sp-dashboard--setup-splash-hooks= runs later, on =window-setup-hook=, and only replaces the buffer of the selected window, so any restored second window (here =*scratch*=) stays. The layout is saved again at every exit, so it keeps coming back. Nothing in the PRs #114-#131 touches this (quick-capture #131 is not merged).

**** Fix
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: fix
:END:
=sp-dashboard--setup-splash-hooks= calls =delete-other-windows= before drawing the Dashboard. It runs once at start-up only, not on refresh. Doc and CHANGELOG updated.

**** Not verified
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-verified
:END:
Not run in Emacs (none in the sandbox); the cause is from reading the config and the upstream =tabspaces= source. Please check in a fresh Emacs. If =*scratch*= still appears, =M-: (window-list)= right after launch and the contents of =var/tabspaces-session.eld= would show who creates it. Under =emacs --daemon= tabspaces defers the restore to the first client frame, which runs after this hook, so a daemon setup could still show the split.

* PR #139: 🐛 Keep the current buffer when a theme is loaded
:PROPERTIES:
:PR_NUMBER: 139
:URL: https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/pull/139
:STATE: merged
:AUTHOR: siainbuletin
:END:
- Link :: [[https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/pull/139][https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/pull/139]]
- State :: merged
- Author :: @siainbuletin
- Opened :: 2026-10-27 10:11
- Merged :: 2026-10-27 10:24
- Branch :: =139-theme-stay-in-buffer= → =main=
- Merge commit :: [[https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/commit/8f5f8fc954c24f9aaca4860a497a78bdd16ea3eb][8f5f8fc954]]
- Labels :: bugfix

** Description
*Before:* =sp-load-theme= from any buffer ended in the Dashboard.

*Cause:* =sp-dashboard= hangs =sp-dashboard--theme-changed= on =enable-theme-functions= and =disable-theme-functions=. It ran =sp-dashboard-refresh= inside the Dashboard buffer, which kills and redraws it with =sp-dashboard-screen=, and that ends in =switch-to-buffer "Dashboard"=. =with-current-buffer= does not change the selected window, so the redraw put the Dashboard in whichever window you were using.

*After:* the splash is redrawn inside =with-selected-window= of the window that already shows it, and not at all when no window does (the palette is still applied; =g= redraws a hidden Dashboard). The selection is restored by =with-selected-window=.

*Checked* (Emacs 29.3, windows only): with the Dashboard in a second window the refresh runs there and the selected window stays; with no window showing it, no refresh runs. *Not checked:* the real Dashboard on macOS.

:PROPERTIES:

- *Dashboard box text.* =sp-fonts-dashboard-menu-height= (0.85) sets the height of =sp-dashboard-menu-face= relative to =default=. =sp-fonts-ui-faces= applies it when the dashboard loads, after a theme loads and on =fontaine-set-preset-hook=, so it follows the fontaine preset.
- Docs and CHANGELOG updated.

**** Not tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-tested
:END:
Nothing was run in Emacs (none in the container). The root cause of the buffer-dependent size is not confirmed; the remapping reset is a defensive fix. Smaller menu text may shift box alignment (the box lines and art are laid out in columns of the base font); set =sp-fonts-dashboard-menu-height= to 1.0 to compare.

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
The 0.85 relative height of #146 made the dashboard boxes misalign. Removed =sp-fonts-dashboard-menu-height= and =sp-fonts-ui-faces=. Instead =sp-dashboard-menu-face= is added to =fontaine-faces= (in the =:config= of the fontaine block, before the first preset is set) and the =t= preset sets =:sp-dashboard-menu-face-height= to 1.0, so the dashboard is back on the grid of the =default= font and a preset can change the height. I read fontaine's source (3.1.0): =fontaine-faces= is a plain list of faces, and a preset reads =:FACE-height= as a multiple of the =default= height. Docs and CHANGELOG updated.

Any other height makes box text and box lines differ in width, so boxes only align at 1.0 unless the layout is moved to pixel widths.

- Picks the file with the same fuzzy search as =sp-find-file=, restricted to =.org= files under =sp-config-docs-directory= (=docs/= next to =init.el=).
- =file:= link with the path abbreviated to =~/=; the docs have no =:ID:=, and an =id:= link would need them in the database. Description defaults to the file's =#+title= (prefix argument asks for it).
- =sp-navi=: =sp-find-file= is split into =sp-find-file-options=, =sp-find-file--read= and the new =sp-find-file-pick=; =C-x C-f= behaves as before.
- Literate docs of =sp-navi=, =sp-org-id-link= and =sp-org-base= updated and checked to match the code.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2VvsAv9bMnVw5hmscGggixs][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
After #152, =M-x= was fine at init but glitched again once Org was in use. The dimming remapped every face with a foreground (over a thousand, from =face-list=) in each buffer behind the posframe. Every redisplay of that buffer looks faces up in that remap list, so a busy Org buffer (indent, numbering, tables, tag groups) redraws slowly on each keystroke in the posframe.

=sp-posframe-dim= now remaps =default= and the faces found on the visible text only (=sp-posframe--visible-faces=, a walk of the =face= property from =window-start= to =window-end=). The look is the same; text scrolled into view while the minibuffer is open is not dimmed.

The doc has two extra checks for the mirrored-buffer symptom: whether =vertico-buffer-mode= is on at the same time as the posframe, and =(setq sp-posframe-dim-always nil)= to rule the dimming out.

**** Not tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-tested
:END:
Nothing was run in Emacs (none in the container). This is a suspected cause, not a confirmed one. I found nothing in the config that turns on =vertico-buffer-mode=, so I could not explain the mirrored buffer from the code.

:PROPERTIES:

=org-insert-link= completes the path of a link type that has a =:complete= parameter. =sp-org-id-link= now sets one for three types, once Org is loaded:

- =help:= reads a function, variable or face (=completing-read= over =obarray=).
- =info:= reads a manual and node with =Info-read-node-name= and inserts Org's =MANUAL#NODE= form (=Top= when only a manual is given).
- =man:= reads a page with =Man-completion-table=. It also gets a follow function (=man=), but only when Org has none for =man:=.

The literate doc has a new section, and =CHANGELOG.org= has the entry.

:PROPERTIES:

A larger font than the frame was sized for is a common cause of clipped text in a posframe. This also changes the size of the plain minibuffer.

Docs: =sp-posframe.org= rewritten (with a section on what was removed), plus =dividers-and-lines.org=, =sp-fonts.org=, =main.org= and =CHANGELOG.org=.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW21PoXemQ4TWuXvmmeKXUB23][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
=sp-insert-note= / =sp-select-note= took seconds to open with the coloured tag column. =sp-org-tag-groups--with-tag-column= binds =vulpea-select-cache= to nil (the column width depends on the frame), so vulpea rebuilds the title and tag column of every note on each call. Per note that meant: sorting a copy of the rules, matching them, looking up the tag group with =mapcar=/=member= over the whole group alist, an =assoc=/=assq= for the colour, =frame-parameter= and =face-attribute=, and building the propertized chips again.

**** Change
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: change
:END:
=sp-org-tag-groups--memoize= keeps a hash table of results for the chip face of a tag, the emoji of a tag list, and the chips of a tag list and width. The table is cleared when the rules, groups, colours, palette, tag face height, =combo-consumes=, link position or the light/dark background mode change (compared with =eq=). Notes with the same tags now cost one hash lookup. Both the =.el= and the literate doc are updated, with a CHANGELOG entry.

**** Not tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-tested
:END:
Nothing was run in Emacs (none in the container); the diagnosis is from reading the code and the profile (time inside =command-execute=, not redisplay). If it is still slow, the remaining cost is vulpea's own =vulpea-db-query= of all notes, which this change does not touch.

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
=M-x sp-load-config-file= is =load-file= rooted at the configuration folder (=sp-load-path=). It lists every =.el= file below it, relative to the folder, and completes on them (category =file=, so Marginalia and Embark work), then loads the chosen one. No need to type the path.

The search is =directory-files-recursively=, not a shell tool, and skips =elpaca=, =eln-cache=, =backups=, =auto-save-list=, =.git=, =var= and =url= (=sp-load-config-file-excluded=).

It lives in =sp-navi= next to =sp-find-file=; the literate doc (=sp-navi.org=) and CHANGELOG are updated. No key binding added.

/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2VvsAv9bMnVw5hmscGggixs][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
With the plain posframe of #156 the =M-x= glitch is gone. This puts the minibuffer text size back, in a way that follows =text-scale-adjust=:

- =sp-minibuffer= maps the fontaine face =sp-minibuffer-face= (1.36 of =default= in =regular=, the same as =sp-text-face= in Org) onto =default=, as before.
- It then calls =text-scale-set= with the =text-scale-mode-amount= of the window that was selected when the minibuffer opened. So ~s-=~ / =s--= / =s-0= in a buffer scale the text of the next =M-x=, file picker or note picker in step with the buffer's text. A minibuffer that is already open does not change size.
- It is on =minibuffer-setup-hook= (the selected window is only known there), not =minibuffer-mode-hook=.
- It does not reset =face-remapping-alist=, which is what dropped the text scale in #146.

Docs (=sp-fonts.org=) and CHANGELOG updated.

**** Reading of the request
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: reading-of-the-request
:END:
I read "the size of the text equals the fontaine face" as: the base size is the fontaine face (=sp-minibuffer-face=), not a size of its own. Org text still uses =sp-text-face= as before. If you wanted the minibuffer at the plain =default= size, change the first line of =sp-minibuffer=.

**** Not tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-tested
:END:
Nothing was run in Emacs (none in the container). The glitch's cause was never found, and this text size was active while it happened (#146 to #154). If it returns, remove =(add-hook 'minibuffer-setup-hook #'sp-minibuffer)= first.

**** Cause
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: cause
:END:
=sp-bibliography-dir= was =(sp-paths--dir sp-documents-dir "bibliography/")=, but the first argument of =sp-paths--dir= is an environment variable /name/. =getenv= returned nil, so the folder became =bibliography/= below =default-directory=, which does not exist. =sp-bibtex-files= was then nil and =citar-bibliography= empty, hence =citar-select-refs: No bibliography set=. (=sp-bibtex-dir= no longer exists since #92; =sp-bibliography-dir= is the only option.)

**** Fix
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: fix
:END:
=(sp-paths--dir "SP_BIBLIOGRAPHY_DIR" (sp-path sp-documents-dir "bibliography/"))=: the env var, else =bibliography/= below =sp-documents-dir=, as the =sp-academic= doc already said. Doc and CHANGELOG updated.

**** Not tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-tested
:END:
Nothing was run in Emacs (none in the container). After updating, run =C-c w b r= (=sp-bibtex-register=) or restart; the folder must contain =.bib= files whose names start with a letter or digit.

- =sp-help=: advice on =shortdoc-add-function= turns a nil section into an empty string. Remove it once =taxy= is fixed.
- =sp-org-id-link=: =help:= also gets its own follow function (=sp-org-link-follow-help=) that opens faces, which the completer offers and Org's follow function rejects.

Column width and word wrap of the exc table are now part of the spec, so a saved view keeps them with its columns.

- New spec keys =:column-widths= (alist =(COLUMN . WIDTH)=, =t= for the columns not listed) and =:wrap= (=wrap= or =fit=). Views, the dynamic block and the menu carry them like any other key; vui and Org ignore them.
- =wrap= keeps the widths and wraps long text onto more lines. =fit= sizes each column to its longest text, up to =sp-collec-query-exc-max-width= (80). An explicit width always wins.
- New options =sp-collec-query-exc-wrap= and =sp-collec-query-exc-max-width=; =sp-collec-query-exc-column-widths= stays the default. A width in the spec overrides them.
- Menu: =w= sets the width of one column (or =other=), =W= cycles the wrap between default, =wrap= and =fit=.
- Docs and CHANGELOG updated.

Not run in Emacs (none in the container, and exc is not installed). Branch name could not be renamed to =169-…=: the proxy blocks branch renames.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2SnxWxFd1BzigKY2tZa4GJe][project thread]]/

A query table can now be sorted by several columns, applied in the order they are set.

*How I read the request:* "sort a column based on multiple parameters, set in order" as a primary sort key plus tie-breakers (like a spreadsheet's multi-level sort), each with its own direction.

- =:sort-by= may be a list of columns: the first is the primary key, each next one breaks ties of those before it. An element may be =(COLUMN . asc)= or =(COLUMN . desc)=; plain columns use =:sort-desc=. A single column still works.
- The sort is stable, so ties keep the query order (before, descending reversed them too).
- Menu: =o= reads the columns in order (=rating,title:desc=); =O= is the default direction for columns without their own.
- vui: clicking a column makes it primary and keeps the earlier clicks as tie-breakers (the number after the arrow is the rank); a Reset button returns to the spec's sort.
- exc and Org renderers, the dynamic block and saved views take the list through the spec; the summary line says "sorted by ...". exc's own in-grid sorting is not touched.
- New =tests/sp-collection-query-tables-test.el= (core sort with stubbed Vulpea, passes on Emacs 29.3). Menu and vui were not run in Emacs.
- Literate doc and CHANGELOG updated. Based on main after #169.

/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW28jXjUaoq76mQCkZLcJxtaz][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
Removes =sp-minibuffer= and its =minibuffer-setup-hook= line from =sp-fonts= (#161), which remapped =default= and set =text-scale= in the minibuffer buffer on every prompt and mirrored the minibuffer / glitched =M-x= in =vertico-posframe=.

The larger text now comes from one setting: =sp-posframe-update-font= turns =sp-minibuffer-face= (fontaine, 1.36 of =default= in =regular=) into =vertico-posframe-font=, a font spec with the =default= family at that size. It runs once at load and on =fontaine-set-preset-hook=; nothing runs per prompt. This is step 2 of the rebuild plan in the =sp-posframe= doc.

**** Trade-offs
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: trade-offs
:END:
- The size no longer follows =text-scale-adjust= of the calling buffer.
- Prompts shown at the bottom of the frame (plain =read-string=, =y-or-n-p=) and the terminal fallback keep the =default= size.
- If the glitch returns, set =vertico-posframe-font= to nil first (one line to bisect).

Docs (=sp-fonts.org=, =sp-posframe.org=) and CHANGELOG updated. Not run in Emacs (none in the container); please check the posframe size with =M-x=.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2DtCMR6qcoYVuswMQFkPCKF][project thread]]/

Follow-up to #173 for =rel-anno-fa2=.

- *Room between nodes:* graph-fa2 lays nodes out without knowing label sizes, so labels overlapped. Nodes are now drawn =relationship-annotator-fa2-spread= (4) times farther apart on a canvas that many times larger (advice on =graph-fa2-normalise-coords= and its inverse, so drag and click still match). Labels keep their size, so zoom in to read. The engine is now =2d=: in 3d, nodes behind each other overlap whatever the spacing.
- *Box behind each label:* a rounded box in the node's colour at 75% opacity (=relationship-annotator-fa2-box-opacity=); the text takes the theme foreground or background, whichever contrasts. graph-fa2 has no box option, so this post-processes its SVG (advice on =graph-fa2--render-svg=). I chose the box over making the box the node, because the circle still gives the layout and click target.
- *Theme colours:* the node fill is the foreground of a theme face per tag group colour (=relationship-annotator-fa2-group-faces=: orange is =warning=, green is =success=, gray is =shadow=, ...), and text, edge labels and edges follow =default= and =shadow=. It reads the theme each time the command runs.

Tested in headless Emacs 29 with the real graph-fa2: the SVG gets the boxes, and across 12 to 60 boxes (2d), overlapping pairs went from 6 to 33 at spread 1 to none at spread 4. In 3d some still overlapped, hence the 2d engine. Not seen on screen: how the colours look on your themes and the zoom level. Literate doc and CHANGELOG updated.

**** Changes

**** Is it fontaine?
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: is-it-fontaine
:END:
Probably not (read from the sources of fontaine, posframe and vertico-posframe; not run). =fontaine= only sets faces and knows nothing about child frames. =posframe= sizes and positions the child frame with the parent's =default-font-width= and =default-line-height=, so a larger font in the child needs more room than it gets. The doc lists what is not ruled out (font-spec vs string, points vs pixels) and three next steps.

Not run in Emacs (none in the container).

*Before:* seeing the output of one edit meant tangling all 130 module docs (the README block), or running =sp-tangle-all=, which listed four docs that no longer exist.

*Reading of "all notes":* the literate module docs in =docs/tangles/= (tangled to =libraries/modules/=), not the =~/notes= vault.

**** Changes (=sp-org-babel= doc and module, README)
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: changes-sp-org-babel-doc-and-module-readme
:END:
- =sp-tangle-changed=: tangles only docs whose text changed since they were last tangled. It compares a SHA-1 of each doc with the one in =tangle-hashes.eld= in =sp-cache-dir=, written after a successful tangle. No git is needed, so it works with yadm and uncommitted edits. A doc is also tangled when it has no entry or an =.el= it wrote is missing. =C-u= forces all.
- Changed =:tangle= path: the path is part of the doc text, so the doc is tangled to the new file; the old file is left in place and a message says so.
- A failing doc is reported, keeps its old entry and is retried next time; deleted docs are dropped from the cache.
- =sp-tangle-changed-and-reload=: also reloads the written modules that are loaded (via =sp-reload--run= if present, else =load=).
- =sp-tangle-on-save-mode=: opt-in, tangles the saved doc if it changed.
- =sp-tangle-all= now tangles every module doc; =sp-literate-files= is removed.
- README: new "Tangling only what changed" section (Emacs and shell).

Not done: a git-diff mode (the hash cache covers the same need without requiring commits).

**** Tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tested
:END:
Emacs 29.3 in batch on the real tree: 130 docs found, first run tangled 167 files, second run 0. A scratch tree covered a retargeted doc, a deleted output, and force. Not run in the interactive config. A full tangle also rewrites ~20 modules that differ from their docs (final newline and similar); I did not commit those.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2VaozMqv8TaGKJqSqW7rjFE][project thread]]/

*Before:* searching the tab inbox meant =sp-tab-inbox='s title mentions in the sidebar; no free-form or semantic query, and no way to file the results into a new note.

*After:* =C-c k t= (=sp-tab-psearch=) asks for a query and opens a p-search session over the inbox only, ranked by =org-semantic=. In the result buffer, =embark-act= collects the result at point (=c=) or the top N (=C=) into a note you pick or create.

**** Changes (new =sp-tab-psearch= module and doc, =init.el=, docs, CHANGELOG)
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: changes-new-sp-tab-psearch-module-and-doc-initel-docs-changelog
:END:
- Candidate generator: each line of =sp-tab-inbox-dir= is a candidate (headings, keywords and drawers skipped), opened on its line.
- Semantic prior: query goes to =org-semantic= with a =dir:= predicate for the inbox, so nothing else in the notes appears. Hit order sets the score (0.9 down to 0.55), lines no hit contains get 0.3. =C-u= also adds p-search's word query.
- =sp-tab-psearch-engine= (=C-c k T=): same search as a p-search engine search box.
- Collect reuses =sp-tab-inbox-collect-all= (background move, link left behind, new note from a title).
- Loaded late, after =sp-semantic=. p-search is already installed by =sp-search= (use-package with Elpaca); this module installs nothing.

**** Choices to check
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: choices-to-check
:END:
- *"Embark collect"* is read as an embark action on the result set (targets =sp-tab-idea= and =sp-tab-idea-results=), not an =embark-collect= buffer: p-search results are not completion candidates.
- org-semantic's grouping by note/section is not used (the unit is a line); only its ranking is.
- The semantic search blocks while the prior is calculated, and runs twice on start (p-search recalculates).
- Branch number 182 was the next free number when I pushed; check nobody else took it.

**** Tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tested
:END:
Emacs 29.3 in batch with cloned p-search, compat and embark, and a stub for org-semantic: generator, both priors, ranking, document ids, both embark targets. *Not run:* the real org-semantic server (and whether it indexes =inbox/tabs/=, see =.org-semantic-ignore=), Elpaca, the interactive collect prompt.

Binary and state files that packages wrote into the config folder (and that were tracked in Git) now live in ignored folders. Full table in the new "State files" section of =docs/tangles/base/sp-globals.org=.

| File                                                                              | Now                                                                                                                       |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| =vulpea.db= (=vulpea-db-location=)                                                | =var/=                                                                                                                    |
| =discourse-graphs.db= (=dg-db-file=)                                              | =var/=                                                                                                                    |

| =.org-id-locations=                                                               | already =var/cache/=, nothing to change                                                                                   |
| =bookmarks= (=bookmark-default-file=)                                             | =libraries/lambda-user/= (=sp-user-dir=, the existing folder for personal files, tracked by Git: bookmarks are user data) |
| =projectile-bookmarks.eld=                                                        | =var/etc/= (known projects, kept)                                                                                         |
| =projectile-frecency.eld=, =project.el= list, =amx-items=                         | =var/cache/=                                                                                                              |
| =org_dataview.db=, =places.eld=, =projects.eld=, =agent-shell/markdown-links.eld= | untracked and ignored (see below)                                                                                         |

**** Findings
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: findings
:END:
- *amx*: =amx-items= held only amx's initial command list and an empty history. Nothing in the config installs or loads amx; the file is a leftover. If a package pulls amx in, its save file is now in =var/cache/=.
- *=.eld= files* (tracked at the root, all package defaults, none edited by hand): =projectile-bookmarks.eld= (known projects, kept), =projectile-frecency.eld= (visit counts, cache), =projects.eld= and =places.eld= (stale: =nil= and an old =elpa/lambda-themes= path), =agent-shell/markdown-links.eld= (opened links, cache). Already elsewhere: =tabspaces-session.eld=, =fontaine-latest-state.eld=, saved query-table views. User data among them: only the known-projects list and the saved views. No =tangle-hashes.eld= or reload-hash file exists in the repo.
- *=org_dataview.db=*: an SQLite table of Org properties from the =org-dataview= experiment, which is commented out in =sp-org-ext=. I did not guess its location variable, so it is only untracked and ignored.
- =forge-database.sqlite= and =url/cookies= are also tracked at the root; left alone.

**** Before you pull (Git deletes the tracked copies)
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: before-you-pull-git-deletes-the-tracked-copies
:END:
#+begin_src sh
cd ~/.config/emacs-modular && mkdir -p var/etc var/cache
cp discourse-graphs.db var/discourse-graphs.db
cp org_dataview.db var/org-dataview.db
cp savehist var/savehist
cp projectile-bookmarks.eld var/etc/
cp projectile-frecency.eld var/cache/
[ -f vulpea.db ] && mv vulpea.db var/vulpea.db   # untracked, Git does not touch it
#+end_src

=bookmarks= is moved by Git. If =vulpea.db= is not moved, Vulpea just rebuilds it (slower first start). Nothing is deleted on your machine by me.

/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2DKRxoYBrmeAxkSjCBcW8dP][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
The query tables (=#+BEGIN: collection-query-table=, read from Vulpea's database) only changed when you ran =C-c C-x C-u=. New =sp-collec-query-dblock-auto-mode= does that step for you. It is *off by default*: turn it on with =(sp-collec-query-dblock-auto-mode 1)=.

- =open=: a moment after visiting an Org file that has a block (idle timer, so opening is not slowed).
- =save=: =sp-collec-query-dblock-delay= (2 s) after any Org note is saved, every open buffer with a block is updated (gives Vulpea's autosync time to read the file).
- Only the =collection-query-table= blocks (and the old =vulpea-table= name) are touched, never clock tables; buffers without a block are skipped by a text search.
- No loops: an unchanged result leaves the buffer unmodified (compared by buffer hash); nothing is saved unless =sp-collec-query-dblock-save= is set, and then only a buffer with no unsaved edits, and that save starts no new round.
- Also =M-x sp-collec-query-dblock-update-all= for a one-off.

Docs: new section "Keeping dynamic blocks up to date" in =docs/tangles/funct/sp-collection-query-tables.org=; the =.el= is tangled from it. CHANGELOG entry under Open pull requests.

**** Tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tested
:END:
Emacs 29.3 batch, 7 new ERT tests in =tests/sp-collection-query-tables-test.el= with the block writer stubbed: same result stays unmodified, new result written, other dblocks untouched, save only when asked and never over unsaved edits, old block name, hooks added and removed.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2X5GbEkTg1acJJLTffK42Xc][project thread]]/

Adds =sp-author-notes= (=M-x sp-author-notes=, =sp-author-notes-preview=), documented in =docs/tangles/funct/sp-author-notes.org=.

What it does:

- Reads =litnotes/= (file-level meta only) and fixes typos of =pub-author= (=pub-authro=, =Pub_Author=; two edits away is only reported).
- Creates a =:person:= note for each plain author name with no note, via =sp-org--write-note=, and turns the name into an =[[id:...]]= link. (=sp-org--create-note= does not exist; this is the function behind =sp-org-create-note-and-link=.)
- In each =:person:= author note: ensures =* Basics=, then =* Works= after it, then a =collection-query-table= block (=:parent-of "self" :parent-prop "pub-author"=, columns title, read-status, read-priority, pub-year, relevance-factor, sorted by pub-year) unless one exists.
- Report buffer of fixed / created / converted / updated notes, plus things left alone.

Safety: preview first, asks before writing; idempotent; insert-only; backups in =author-notes-backups/=; skips files with unsaved buffers; ambiguous or conflicting titles are reported, not touched.

Tested: 8 ERT tests in Emacs 29.3 batch with a temporary vault (=sp-org--write-note= stubbed). Not tested: the real =~/notes=, vulpea DB, filling the dblocks, the report buffer on screen.

Adds =sp-author-notes-bibtex= (=M-x sp-author-notes-bibtex=): the "additional" view of the author notes, for works that exist only as BibTeX entries.

- Reads the =.bib= files of =sp-bibtex-files= (keys like =smith2020attention=).
- Compares the title of every =:person:= note with each entry's =author= field: *exact* after flipping =Last, First=, *possible* when last name and first initial agree.
- Leaves out entries that already have a litnote (key found in the head or file name of a note in =litnotes/=: =REFERENCES=, =ROAM_REFS=, =#+reference:=, =@key=).
- Report buffer, one section per author note. =c= creates the litnote for the entry at point, =C= for all exact entries of the section (both ask first), =RET=/=o= visit, =g= refreshes.
- The note is made by =sp-author-notes-bibtex-create-function= (=citar-create-note= by default, so the =sp-litnotes= templates apply), then a =- pub-author :: [[id:...][Name]]= line is added so it joins the =Works= table.

Docs: =docs/tangles/funct/sp-author-notes-bibtex.org= (the =.el= is tangled from it), README and CHANGELOG entries, loaded in =init.el= after =sp-author-notes=.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW26HKpAWZDaiUHoQ6yyQQEt8][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
=tools/quick-capture-native= no longer waits for Emacs. It now:

1. asks for the line in the macOS dialog (or takes it as an argument, skipping the dialog),
2. writes it atomically to a spool folder (=~/.local/state/quick-capture=, override with =QUICK_CAPTURE_SPOOL=),
3. pokes Emacs in the background with =emacsclient -n -e '(sp-quick-capture-drain)'= and returns.

=sp-quick-capture-drain= (new) files the queued lines oldest first and deletes each file. It runs on the poke, 2 seconds after the module loads (lines captured while Emacs was down), and after =sp-quick-capture-drain-interval= (30) idle seconds. Failures go to =failed/= in the spool. The file's mtime is the capture time, used for =:CREATED:= and for relative dates (=!tom=), so a line filed days later still means what you meant.

**** Why this approach
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: why-this-approach
:END:
Before, =emacsclient -e= blocked while Emacs was busy and the line was lost when Emacs was not running. A spool file keeps the task safe on disk and needs no extra tool: AppleScript and bash are already used, and Hammerspoon, Shortcuts, Alfred or Raycast can call the script (with an argument, if they have their own input box). Writing straight into =inbox.org= from bash was rejected: it would race with the open Emacs buffer and duplicate the parser.

**** Tests
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tests
:END:
- 4 new ERT tests (capture time, ordering, partial files ignored, failures parked, no spool); all 13 pass in Emacs 29.3 batch.
- Real daemon on Linux: with the daemon stopped (=SIGSTOP=) the script returns in 0.02 s and the line is filed on resume. Plain =emacsclient -n= did hang for 15 s on a stopped daemon, which is why the poke runs in the background. With the daemon dead the line stays queued.
- Not run on macOS (dialog, notifications, hotkey launchers).

The module is tangled from =docs/tangles/text/sp-quick-capture.org=; CHANGELOG entry is in the Quick capture set.

**** Why the search failed
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: why-the-search-failed
:END:
=[]= is the empty vector of enabled sources: =consult-omni--multi-lookup= takes =(aref sources 0)= and there were none. Cause was in the config, not the package: =(require 'consult-omni-sources)= only defines the loader, and the call to =consult-omni-sources-load-modules= sat in a =:tangle no= block, so no source was ever defined and every name in =consult-omni-multi-sources= was silently dropped. (A source is also dropped while its API key, program or package is missing, so a list of only such names fails the same way.)

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
- Vendored copy of consult-omni in =libraries/modules/cloned/consult-omni/= (GPL-3.0-or-later; upstream ships no LICENSE file, so the GPL text is added and every file keeps its header). =VENDORED.org= has the upstream commit and the two local patches (a clear =user-error= instead of =aref= on an empty vector).
- =sp-browsing=: loads that copy with =:ensure nil= + =:load-path= (same pattern as =sp-consult-snapfile=; this is a deliberate exception to the Elpaca rule because you asked for the source in the config), calls the loader in =:config=, ends with =provide=, and is added to =sp-late-modules=.
- The three scope commands passed =args= where =consult-omni-multi= expects =min-input=; they now share one helper.
- TODOs: API keys in =var/consult-omni-secrets.el= (ignored by Git); a =Vulpea= title source for =consult-omni-local=; =sp-fetch-academic-omni= (=C-c w b s=) sends a scholar result to =sp-fetch-academic-doi= or =-download=. Left as TODO with notes: DEVONthink, sp-trails integration, results in another buffer, launcher.
- Google Scholar: comparison in the =sp-browsing= doc. Recommendation: keep =biblio-gscholar=; use OpenAlex/PubMed/Scopus through consult-omni, joined at the DOI. Scholar has no API, and a keystroke-driven source would scrape it repeatedly and hit CAPTCHAs.

**** Heads up
:PROPERTIES:

:END:
- The old doc had a real-looking Google Custom Search key in a commented line. Removed, but it is in Git history: rotate it if it is real.
- Rebasing onto =main= brought in the litdb block from #197; the doc and =.el= agree (tangle check passes).

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2LUVdS2HhkPxfyzVVQAEeL1][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
=sp-reading-mode= in =sp-writedesk= (=C-c w r=): a buffer-local minor mode for reading long prose in Org. From Rougier's book-mode and its article example it keeps the margins (8 left, 6 right), the line spacing (1) and the zero fringes; all are =defcustom=s.

- Turns =olivetti-mode= off while active (both use window margins) and back on afterwards if it was on.
- Wraps lines (=visual-line-mode=).
- Records the local state of =line-spacing=, margin and fringe widths, =word-wrap=, =truncate-lines=, =visual-line-mode= and =olivetti-mode= first; toggling off restores each.
- Margins are reapplied to every window on the buffer after window changes.

Only the ideas are used; the code is new (book-mode is GPL-3.0, nothing copied). Left out: the header/mode-line, frame resizing and =message= override, and Rougier's margin bullets and heading markers (listed as not done in the doc).

**** Tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tested
:END:
Emacs 29.3 batch: on sets spacing 1, margin 8, fringe 0, visual-line on, olivetti off; off restores everything (including non-local state) and olivetti on. =tools/tangle-all.el= writes the =.el= identical to the committed one. Not seen on screen in a real frame.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2YZxiADvTCtDjAA91N2hKJ7][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
=org-table-widget= was already enabled in =sp-textui=, but it ran with defaults that look nothing like Obsidian, and =org-modern= was drawing its own borders over the same tables (its README says to turn =org-modern-table= off). In =sp-org-tables=:

- =org-modern-table= is =nil=; zebra stripes are off.
- Widget borders and header row take quiet colours blended from the theme (=sp-org-tables-border-strength= 0.22, =sp-org-tables-header-strength= 0.07), recomputed on =enable-theme-functions=.
- =sp-org-tables-quiet-pipes-mode= (on in Org buffers) dims =|= and rule lines of the plain-text table, for terminals and while a table is revealed for editing.

**** Is it possible?
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: is-it-possible
:END:
Nearly, in a GUI. The widget always draws a full grid (outer box and vertical bars), so borders can be made faint but not removed. For fully borderless Obsidian rows a different renderer would be needed. In plain text, Org cannot hide the pipes without hurting editing, so they are only dimmed.

**** Tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tested
:END:
4 ERT tests in Emacs 29.3 batch (colour blend, =org-modern-table=, dimmed pipes). The doc tangles to the module. Not seen in a graphical Emacs: please restart and look at a table, then adjust the two strength options to taste.

  - =litdb= runs =litdb fulltext= and is in the default =consult-omni-multi-sources=.
  - =litdb semantic= runs =litdb vsearch= (loads the model on each call, so it is only a command, =consult-omni-litdb-semantic=).
  - Results are candidates in the minibuffer; =RET= on one opens its address (OpenAlex/DOI) with =browse-url=, or visits the file. Generic: any record litdb holds (e.g. later from DEVONthink) shows up.
  - Disabled when the =litdb= program is not on =exec-path=. =b=/=B= in =sp-search-menu=.
- *No accidental Google*: =RET= on input that is not a result (results not arrived yet) ran =consult-omni-external-search= in the browser. =sp-consult-omni-ignore-new= now only says nothing was opened.

Docs (=sp-browsing.org=, =sp-search.org=), tangled modules and CHANGELOG updated; tangle check agrees for these files.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia*/

**** Summary
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: summary
:END:
- =sp-litnotes= now uses =citar-vulpea= only; =citar-denote= is removed. Citation keys live in the =ROAM_REFS= property (=@key=), and =citar-vulpea-mode= is switched on (it was never enabled before).
- New =sp-litnotes-refs=: =M-x sp-litnotes-refs-report= (dry run, writes nothing) and =M-x sp-litnotes-refs-convert=. It asks up to three questions: move =#+reference:= to =:ROAM_REFS: @key=; create an =:ID:= for notes that have none; add a stub entry to =master.bib= (the inbox) for each key no registered =.bib= has. Every changed note and =master.bib= are backed up first; safe to rerun.
- The report lists keys that no registered =.bib= has, keys used by several notes, and for each key whether a PDF exists under its own name or only under its =crossref= parent (needed by the DEVONthink link in #209).

Follows #209 (design).

**** Test plan
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: test-plan
:END:
- [X] 6 ERT tests in Emacs 31.1 batch (=tests/sp-litnotes-refs-test.el=).
- [X] Dry run read on the real =~/notes/litnotes= (1251 notes): 1185 convert, 1 merge, 65 have no =:ID:= (would get one if you agree), 87 keys are not in any =.bib= (87 stubs for =master.bib=).
- [ ] Run =M-x sp-litnotes-refs-report= in Emacs, read it, then =M-x sp-litnotes-refs-convert=.
- [ ] Restart Emacs and check =citar-vulpea= finds the converted notes (=C-c w b n=).

* PR #211: ⚡ Cache the dashboard's open TODOs per agenda file
:PROPERTIES:
:PR_NUMBER: 211
:URL: https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/pull/211
:STATE: closed
:AUTHOR: siainbuletin
:END:
- Link :: [[https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/pull/211][https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/pull/211]]
- State :: closed
- Author :: @siainbuletin
- Opened :: 2026-10-31 17:31
- Closed :: 2026-10-31 17:31
- Branch :: =claude/project-thread-sy67o6= → =main=
- Merge commit :: [[https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/commit/3c2562bdbb72293baf3bc167cecc154270b195b6][3c2562bdbb]]

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2HBvg9rAnd4CKXNEFXyzUer][project thread]]/

**** Summary
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: summary
:END:
The dashboard read every agenda file through Org at each start and redraw. It now keeps each file's open TODOs in =sp-cache-dir= (=dashboard-entries.eld=), keyed by path + mtime + size.

- Only new or changed files are read at start; deleted files are dropped; the cache is dropped when =org-todo-keywords= changes.
- Deadline/scheduled are cached as absolute days and made relative on read, so they do not go stale overnight.
- A changed file is read from disk in a temp buffer (no mode hooks, nothing left open): =org-map-entries= on a file name reuses an open buffer, which could put an older version in the cache. A buffer with unsaved edits is read instead and not cached.
- The per-draw =sp-dashboard--entries-cache= and the public/private filtering in =sp-dashboard--todos= are unchanged.
- Message: =[dashboard] read 100 agenda files: 99 cached, 1 re-read, in 0.01s=.
- =M-x sp-dashboard-clear-entries-cache= resets it.

**** Findings
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: findings
:END:
*Coverage (100 agenda files from the running Emacs).* =org-map-entries= finds 362 keyword headings (339 open, 23 done). org-ql =(todo)= finds the same 339 plus 3 TODOs under a =* Archive :ARCHIVE:= heading, which the dashboard skips on purpose; with =(not (tags "ARCHIVE"))= the two match exactly. The file with its own =#+TODO: OPEN | ANSWERED= is read correctly by both. vulpea.db has only 35 todo rows (it indexes only headings with an ID), so it cannot be the source.

*Engine speed.* org-ql is not meaningfully faster: cold 2.5--3.4 s against 2.5--2.9 s for =org-map-entries=, almost all of it visiting the files. Warm it was 0.02--0.04 s against 0.05--0.07 s, possibly its own cache. The cache therefore keeps =org-map-entries= (no extra package).

**** Before / after (100 files, 339 entries, Emacs 31.1 batch =-Q=, so no real org-mode hooks)
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: before--after-100-files-339-entries-emacs-311-batch--q-so-no-real-org-mode-hooks
:END:
| Case                               | Time         | GC                  |
|------------------------------------+--------------+---------------------|
| Before, cold                       | 2.5--3.1 s   | 2 GCs, 0.03--0.04 s |
| Before, warm (buffers open)        | 0.05--0.10 s | 0--1 GC             |
| After, first start (no cache file) | 1.21 s       | 3 GCs, 0.06 s       |
| After, all files cached            | 0.00--0.01 s | none                |
| After, one file changed            | 0.50 s       | 1 GC, 0.02 s        |

Cache file: 98 KB.

**** Tests
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tests
:END:
7 ERT tests (=tests/sp-dashboard-entries-test.el=): hit, persistence, changed file, deleted file, keyword change, relative days, archived/unsaved. Run in Emacs 31.1 batch. Not seen in the interactive dashboard; the figures above do not include the org-mode hooks of the real configuration.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2X5GbEkTg1acJJLTffK42Xc][project thread]]/

Follows #204. In =sp-author-notes=, an unquoted =pub-author= piece with more than one comma (=Francisco López-Muñoz, Gabriel Rubio, Juan D. Molina, Cecilio Alam=) was read as one name. It is now its own case:

- The report has a section "Lists of names with commas, to disambiguate" with the split it proposes: each piece a name when the first piece has two words or more, =Last, First= pairs (flipped) when it is one word and the count is even, no proposal otherwise.
- When the changes are written you are asked whether to split it (=sp-author-notes-disambiguate-function=, default =y-or-n-p=). Yes makes one author and one =:person:= note per name; no leaves the text as it is.
- One comma (=Smith, John=) is still one name; =;=, =and= and quotes work as before.

Tested: 15 ERT tests in Emacs 29.3 batch with a temporary vault. Not run on the real =~/notes=.
