First piece of integrating =sp-search= / =consult-omni= with =sp-trails=: a new module =sp-trails-search= (with literate doc).

- =sp-trails-search= (=o= in =sp-trails-map=, =j= in the =C-c s m= menu) asks which consult-omni search to run (web and notes, web, scholarly, my notes), starts/resumes a trail if none is current, and runs it.
- =RET= on a result still opens it in the external browser, and also adds it to the trail as a =TOREAD= page (query, source, DOI, authors kept as properties). Nothing is recorded while only browsing results.
- The page hangs under the trail page at point, else under the trail. The browser extension later reports the same URL, which =sp-trails-add-page= dedupes, and links followed from it become its children.
- Embark action =t= records a result without opening it.
- Done by advising =consult-omni--get-source-prop= for =:on-callback= only while a trail search runs, so no vendored code is patched.

Not in this PR (listed in the doc): ripgrep results as trail nodes, linking saved views to trail nodes, recording note results.

:PROPERTIES:

=sp-dashboard--scan-file= (added in #213) reads each changed agenda file with =insert-file-contents= in a =with-temp-buffer=, then sets =buffer-file-name=. The insert leaves the buffer modified, so when =with-temp-buffer= kills it Emacs asks =Buffer  *temp*-123456 modified; kill anyway?=, once per scanned file. =--debug-init= shows nothing because it is a prompt, not an error. Before #213 the files were visited through =org-map-entries= on file lists, with no such buffer.

**** Fix
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: fix
:END:
Mark the buffer unmodified before setting =buffer-file-name= and again after =org-mode=. Module, tangled doc, CHANGELOG and one ERT test updated.

Integrates the pasted =font-cycle.el= into =sp-fonts= (doc section "Font cycling" + tangled module), on top of the existing fontaine presets.

- =M-x sp-font-cycle= opens a transient menu: left/right cycle the installed families, up/down change the size (reusing =font-size-increase=/=-decrease=), =y= copies the =set-face-attribute= form, =r= restores the starting font, =q= quits.
- The family list is =sp-font-cycle-families= (your list) plus the default families of =fontaine-presets=, filtered by =find-font=.
- *=s= saves permanently*: it asks for a fontaine preset (current one by default) and rewrites =:default-family= / =:default-height= of that preset in =docs/tangles/ui/sp-fonts.org= /and/ =libraries/modules/ui/sp-fonts.el= (so the tangle check stays green), updates the preset table row in the doc, then =y-or-n-p= offers to =load= the module and re-apply the preset. It refuses if a buffer visiting either file is modified.
- No key is bound (=C-c f= is taken); bind =sp-font-cycle= where you like.

New module =sp-litnotes-titles= (section of =docs/tangles/academic/sp-academic.org=, required by =sp-litnotes=). Litnotes are identified by =ROAM_REFS= now, so the title no longer has to be the citekey.

- =M-x sp-litnotes-titles-report= is a dry run (writes nothing): per note, the references, old and new =#+title:= (from =pub-title=), old and new file name, and =file:= links elsewhere that name the old file. Skipped or flagged: no =:ID:= drawer, no or empty =pub-title=, a file name in neither scheme, a title with no slug, a new name that already exists or that two notes would share, case-only changes; notes that share a title are listed too.
- =M-x sp-litnotes-titles-apply= shows that report, asks once, copies each note to =var/litnote-title-backups/<time>/=, writes the title, renames the file, then =vulpea-db--forget-file= (old path), =org-id-add-location= and =vulpea-db-update-file= (same calls as =sp-split--denote-rename=). The =:ID:= is checked unchanged after the write; locked files and files with unsaved buffers are skipped.
- File names: Denote =ID--slug__keywords.org= (the litnotes of citar-denote) and =YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_slug.org= are read; the identifier, separator and keywords stay and only the slug is rebuilt (lower case, ASCII, 100 characters at most; =sp-litnotes-titles-slug-function=). =sp-litnotes-titles-rename-files= nil copies titles only.
- Independent of the =ROAM_REFS= conversion of #210: it can run before or after it.

Follows #212. In =sp-author-notes=:

*=and= separators*

- =Ann Lee and Bo Roe=, =Smith, John and Doe, Jane= and =Smith, John and Ann Lee= still split on =and= as before.
- A list with commas that ends in =and= (=Ann Lee, Bo Roe, and Cy Poe=) used to split at the =and= and leave =Ann Lee, Bo Roe,= as one flipped name. It is now one disambiguation case (as in #212) with all the names proposed.

*Dropping candidates*

- In the report, =d= drops the candidate on the line from the plan and refreshes the preview, =u= restores it, =A= writes what is left, =g= refreshes keeping the drops. A note (litnote, author note, note to tag) is dropped as a file (not read or changed); an author to create is dropped by name (no note, the name stays plain). Dropped items are listed at the end of the report.
- =M-x sp-author-notes= now asks =y= (write all), =r= (stay in the report to review) or =q=. =M-x sp-author-notes-preview= forgets earlier drops.
- I chose dropping over marking: the default is "write everything shown", and =d= removes the exceptions.

Tested: 18 ERT tests in Emacs 29.3 batch (report keys driven in a batch buffer). Not run on the real vault or on screen.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BZHwSgnGAC4LTh4wgvYJsE?thread=cmsg_01BZHwSgnGAC4LTh4wgvYJsESgfFwDt41Q2LvPimo5EdKU][project thread]]/

Before: plugging the iPod into the Mac let Finder sync it straight away, which read and deleted =iPod_Control/iTunes/Play Counts=, so Legacy Scrobbler had nothing left to scrobble.

After: =~/.config/listening/ipod-no-autosync= turns that off and can undo it.

- =on= (default, safe to rerun) sets ~dontAutomaticallySyncIPods = true~ in =com.apple.AMPDevicesAgent= (Finder's device sync helper, 10.15+) and =com.apple.iTunes= (10.14 and earlier), then restarts =AMPDevicesAgent=. Earlier values are saved for =off=.
- =status= shows both settings, the agent, mounted iPods and whether =Play Counts= is still on them.
- =off= restores the values from before =on=.
- =backup= copies =Play Counts= + =iTunesDB= from every mounted iPod to =$XDG_DATA_HOME/listening/ipod-backups/=, skipping unchanged copies.
- =agent install|remove= adds a launchd agent (=StartOnMount=) that runs =backup= whenever a volume mounts.

The per-device Finder checkbox "Automatically sync when this iPod is connected" is not changed by the script; the docs and =on= output say to untick it once.

How: bash 3.2--compatible script in =.config/listening/=, a new section in =PLAN.org=, and a CHANGELOG entry. Stacked on #171 because =PLAN.org= only exists there.

Testing: run in a Linux container against stand-ins for =uname=, =defaults=, =pgrep=, =killall= and =/Volumes= (=IPOD_VOLUMES= override): on → on again (no-op) → backup ×2 (second skipped) → off restored the original =false= and removed the unset key. *Not run on a Mac*: whether current macOS still honours the =AMPDevicesAgent= key, whether Finder reads Play Counts on connect even without syncing (the backup agent is the fallback and may lose that race), and the launchd agent.

- Labels :: new-feature, needs-further-testing

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2DwKs8EnpZNPfWS66eBJq9A][project thread]]/

Stacked on #228 (it moved the docs of these commands into =sp-org-lint.org=); retarget to =main= after #228 merges.

**** Summary
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: summary
:END:
=sp-author-notes= (preview, apply, refresh), =sp-author-notes-bibtex=, =sp-litnotes-refs-report=/=-convert= and =sp-litnotes-titles-report=/=-apply= no longer read and write the whole vault in one go. A new module, =sp-async-work=, runs them as jobs in slices of 50 ms from timers, between your keystrokes (it stops a slice early when a key is waiting).

- Progress is in the mode line, e.g. =[Litnote titles writing 12/340]=. =M-x sp-async-work-cancel= stops a job; files already written keep their backups.
- A job waits while you type in the minibuffer, so its questions never replace yours.
- Reports open when the reading is done; the commands return at once.
- A big =.bib= file is read 200 entries per slice.

**** Why not a second Emacs
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: why-not-a-second-emacs
:END:
The footnote lint uses =emacs -Q --batch=, which fits a pure file-to-result job. These commands ask questions in the middle (disambiguating names, missing years, confirmations), query the Vulpea database, create notes through the interactive machinery, and update open buffers and the database after writing. A headless Emacs has none of that, so each command would be split into two copies of its logic. Slices keep every question and database call where it was; nothing runs in parallel, so there is no race with your editing.

**** Safety
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: safety
:END:
- Report first, backup before write: unchanged.
- =sp-litnotes-refs-convert= now asks its (up to three) questions right after the report opens, before any writing, so nothing asks you something while you work elsewhere.
- =sp-litnotes-refs-convert= and =sp-litnotes-titles-apply= re-check each note right before writing: skipped if its buffer has unsaved changes or it changed since the report (named in the summary). Open buffers without changes are reverted/killed as before.
- =sp-author-notes= keeps its earlier rule: an unsaved buffer is saved first when you apply.

**** Decisions for you
:PROPERTIES:

**** Summary
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: summary
:END:
=M-x sp-author-notes-bibtex= made Emacs unresponsive. It was not a missing file: every author note was compared with every author of every entry (people × entries × authors, each comparison allocating strings). With #229's slices it still froze, because one author note is one indivisible step and took seconds on a big =.bib=.

- The entries without a litnote are indexed once (new "indexing" stage) by full author name and by last name plus first initial; a note looks up only its own keys. Results and their order are unchanged.
- Missing files: a file of =sp-bibtex-files= that cannot be read is skipped with a message. No files, or none readable, stops with a =user-error= naming them and suggesting =sp-bibtex-register=.
- Doc (=sp-org-lint.org=) tangled, CHANGELOG entry added.

:END:
- 3,000 author notes, 500 entries: 48.7 s before.
- 3,000 author notes, 40,000 entries (31 MB =.bib=), 5,000 litnotes: about 7 s after (3.8 s reading the =.bib=), in slices. Before, extrapolated, hours.

Reports =author=/=editor= names not in the canonical =Last, First= form, fields out of the order of =sp-bibtex-field-order=, duplicate keys, entries it cannot read, and names one typo (≤2 edits) away from an existing author note.

- =sp-bibtex-author-capf= in =bibtex-mode=: completes names in =author=/=editor= from the author notes, in =Last, First=.
- *No author note is ever created*; the vault is only read. A name with no note is not reported.

/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2HHkasK1mnHK76yFvmtt9Jo][project thread]]/

*Cause.* =org-table-widget= hides each row's source and draws the row as the =before-string= of an overlay. A click or =RET= is delivered to the hidden source, where =org-open-at-point= finds no link, climbs to the headline and offers every link of the entry. That is the menu.

*Fix* (in =sp-org-tables=, literate doc updated):

- A click follows the link under the pointer (advice on =org-open-at-mouse=, reading the =htmlize-link= property the widget keeps in its cells).
- =RET= (in =org-table-widget-map=) and =C-c C-o= on a row follow its link; a chooser appears only when the row has several links, since =RET= cannot know which was meant. A row without links keeps the old =RET= (=org-return=).

*Tested.* 5 ERT tests with a faked widget row, Emacs 29.3 batch (=tests/sp-org-tables-links-test.el=), and the tangle check. *Not run* with the real widget in a graphical Emacs (also the layout preserving =htmlize-link= across wrapped cells, which I read in the source but did not see run).

**** Summary
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: summary
:END:
Fixes =Error running timer 'vulpea-ui--run-scheduled-sync': (wrong-type-argument vulpea-note nil)=.

The sidebar sync renders the backlinks widget, which calls =vulpea-ui-backlinks-note-filter= with the note of each linking file. That note is nil when the file is not in the vulpea database yet (new, unsynced or untracked file, as happens around the =sp-org-tag-= commands that open or create files). Our filter called =vulpea-note-tags= on it. It now keeps such files.

Changed in the org source (=docs/tangles/vulpea/sp-vulpea.org=) and the tangled =sp-vulpea-ui.el= identically, plus a CHANGELOG entry.

**** Testing
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: testing
:END:
Not run: no Emacs in the container, and the filter is an inline =use-package= option, so no ERT test. The cause was read from the installed vulpea-ui source (=vulpea-ui--backlinks= calls the filter with =file-note=, which can be nil).

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW26mksCEt6KEG7sXwPqeNpNV][project thread]]/

New module =sp-refile= (doc =docs/tangles/funct/sp-refile.org=, tangled =sp-refile.el=) with one command, =sp-refile= (=C-x s t=, =C-c C-w= in Org):

- On a heading it asks "Refile to" with one list: headings of the current note (the =org-refile= case), =[New note: own file]= (calls =sp-split-leave-parents=, so the #240 =- seealso ::= handling is unchanged) or =[Another note...]= (pick a note, then a heading or the top of it).
- Before the first heading (or =C-u C-u=) it merges the whole note under a heading of another note: title becomes the heading, filetags its tags, the =:ID:= stays so links still resolve, then the old file is deleted after confirmation.
- The copy is saved in the target before the source is removed.

Decisions to check:

- =vulpea-merge= is not in this repo or the container's Vulpea, so the merge is built from Org functions only.
- =sp-split-leave-parents= stays as the split engine (code and tests untouched); =sp-refile= requires it. I did not move its 650 lines.
- =C-x s t= now runs =sp-refile= (autoload and binding in =sp-org-base=); =sp-move-region-to-heading= (loose text, =M-a=) is untouched.

Testing: 4 ERT tests (=tests/sp-refile-test.el=) pass in Emacs 29.3 batch with Vulpea/Denote stubbed. The prompts, the split path, merge deletion and the real Vulpea database were not run.

Branch is the session's =claude/project-thread-rbj71z=, not number-prefixed, as the number was not known beforehand.

Opening an Org file failed with =Invalid association in tag alist: <<<<<<<=.

*Cause (likely):* =main= has no conflict markers anywhere (checked with =git grep=), so the leftover is only in the local copy on the Mac. =sp-org-tag-registry.el= is a data file that =sp-org-tag-add= edits and =load-file=s, and a =<<<<<<< HEAD= line inside its quoted list reads as the symbol =<<<<<<<=, which Org rejects. The recent =Merge branch 'main'= commit is the probable source. The =git-gutter:live-update= error is probably a side effect of the failed mode setup; not confirmed.

*To fix your copy:* open =~/.config/emacs-modular/libraries/modules/funct/sp-org-tag-registry.el=, keep both sides' tags, delete the =<<<<<<<=, ~=======~ and =>>>>>>>= lines.

*This PR:*

- =sp-org-tag-registry.el= drops non-tag entries (such as marker symbols) and shows a warning, so Org still starts.
- =tools/check-conflict-markers.sh= and the =conflict-markers= workflow fail on leftover =<<<<<<<= / =>>>>>>>= lines (checked on a file with markers).
- CHANGELOG entry.

Not run in Emacs (none in the container).

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2GtzUm5hXcLmjePs7nN39W2][project thread]]/

Settles ADR 0020 and implements it.

- *Unsorted group:* a tag in no group is allowed. =sp-org-tag-group-of= answers =("unsorted")=: no emoji, default colour, no warning. The tag menu heads them =unsorted=, last. =M-x sp-org-tag-groups-list-unsorted= lists them.
- *Registry from groups:* =sp-org-tag-registry.el= now sets =sp-org-tag-groups-alist= and =sp-org-tag-groups-ungrouped= and derives =org-tag-persistent-alist= from them (=sp-org-tag-groups-to-alist=, Org's group-tag form). =sp-org-tag-add= asks for the group and inserts the tag in that element. =sp-org-tag-groups= no longer holds a copy of the data. Group names are registered tags and are in their own group.
- *ADR 0020:* records both decisions and what was implemented, including that a member named like its group is left out of the Org form.
- Docs (=.org=) and tangled =.el= edited together; tests and CHANGELOG updated.

Not run in Emacs (none in the container); tangle done by hand.

The tag chip colours in =sp-select-note= / =sp-insert-note= no longer use Notion's fixed hex pairs; they follow the active theme.

- =sp-org-tag-groups-palette= keeps its ten slot names (=default=, =gray=, ... =red=), so =sp-org-tag-groups-colors= is unchanged. Each slot now names a face (=error=, =success=, =link=, =link-visited=, =font-lock-keyword-face=, ...), a colour, or a mix =(A B WEIGHT)=; =nil= is neutral. The sp themes colour those faces from their palette, so any theme works through them.
- New =sp-org-tag-groups-palette-entry=: hue blended into the =default= background (0.22 light, 0.32 dark, as in #246), foreground nudged until contrast is at least 4.5.
- Recomputed on theme change via =sp-after-load-theme-hook=.
- A group with no colour, such as =unsorted= from #248, gets the neutral =default=. I did not touch the group list or colours, to avoid conflicts with #248.
- Doc (=.org=) and tangled =.el= edited together; CHANGELOG entry added; new =tests/sp-org-tag-groups-test.el= (5 tests, pass in Emacs 29 batch).

Not checked in a GUI: how the chips look in each theme. The face-to-slot mapping (e.g. =yellow= = =warning=, =pink= = =link-visited=) is my guess; adjust the palette if a colour looks off.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2LUVdS2HhkPxfyzVVQAEeL1][project thread]]/

Follows #200 (merged).

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
Added to =sp-reading-mode=:

- *Margin glyphs* from Rougier's =draft.org=: =#=, =##=, =###= for heading levels 1-3 and =•= for top-level bullets, in the left margin. A level 4 heading is a run-in paragraph head: =§= (=sp-reading-paragraph-glyph=) in the margin and the line break after the title hidden, so the title leads into the paragraph. Done with font-lock =display= keywords; turning the mode off removes them and unfontifies so nothing stays behind.
- *Frame resizing* (=sp-reading-frame-size=, 81x51 text columns/lines plus margins). Old size kept in a frame parameter and restored; skipped for fullscreen and non-graphical frames; nil disables.
- *Mock pagination* (=sp-reading-paginate=): =C-v=, =M-v=, =<next>=, =<prior>= turn whole pages (next page starts where the last stopped; previous goes back by the current page's screen lines). Prefix argument scrolls as usual. The header's page number follows because point moves to the top of the page. Mouse wheel unchanged.
- *Line spacing* default 1 pixel -> 0.3 of the line height.

Doc, tangled =.el= and CHANGELOG updated.

**** Tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tested
:END:
Emacs 29.3 batch: display properties on each heading level, bullets and the newline; removal and restore of all saved settings; frame parameter save/restore with =display-graphic-p= stubbed; page turning forward and back with stubbed window functions. =tools/tangle-all.el= writes the same =.el=. *Not tested:* a real GUI frame (frame resizing, real =window-end=, text-scale with margins, interplay with =org-indent= or =org-modern=).

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2FK94NRG8x7zRDHP6w2r8ca][project thread]]/

Replaces the plain rendering of heading tags in Org buffers with SVG chips from [[https://github.com/rougier/svg-tag-mode][svg-tag-mode]], driven by the existing tag groups.

- *Install*: =use-package= with Elpaca, =svg-lib= from MELPA and =svg-tag-mode= from =rougier/svg-tag-mode=.
- *Colour*: each chip uses =sp-org-tag-groups--chip-face=, so it takes the group colour from the theme-derived palette (#249); =unsorted= tags are neutral (#248). A theme change redraws the chips.
- *Emoji*: the tag's emoji is shown in front of the chip in =sp-org-tag-groups-select-emoji-face= (#247), the same as =sp-select-note=. =sp-org-svg-tags-show-emoji= turns it off.
- *How*: =svg-tag-mode= puts one display on one match, so there are three keywords: the tag name (chip), the colon before it (emoji) and the final colon (hidden). Matches outside the tags of a heading are ignored.
- *Toggle / fallback*: =M-x sp-org-svg-tags-global-mode=, default from =sp-org-svg-tags-enable=. In a terminal frame, or without SVG support, it stays off and the tags are plain text.
- *Interactions*: stays off if =org-modern-tag= is on (it is nil in =sp-org-appearance=); =org-indent= only sets a line prefix and =org-tags-column= is 0, so no alignment is needed.
- Edited the doc (=sp-org-tag-groups.org=) and re-tangled =sp-org-tag-groups.el=. That also brings in =sp-org-tag-groups--explicit-groups=, which the committed =.el= lacked (same fix as #252, so the two will merge cleanly).

Tests: 4 new ERT tests, 9/9 pass in Emacs 29.3 batch (=-L libraries/modules/funct -L libraries/modules/ui=); I also ran the real =svg-tag-mode= font-lock over a sample buffer with a stub for the image. *Not run in a graphic frame*, so how the chips look and whether the emoji sit well with the chip height has to be checked on the Mac.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Xb5LqaNLG6saSgoKaUBss1?thread=cmsg_01Xb5LqaNLG6saSgoKaUBss1JG5WS2CLneVnRb5S9eMFEo][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
- =.config/beets/beets.org=: starter literate config. It tangles two files into =.config/beets/synology/=:
  - =config.yaml=: beets config (library =/config/musiclibrary.blb=, music =/music=, plugins web, chroma, fetchart, embedart, lastgenre, scrub, info, missing, duplicates). It pulls in =secrets.yaml= with =include:=.
  - =compose.yaml=: Container Manager project for =lscr.io/linuxserver/beets:latest=, with volumes =/volume1/docker/beets:/config=, =/volume1/music:/music= and =/volume1/music/_import:/downloads=, on port 8337.
- =.config/beets/deploy-to-synology.sh=: tangles with =emacs -Q --batch= when a tangled file is missing or older than =beets.org= (or when given =-f=), then copies with =scp -O=. Settings come from =-H/-u/-p/-d= or =SYNOLOGY_HOST/USER/PORT/DEST=, with defaults =192.168.88.10=, =$USER=, =22= and =/volume1/docker/beets=. =-n= is a dry run. It copies a local =secrets.yaml= if there is one, and otherwise creates an empty one on the NAS.
- =.config/beets/.gitignore= keeps =secrets.yaml= and local beets state out of the repo.
- =README.org=: new *Homelab configuration* section that links to =beets.org= and the script.

**** Choices to check
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: choices-to-check
:END:
- The files go into =synology/= and not into =~/.config/beets/config.yaml=. That is where a beets on the laptop would look for its config, and the container paths (=/music=, =/config=) would break it.
- The =web= plugin has to stay enabled, because the image runs =beet web= as its main process and its health check waits for port 8337.
- ~PUID=1026~, ~PGID=100~, ~TZ=Etc/UTC~ and the =/downloads= folder are guesses, marked as such in =beets.org=.
- I didn't add a CHANGELOG entry, because =CHANGELOG.org= covers only the Emacs config.

**** Tested (in a Linux container, not against a real NAS)
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tested-in-a-linux-container-not-against-a-real-nas
:END:
- Tangling with Emacs =-Q --batch= writes 6 blocks, and both YAML files parse.
- The tangled =config.yaml= (with local paths) loads in beets 2.14.1 and =beet ls= works. With =secrets.yaml= missing, beets prints a warning and carries on.
- The script passes =shellcheck=. I ran it end to end against stub =ssh=/=scp= that write to a local folder: first run tangles, second run skips the tangle, a newer =beets.org= makes it tangle again, =secrets.yaml= gets copied when it exists, and bad port, relative destination, extra arguments and a missing Emacs each fail with a clear message.
- Not run: real =scp= to DSM, or the container itself.

/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2845x3ZWN18byCsCBRdx4xj][project thread]]/

New "Dynamic block templates" section in =sp-org-base= (doc and tangled =.el=).

- =sp-org-dblock-templates=: customizable alist =(LABEL . PLIST)=; the plist is what =org-create-dblock= takes (=:name= plus block parameters).
- =M-x sp-org-dblock-insert-template= (also =C-c C-x t= in Org buffers): pick a template with =completing-read=, insert it at point, update it (=sp-org-dblock-update-after-insert=, default on), leave point on the =#+BEGIN= line.
- Default template "Children of this note": =collection-query-table= with =:parent-of self :columns (:title) :sort-by :title=.
- =:parent-of self= is resolved by =sp-collec-query-resolve-parent-of= on every update to the ID of the note the block is in (=org-id-get-create=, so a note without an ID gets one). It accepts the symbol =self= and the string ="self"=, so the template needs no change in the table code.
- CHANGELOG entry under Open pull requests (to move into a feature set when merged).

Tested in Emacs 29.3 batch: 4 new ERT tests in =tests/sp-org-base-dblock-test.el= pass (they use a stub dblock, not Vulpea). =tools/check-tangle.sh= is clean for =sp-org-base.el=; the only drift it reports is =sp-search.el=, already on =main=. Not tried in the live Emacs with Vulpea, so inserting the real table in a note needs a check on the Mac. =C-c C-x t= was unbound in =org-mode-map= in stock Org; check it does not clash with your own bindings.

Hardening found while looking for the Emacs start-up hang. Neither change is shown to cause the hang.

*=sp-tab-inbox=*: both =rg= runs over =~/notes/inbox/tabs/= (the sidebar widget search and the backlink search) were unbounded and synchronous. They now use =sp-tab-inbox-rg-limits= (=--no-config --threads 2 --max-filesize 2M --max-columns 300 --max-columns-preview --max-count 20=), and titles in =sp-tab-inbox-ignored-terms= ("inbox", "home", "notes", ...) are not searched.

*=sp-dashboard=*: the macOS Focus file =~/Library/DoNotDisturb/DB/Assertions.json= is protected (Full Disk Access). Reading it and adding a kqueue watch on its folder, every 30 s while the Dashboard exists, made =tccd= log each refused attempt. The new option =sp-dashboard-read-macos-focus= (default nil) skips both. The flag file =sp-dashboard-focus-flag-file= still works.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2NidJm7Tzd128tJp4sbpQtK][project thread]]/

=sp-ai= is out of the startup list in =init.el=. Its git-sourced packages (claude-code, efrit, vulpea-mcp, monet) made Elpaca block in =elpaca-wait=, and it was the slowest module at start (about 12 to 15 s).

New command =M-x sp-ai-load= (defined in =init.el=): loads =sp-terminal= (the =eat= backend that claude-code waits for), then =sp-ai=, then runs =elpaca-process-queues= so missing packages install. It logs to =*Messages*= through =sp-require-module=.

*Consequence:* the MCP servers (mcp-server-lib, vulpea-mcp, org-mcp) are down until =sp-ai-load= runs, so Claude's MCP calls through =emacs-mcp-stdio.sh= get no answer. A headless daemon that must serve them needs to run =sp-ai-load= after start.

Docs: =sp-ai.org= and =load-order.org= say so; CHANGELOG entry added. Not run in Emacs (none in the container); parentheses of =init.el= checked by script.

Found while looking for the Emacs start-up hang. In a batch profile of a copy of the real vault and =vulpea.db=, 56% of the CPU over 145 s was =vulpea-select-cache-prewarm-step=, which reads every row of the database into a candidate cache for =vulpea-find= and =vulpea-insert= as soon as =vulpea-db-autosync-mode= starts (500-note chunks on the main thread; =vulpea-select.el= lines 547 and 1036 to 1092).

- =(setq vulpea-select-cache-prewarm nil)= in the vulpea base settings. The cache is then built at the first =vulpea-find= or =vulpea-insert=, which pauses once.
- New option =sp-vulpea-autosync-delay= (30 idle seconds, was a fixed 5) for starting autosync.

Org doc edited first, =.el= to match; CHANGELOG entry added. Not run in Emacs (none in the container). The hang is not confirmed fixed: a native sample of the live Emacs also showed =org-element= parsing from the autosync indexing itself.

- =migrate.sh=: =preflight=, =backup=, =restructure= (clone of the yadm repo, history kept, =git mv= on branch =stow-layout=), =dryrun=, =cutover=, =verify=, =retire=, =rollback=. Files Stow replaces are moved into a backup folder, never deleted.
- =README.md=: the guide (dry run, backup, untracking yadm, =~/.git= gitfile and =GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=, Magit/Forge, =--adopt= caveats, folding, Stow's default ignore of =README.*=/=.gitignore=).

:PROPERTIES:

Design note =docs/architecture/global-keymap-namespaces.org=, modelled on Lambda Emacs' =lem-setup-keybindings.el=. No code or key changes.

- Audit of =sp-keys= and every other binding in =libraries/modules/=: four global collisions (=C-c s l=, =C-c s r=, =C-c m=, =<f6>=), a three-way one on =C-c f=, ten local shadows of global keys (Python and Org mostly), =C-x C-SPC= hiding =pop-global-mark=, and eleven commands in the leader tree with no definition in the repo.
- Caveats: leader key options, load order and Elpaca timing of =:bind=, terminal and macOS key limits, which-key labels, mode-local overrides, migration shims, and a three-layer test.
- Design: one =defvar-keymap= per feature module, mounted by =sp-keys= from one registry table; five steps, the first changing no key.
- README row and CHANGELOG line added.

Not run in Emacs (none in the container). Statements about Emacs defaults are marked "(memory)" in the doc and need one check in a real Emacs.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2FEnkbKDW2SF6o1VMULYvEt][project thread]]/

New module =sp-litnotes-meta= (doc: =docs/tangles/academic/sp-litnotes-meta.org=). After =citar-create-note= it fills the first section of the note from the BibTeX entry:

- =pub-author=: one link per author (=author=, else =editor=). Matched by name against existing notes in the Vulpea db (a =person= note wins); if none exists, a new =person= note with an ID is written and linked.
- =pub-title=, =pub-year= (year, else =date=, else the crossref's year).
- =bib-parent=: link to the litnote of the =crossref=d entry, only if that note exists (otherwise left out, with a message).
- =bib-project=: minibuffer picker over notes tagged =project=, default the thesis.

Existing values are never changed. =M-x sp-litnotes-meta-fill= does the same for an existing note; =sp-litnotes-meta-auto= turns the advice off.

Tests: =tests/sp-litnotes-meta-test.el= (6 pass in Emacs 29, Vulpea stubbed). Not run on the real vault or with real =citar-vulpea=: the note file must exist on disk right after =citar-create-note= for the advice to find it.

/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2FEnkbKDW2SF6o1VMULYvEt][project thread]]/

Stacked on #281 (which is stacked on #280); retarget after those merge.

- *Matching:* =sp-author-notes--title-key= folds accents (=sp-author-notes-fold-diacritics=: ø ł ß æ œ đ, and everything that decomposes, so ă â î ș ț and the cedilla ş ţ), so =Søren=/=Soren Kierkegaard= find the same note, in =sp-author-notes=, =sp-author-notes-bibtex= and =sp-litnotes-meta=.
- *BibTeX escapes:* =S{\o}ren=, =Bulat{\u a}=, =\c{S}tefan=, =\"o=, =\'{\i}= ... are decoded to Unicode (=sp-author-notes-latex-to-unicode=), and the cedilla ş/ţ are written as the Romanian comma-below ș/ț. Applied to names and to =pub-title=.
- *File names:* new notes get an ASCII slug (=sp-org-slugify= folds accents); the title keeps the accents.
- *Duplicates:* several =person= notes that spell a name alike are named in the preview; apply asks which to use (=sp-author-notes-duplicate-function=, default: the spelling with the most accents). =M-x sp-author-notes-normalize-duplicates= asks per group which note to keep and, after one question, points the author and editor links of the litnotes at it (with backups). The other notes are listed, not merged or deleted.

Tests: =sp-author-notes-test.el= 24/24 (new: folding and LaTeX decoding, accent-insensitive link, duplicate spellings, normalize), bibtex 7/7, litnotes-meta 7/7. Not run on the real vault.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW21kRXq9R8f9BL3eSYVrQpsh][project thread]]/

Applies the first part of =docs/architecture/global-keymap-namespaces.org= so it can be tried, and aligns the modifier keys across macOS, Linux and Windows.

*Leader key: =C-;=.* Not =C-z=, =C-x=, =C-c= or =C-v= (clipboard and undo keys), not =Ctrl+Space= or =Cmd+Space= (OS and Alfred). =sp-spelling= unbinds =C-;= in =flyspell-mode-map=.

*What to try after merging (GUI):*

- =C-;= then =b=, =g=, =f=, =w=: the existing groups, now under =C-;= (with which-key).
- =C-; a= (agenda, capture, focus HUD), =C-; S= (easysession), =C-; z= (spelling: =p= previous, =n= next, =.= at point), =C-; f d= (dirvish), =C-; w M= (jump to minibuffer), =C-; w D= (redraw), =C-; b P= (=pop-global-mark=).
- =C-x C-SPC= prints where the leader moved and waits for the next key.
- Old =C-c s s/L/d/R= and =C-c e b b= still work and print where they moved to.
- =M-x sp-keys-audit= lists leader keys with no command and the shims still alive.
- Mac: =Cmd+C/X/V/Z= and =Cmd+Shift+Z= copy, cut, paste, undo and redo; =M-x= is Option+X.
- Mac window manager: hold Caps Lock plus =h/j/k/l=, =1=-=9=, =a b d e m t w=, =Tab=, =/=, =,= (the old =alt-*= keys of AeroSpace); Caps Lock + =Shift+;= enters service mode.
- Linux (i3, sway): Caps Lock is =$mod=; dmenu is =$mod+d=.

*Changes:*

- =sp-prefix= is =C-;=.
- Collisions removed: =C-c s l/r= (consult only), =C-c m= (supersonic only), =<f6>= (projectile only), =C-c f= (Org footnotes only; =org-focus-hud= and =dirvish= lose their =:bind=, keep =:commands=).
- Shims live in =sp-keys-moved= until removed.
- Removed: Python configuration (=sp-python=, =ein=) and Evil (last commit with it: 4164bae).
- Clipboard and undo (=sp-macos=, =sp-text-manipulation=): on the Mac, Command is Super and Option is Meta, =s-c/s-x/s-v/s-z/s-Z= are plain bindings and CUA is off. On Linux and Windows CUA stays for =C-c=/=C-x= with a region only; =C-v= is =yank=, =C-z= is =undo=, =C-S-z= is =undo-redo=. The two =C-z= unbinds moved to =sp-text-manipulation=.
- Window managers (non-Emacs): =aerospace.toml= no longer binds =alt-*= in main mode; Hammerspoon (=aerospace-keys.lua=) turns Caps Lock into F18 and runs the same =aerospace= commands. i3 and sway use Caps Lock as =$mod= (=caps:super=) and no longer bind Alt; i3's dmenu moved from Alt+Space to =$mod+d=. Windows has no window manager here.
- Design doc: new sections "Keys freed by CUA", "Replacing CUA" and "Same keys on macOS, Linux and Windows" (linked to ADR 0019, ADR 0023, =sp-syslinux=, =sp-syswin=, =sp-macos=, =sp-text-manipulation=, =sp-globals=).
- Docs and =.el= edited together; the doc blocks and the changed =.el= files match when compared ignoring whitespace.

*Not done (later PRs):* one =defvar-keymap= per module and the registry, moving the =C-c w= / =C-c k= / =C-c d= keys, an Org local leader, the batch test, the 11 undefined leader commands.

Not run in Emacs, AeroSpace, Hammerspoon, i3 or sway (none in the container). Check the =aerospace= path in =aerospace-keys.lua= and whether =s-b=/=s-i= reach Emacs on Linux.

Fixes =browse-url-url-at-point: Wrong type argument: buffer-or-string-p, (link ...)= when opening a URL in an Org file.

- =browse-url-url-at-point= calls =(thing-at-point 'url t)=, which strips text properties from whatever the provider returns. A list (a parsed =link= element) there gives exactly this =buffer-or-string-p= error.
- Org buffers now use =sp-org-url-at-point= as the =url= provider. It always returns a string or nil.
- A Markdown link pasted inside a plain link (~https://[www.youtube.com/watch?v=x](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x)~) opens the inner address.
- Doc section, CHANGELOG line and =tests/sp-org-url-test.el= added.

*Caveat:* I did not find in this repository the code that returns the link object, so the cause is inferred from the error and the =thingatpt= source. The fix guards the answer for Org buffers. If it still fails, =M-x toggle-debug-on-error= and send the backtrace.

Not run in Emacs (none in the container).

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2WvunRxqLgBGFzjJ85aXPfJ][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
CUA is gone on every system, and the Emacs defaults for the same jobs are unbound, so there is one layer of keys.

- *Mac (Command = Super):* =s-c= copy, =s-x= cut, =s-v= paste, =s-z= undo, =s-Z= and =S-s-z= redo (the latter is the event Emacs usually gets for Command+Shift+Z).
- *Linux and Windows (Ctrl):* =C-S-c= copy, =C-S-x= cut, =C-v= paste, =C-z= undo, =C-S-z= redo.
- *Unbound everywhere:* =C-y=, =C-w=, =M-w=, =C-_=, =C-/=, =C-?=, =C-M-_=, =C-x u=.
- =sp-text-manipulation.org= documents it, including a caveats list for unbinding =C-w=/=M-w=/=C-y=. =sp-keys.org= no longer says CUA is on. The =.el= is the tangled copy.

**** Readings I chose
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: readings-i-chose
:END:
- Without CUA, plain =C-c= and =C-x= must stay prefixes, so copy and cut on Linux/Windows use the Shift variants. Say if you would rather have something else.
- Redo is the built-in =undo-redo=, not undo-tree.
- No CHANGELOG edit (nightly routine owns it).

Not run in Emacs (none in the container); please try on the Mac and on Linux/Windows.

* PR #296: 🔧 Super prefix swap on Linux/Windows; i3 and sway stop using Super
:PROPERTIES:
:PR_NUMBER: 296
:URL: https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/pull/296
:STATE: merged
:AUTHOR: siainbuletin
:END:
- Link :: [[https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/pull/296][https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/pull/296]]
- State :: merged
- Author :: @siainbuletin
- Opened :: 2026-11-05 19:37
- Merged :: 2026-11-06 11:22
- Branch :: =296-super-prefix-swap= → =main=
- Merge commit :: [[https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/commit/89b63d63aaf84e952407e4beda7bc1874faddf12][89b63d63aa]]
- Labels :: new-feature, simplifying, needs-further-testing

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2WvunRxqLgBGFzjJ85aXPfJ][project thread]]/

Follow-up to #294.

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
*Emacs (Linux/Windows, =sp-text-manipulation=)*

- =s-c= is translated to =C-c= and =s-x= to =C-x= (=key-translation-map=), so Super carries the prefixes: =s-c C-c= = =C-c C-c=, =s-x C-f= = =C-x C-f=.
- A typed =C-c= / =C-x= that starts a key sequence becomes copy / cut (private events =<sp-copy>=, =<sp-cut>=). Inside a sequence they keep their stock meaning. This replaces the =C-S-c= / =C-S-x= from #294.
- On Windows =w32-lwindow-modifier= / =w32-rwindow-modifier= are =super=.
- Mac is unchanged.

*i3 and sway (options for freeing Super)*

- Chosen: Caps Lock becomes the Level 3 shift (=lv3:caps_switch=, Mod5) and =$mod= is =Mod5=. Nothing binds Mod4 any more, so the Windows key reaches Emacs. Same physical layer key as AeroSpace on the Mac.
- Other options, not taken: =caps:hyper= (Hyper often shares Mod4 in X, so it may not free Super); Alt as =$mod= (clashes with Meta, which Sia reserved for Emacs); Ctrl+Alt chords (awkward, and Ctrl+Alt is used by terminals/Emacs).
- Caveat of the choice: Caps+letter yields AltGr-level characters on layouts that have them, but the WM grabs bound combinations first.

*Docs*

- =sp-keys.org=: new section "Replaced prefixes and chords" with a table of stock key vs Mac vs Linux/Windows, and how to look up a key (=C-h k=, =C-h w=).
- Top-level =README.org=: note that most keys are bound differently, pointing to that table.
- =sp-text-manipulation.org= and =global-keymap-namespaces.org= updated, with the caveats (Windows takes =Win+C= / =Win+X=; needs a remap).

**** Not run
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-run
:END:
No Emacs, i3 or sway in the container. The "starts a sequence" check uses =this-command-keys-vector= from memory; try =C-h k s-c C-c=, =C-h k C-c=, =C-c C-c= in Org, and =lv3:caps_switch= + =$mod= in i3/sway. No CHANGELOG edit (nightly routine owns it).

/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2WvunRxqLgBGFzjJ85aXPfJ][project thread]]/

**** Why
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: why
:END:
After pointing Hammerspoon at =~/.config/hammerspoon=, it failed with =init.lua:3: attempt to index a boolean value (global 'stackline')=. =require "stackline"= finds the empty top-level =stackline.lua= (it returns =true=), so =stackline:init()= errors, and the AeroSpace keys on the last line never load. That is why Caps Lock and Option did nothing for AeroSpace.

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
- =init.lua= requires =aerospace-keys= first.
- stackline is loaded inside =pcall=; a failure is printed to the Console (=stackline not loaded: ...=) and no longer stops anything.

**** Not fixed
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-fixed
:END:
stackline itself stays broken: =stackline.lua= is empty and =lib/= is called =stackline-lib/= in this folder, so it does not match the layout stackline expects. Say if you want it repaired or removed.

Not run (no Hammerspoon in the container). After merging and =git pull= in =~/dotfiles=, reload the config and hold Caps Lock + =l=.

New =aerospace/.config/aerospace/aerospace.org=, a literate source for =aerospace.toml= (bullet lists, no long paragraphs).

- Tangles to =aerospace.toml= next to it; the blocks reproduce the current file exactly (compared line by line ignoring blank lines: 78 = 78), so =aerospace.toml= is not touched.
- Section "Why Hammerspoon runs the keys":
  - AeroSpace binds only =cmd=, =alt=, =ctrl=, =shift= chords, and Emacs uses all of them (Command = Super, Option = Meta, Ctrl).
  - So Caps Lock becomes F18 (=hidutil=), Hammerspoon holds it as a layer and runs the =aerospace= commands.
  - Where the code and its settings live, the key list, the one-off =MJConfigFile= setting, and the costs (Hammerspoon must run, Caps Lock stops toggling capitals, how to go back).
- Every setting of the TOML is explained under its block.

**** Not run
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-run
:END:
No Emacs in the container, so I did not tangle with Org; the check above extracts the blocks myself. Org may add blank lines between blocks, which TOML ignores. No CHANGELOG edit (nightly routine owns it).

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2WvunRxqLgBGFzjJ85aXPfJ][project thread]]/

**** Symptom
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: symptom
:END:
Caps Lock + number (focus, workspaces) works, but Caps Lock + Shift combos (move window, move to workspace) do nothing, and with a text box focused they type capitals.

**** Likely cause
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: likely-cause
:END:
The layer key (F18, from Caps Lock) is bound with =hs.hotkey.bind({}, "f18", ...)=. A hotkey only matches the modifiers it is bound with, so F18 pressed while Shift is already held is not that hotkey: the layer never opens, and Shift+letter types a capital. Pressing Caps Lock first and Shift second would already have worked, so this only breaks when Shift goes down first (or at the same time).

**** Change
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: change
:END:
- =aerospace-keys.lua=: the layer key is bound twice, with no modifiers and with =shift=, both entering and leaving the same layer.
- =aerospace.org=: one line saying the layer opens in either order.

**** Not run, and what to check
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-run-and-what-to-check
:END:
No Mac or Hammerspoon here, so this is a diagnosis from the code, not a reproduced bug. After =git pull= and a Hammerspoon reload, try both orders: hold Caps, then Shift+=h= (move left); and hold Shift, then Caps, then =h=. If Shift first still types capitals, the key events arrive another way and I will switch the layer to an event tap that tracks F18 itself. No CHANGELOG edit (nightly routine owns it).

** Description
/Requested by *Sia*/

Caps Lock + number worked, but Caps Lock + Shift + key (move window / move to workspace) did not, and typed capital letters in a text field.

Cause: the layer key (Caps Lock remapped to F18) was an =hs.hotkey= bound with no modifiers. Hammerspoon matches those exactly, so with Shift already down F18 did not match, passed through to the app, and the Shift+key then typed a capital letter.

Fix (=hammerspoon/.config/hammerspoon/aerospace-keys.lua=): the layer is now an =hs.eventtap= that tracks F18 down/up whatever modifiers are held, swallows it, and looks the next key up with or without Shift (Cmd/Alt/Ctrl pass through). The same bindings are kept.

Only checked with =luac -p=; Hammerspoon is on your machine. To test after merging: =git -C ~/dotfiles pull=, Hammerspoon → Reload Config, then try Caps + Shift + h/l and Caps + Shift + 1, pressing Shift first and Caps first. If Shift-then-Caps still types capitals, the F18 remap itself is not applying: =hidutil property --get UserKeyMapping= should list it.

No CHANGELOG edit (nightly routine owns it).

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2WvunRxqLgBGFzjJ85aXPfJ][project thread]]/

**** Symptom
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: symptom
:END:
Caps+Shift+; enters AeroSpace's service mode, but there is no way back out.

**** Likely cause
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: likely-cause
:END:
The service-mode =esc= binding was =['reload-config', 'mode main']=. AeroSpace runs the commands of a binding in order and stops at the first one that fails, so if =reload-config= fails (or reports an error), =mode main= never runs and the mode is stuck. This is a diagnosis from the config, not a reproduced bug (no Mac here).

**** Changes
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: changes
:END:
- =aerospace.toml=: ~esc = ['mode main', 'reload-config']~ (leave first, then reload).
- =aerospace-keys.lua=: Caps Lock + Esc runs =aerospace mode main=, so there is a way out even when AeroSpace does not receive Esc. It uses the existing =bind= helper, so it works with the current hotkey layer and with the event-tap version in #310.
- =aerospace.org=: kept in sync (the TOML block, the =esc= note, the key list).

**** To check
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: to-check
:END:
After =git pull=, a Hammerspoon reload and =aerospace reload-config=: enter service mode with Caps+Shift+;, then try =Esc=, then again and try Caps+Esc. From Terminal, =aerospace mode main= always works. If neither exits, the Hammerspoon Console or =aerospace reload-config= output will show the real error; send it to me.

No CHANGELOG edit (nightly routine owns it).

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2Jrn2KurzT78udU8WM5CSmZ][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
Replaces the Denote commands I liked, in =sp-notes=:

- =sp-notes-create= (=SPC n c=, like =denote-create-note=): asks for a title and registered tags, writes the note with =:ID:= and =:CREATED:=, visits it. With tags it is written straight into its filing folder (same rules as the tag filing); without tags it stays at the top of the root, as the filing mode leaves it.
- =sp-notes-open= (=SPC n o=, like =denote-open=): =completing-read= over every org file in all subfolders of the notes root. Each candidate is the file name with creation date, tags and title beside it, newest first. Dot folders, =ltximg/=, =attach/= and =data/= are not listed (=sp-notes-open-exclude-regexp=); inbox, area, log and workbook are.
- =:CREATED:= on new notes: added in =sp-org--write-note= (new optional DIR arg and =sp-org-created-stamp=), so person and literature notes made through it get it too.

**** Ambiguity: where =:CREATED:= goes
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: ambiguity-where-created-goes
:END:
- Read as: the file-level property drawer beside =:ID:=, format =[2026-11-07 20:15]= (inactive timestamp, no weekday). It is what =sp-quick-capture=, =vulpea-para= and =sp-org-issues= already write.
- Date shown by =sp-notes-open=: =:CREATED:=, else the id in the file name, else the modification time, so old notes without it still sort.
- Not changed: notes made by =vulpea-create= (=vulpea-find=, inbox tab). Say if you want =vulpea-create-default-function= to add it too.
- ADR 0025 (=-dryrun=/=-convert=) does not apply: these commands do not preview or convert anything.

**** Testing
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: testing
:END:
- 15 ERT tests pass in batch Emacs 29.3 (4 new: stamp format, create writes =:CREATED:= and files by tag, open info/candidates/annotation, date from file name); the author-notes and litnotes-meta tests still pass. Docs tangle to the committed =.el=.
- /untested/ on the Mac, in the real vault, with real vulpea or in the GUI (vertico look of the picker annotations).

**** What was wrong
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what-was-wrong
:END:
- Stacking is =join-with=, which only existed in AeroSpace's service mode as plain =shift-h/j/k/l=.
- After =Caps+Shift+;=, Caps Lock is usually still held, so Hammerspoon's layer takes =Shift+h/j/k/l= as /move window/ first. Both tools then compete for the same chord, so joining only works sometimes (when Caps is released first).

**** Fix
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: fix
:END:
- =Caps+Ctrl+h/j/k/l= runs =aerospace join-with <dir>= directly on the layer, with no service mode.
- The layer key is also bound with Ctrl, so Ctrl-then-Caps works.
- =aerospace.org= documents the new keys. The service-mode keys are unchanged.

**** Testing (not run: no Mac in the container)
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: testing-not-run-no-mac-in-the-container
:END:
- Reload Hammerspoon, open two tiled windows side by side, press =Caps+Ctrl+l=/=h=: they should join into one container (then =Caps+,= for accordion).

:PROPERTIES:

:STATE: merged

- Link :: [[https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/pull/324][https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/pull/324]]
- State :: merged
- Author :: @siainbuletin
- Opened :: 2026-11-07 23:09
- Merged :: 2026-11-08 00:18
- Branch :: =claude/devonthink-reading-db= → =main=
- Merge commit :: [[https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/commit/3d7f2e3b5ba409684ca13c649ba10727e2c294d3][3d7f2e3b5b]]
- Labels :: new-feature, needs-further-testing

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Xb5LqaNLG6saSgoKaUBss1?thread=cmsg_01Xb5LqaNLG6saSgoKaUBss1U4FeuYXuDT9CPaA3fvY258][project thread]]/

**** Why
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: why
:END:
The =literature= database (about 65 GB) is too big for the iPad and for the NAS's WebDAV sync store, which has about 20 GB on the SSD. So =literature= stays on the Mac, searchable from DEVONthink and Emacs, and a small =reading= database syncs instead. A rule fills it, so you don't sort anything by hand.

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
=tools/devonthink-reading.py= has two actions. Both are dry runs unless you pass =--apply=.

- =create= makes =~/Databases/reading.dtBase2= with one group per selected =.bib= file. If the file exists but is closed, it opens it instead.
- =send= moves a PDF into =reading= when its litnote's =read-status= is one of the chosen values (default =to-be-read=) and its citekey is in one of the chosen =.bib= files (default: all of them). It refuses to go over the budget (default 20 GB). With =--return=, it moves records that no longer match back to their old group, which it remembers in =~/.local/state/devonthink-reading/origins.json=.
- You can change the rule as you go: =--status= and =--bib= (both repeatable), or =~/.config/devonthink-reading/config.json=. =--json= prints the plan as JSON for a later Emacs command.
- The rule matches on the citekey: =ROAM_REFS= or =#+reference:= in the litnote, the =.bib= entry key, and the PDF file name =KEY.pdf=.
- The script and its tests are literate: they tangle from =docs/tangles/academic/devonthink-reading.org=, which also has the usage, the settings, how the rule decides, and what is untested. Edit the =.org= and tangle it (=C-c C-v t=); =tools/tangle-all.el= and the =tangle= CI check only cover =sp-*.org= module docs, so they don't check this one.
- Also summarised in =docs/architecture/devonthink-emacs-integration.org=, section "The =reading= database".

**** Tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tested
:END:
- =python3 -m unittest tests/test_devonthink_reading.py=: 11 tests pass. They cover parsing, the rule, the budget, =--return=, dry run against =--apply=, and remembering where each record came from, with DEVONthink faked.
- *Not run on the Mac.* The DEVONthink calls are untested, and so is the question of whether moving an indexed record between databases leaves its PDF in =~/Documents/literature/=. Try =create=, then =send --apply --limit 1=, and check the record and the file.

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
- New module =sp-collection-query-tables-book= (the =sp-collection-query-tables= family already exists, so this is a new part of it, not a new family): a table of the sections of a note tagged =book= or =collection=, sorted by page.
  - Sections are notes whose =bib-parent= links to the book. It is an ordinary query spec (=:parent-of= + =:parent-prop "bib-parent"= + =:sort-by :page=), so every renderer, saved views and dynamic blocks work with it.
  - =C-c w b= / =M-x sp-collec-query-book-open= opens it for the note at point (the book, or one of its sections); elsewhere it asks for a book.
- Two new columns in the core: =:pages= (text of =pub-pages=) and =:page= (its first number, used for sorting). Sections with no number (e.g. roman numerals) sort last.
- New =vulpea-ui= widget "Book position" (=sp-collection-query-tables-book-widget=, order 345): the book as a button, "Section N of M", previous/next buttons, and all sections in page order with the current one marked. It uses the same data function as the table (=sp-collec-query-book-position=). Registered like the Link inbox widgets, and loaded after =vulpea-ui=.
- Literate doc =sp-collection-query-tables.org= updated in bullets; the =.el= files tangled from it.

**** Page property: =pub-pages=
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: page-property-pub-pages
:END:
I used the existing =pub-pages= meta key. The schemas in =sp-vulpea-schemas= already define it for =booksection=, =incollection= and =journalarticle=, so no new key is needed. Its value is text (=12-34=, =pp. 12-34=) and the table sorts on the first number in it. Say so if you would rather have a separate numeric key.

**** Tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tested
:END:
- 6 ERT tests in Emacs 29.3 batch (=tests/sp-collection-query-tables-book-test.el=) with Vulpea stubbed: first-page parsing, the new columns, page order, root detection, position/previous/next, the spec.
- *Not run:* the widget (needs =vui=/=vulpea-ui= and a sidebar), the table renderers, or anything against the real vault. The widget's layout and its order relative to the other widgets are worth a look: open a chapter litnote, =C-x t s=.

Follows #329.

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
- *Views as dblock templates:* a =collection-query-table= block takes =:view "name"=. Other keys in the block override the view's (e.g. =:parent-of=).
  - =sp-collec-query-insert-view-dblock= asks for a view and inserts such a block.
  - =sp-collec-query-view-save-from-dblock= registers a new view from the block at point, with no file editing. The menu's =S= already did the same for a spec. Both write the existing views file (=sp-collec-query-views-file=).
- *Built-in views* (=sp-collec-query-views-defaults=, in the repo; a saved view with the same name wins):
  - =book-sections=: notes linking to this note by =bib-parent=, by page, with a =Check= column.
  - =collection-articles=: same, plus =pub-year=, for a =collection=.
  - =bib-parent-mismatches=: every note in the vault that has a warning.
- *Flagging:* new =:check= column (=sp-collec-query-check=) and =:flagged t= spec key. Rules in =sp-collec-query-check-rules=: a =booksection= needs a =book= parent, an =incollection= a =collection= parent, and a note whose parent is a =book= (or =collection=) must be tagged =booksection= (or =incollection=).

**** Notes
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: notes
:END:
- The views file lives under =sp-etc-dir= (not in the repo) as before. To commit your own templates, copy them into =sp-collec-query-views-defaults= or point =sp-collec-query-views-file= into the repo.
- =book-sections= and =collection-articles= differ only in their columns, because the parent's tag decides the check.
- The menu does not expose =:flagged= yet.

**** Tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tested
:END:

/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2MrY1q4iHAjtGKB9ZK1nKzV][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
- =sp-litnotes-meta-fill= (and the =citar-create-note= advice) also handles three lines:
  - =read-status=: set to =02-preparing= without asking.
  - =relevance-factor= and =read-priority=: prompted, only =01= to =05= accepted, =01= is the most relevant / read first. Empty answer skips.
- The =base-text= schema (in =sp-vulpea.org=, tangled to =sp-vulpea-schemas.el=) requires all three, as strings with =:one-of=:
  - =read-status=: =01-current=, =02-preparing=, =03-review=, =04-paused=, =05-done=.
  - =relevance-factor=, =read-priority=: =01= to =05=.
- =M-x sp-litnotes-meta-status-report=: lists every litnote (status, priority, relevance, title) with counts per status in the header line; statuses outside the list show as a warning.
  - =m=/=u= mark, =M= marks all of one status, =U= clears, =s= changes the status of the marked notes (or the note at point), =g= rescans, =RET= opens.
- =M-x sp-litnotes-meta-backfill-children=: in a book or collection litnote, finds BibTeX entries whose =crossref= is its key and that have no note, lets you pick them (empty = all), and makes each through =citar-create-note= (so =bib-parent= links this note).
  - =bib-project= is copied from the parent; =relevance-factor= and =read-priority= are asked once for the batch.
- The draft query in =sp-vulpea-org-ql= now treats =01=/=02= as relevant (it used ~>= 4~ before the scale was flipped).

**** Notes
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: notes
:END:
- =sp-litnotes-meta-fill= never overwrites existing values; only the report's =s= changes a status.
- Not run on the real vault: existing notes with other statuses (e.g. =to-be-read=) show as warnings in the report until changed. Backfill relies on =citar-create-note= writing the file synchronously (same open risk as #280).
- Tests: =sp-litnotes-meta-test.el= 10/10 in Emacs 29 with stubbed Vulpea and citar; =tools/check-tangle.sh= passes for the changed docs. The report UI was not exercised interactively.
- No CHANGELOG edits.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2DcBZNbSudGuxYj6Xtk3QZf][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
=sp-litnotes-titles-dryrun= and =-convert= can now take the authors, year and title from the BibTeX entry of each note's citekey, so every litnote title can be brought to the =Last (Year) Title= standard.

- =C-u M-x sp-litnotes-titles-dryrun=: BibTeX fills what the note lacks (=missing=).
- =C-u C-u M-x sp-litnotes-titles-dryrun=: BibTeX wins over the meta lines (=always=).
- =sp-litnotes-titles-bibtex= sets the mode without a prefix argument (default nil, so nothing changes unless asked).
- The dry run still writes nothing. The report shows the proposed titles, marks values taken from BibTeX (=from BibTeX: authors, year=), and lists notes whose citekey has no entry. =convert= is unchanged otherwise (one confirmation, backups).

**** How
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: how
:END:
- Reuses =sp-litnotes-meta--field=/=--year= (braces, LaTeX accents to Unicode, year from =date= or =crossref=) and =sp-author-notes-bibtex--files=.
- New =sp-litnotes-meta-build-index=: the =.bib= files are read once per run (in a first background slice) into =sp-litnotes-meta--index=; =sp-litnotes-meta--entry= uses it when set. Without it, behaviour is as before.
- Source edited in =sp-org-lint.org= and =sp-litnotes-meta.org= and tangled. Five new ERT tests; =sp-litnotes-titles= and =sp-litnotes-meta= tests all pass on Emacs 29.3 (20/20). Not run on the real vault.

**** Ambiguities I resolved
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: ambiguities-i-resolved
:END:
- =sp-bibtex-dir= no longer exists (merged into =sp-bibliography-dir=), so the files come from the usual registered list.
- Names come from the =author= field only, never =editor=. =and others= is dropped, a name wholly in braces is one name, and last names are used as written (so no accent-insensitive matching is needed for titles).
- In =missing= mode an ambiguous =pub-author= also counts as lacking.
- Citekeys must match the entry exactly; the first key with an entry wins.
- Values typed in during =convert= win over BibTeX. Meta lines are not written; =sp-litnotes-meta-fill= does that.
- No CHANGELOG edit (nightly tidy). Branch is the session's designated =claude/project-thread-g1foaj=, not a number-prefixed name, since the number was unknown before opening.

Follows #330.

**** The load error
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: the-load-error
:END:
=Cannot open load file ... sp-collection-query-tables-book= is not a code bug: =sp-collection-query-tables-book.el= (and the =-book-widget= file) are in =main=, but =~/.config/emacs-modular= is a tree of Stow links, and a file added by a pull has no link until you re-stow. Fix on your side, once after pulling:

#+begin_example
cd ~/dotfiles && stow -R emacs-modular
#+end_example

(this is in =stow-migration/README.org=). No code change is needed for it; the doc now says so.

**** What this PR changes: where saved views live
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what-this-pr-changes-where-saved-views-live
:END:
- =sp-collec-query-views-file= now defaults to =views/sp-collection-query-tables-views.el= *inside the configuration*, and that file is tracked in the repo (empty at first). After =stow -R emacs-modular= it is a link into =~/dotfiles=, so a view saved from the menu (=S=) or with =sp-collec-query-view-save-from-dblock= shows up in =git status= there, ready to commit. Nothing has to be copied or moved by hand.
- The older locations (below =sp-etc-dir=, and directly in the config) are still read until the new file holds a view; the next save writes the new file, carrying those views over.
- Built-in views stay in the code (=sp-collec-query-views-defaults=).

**** Tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tested
:END:
- 6 template tests (new: empty tracked file falls back to the older file, and a save carries its views over) and 7 book tests pass in Emacs 29.3 batch.
- *Not run:* writing through the Stow link on your Mac (it relies on =write-region= following the link), or the interactive commands.

No CHANGELOG edit, per the nightly-tidy rule.

Follow-up to #335 (backfill all children).

**** Problem
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: problem
:END:
Notes made by =sp-litnotes-meta-backfill-all-children= came out with =#+title: Notes on <author>, <title>= and a =#+print_bibliography:= line. Both come from citar's own file-note template (=sp-citar-note=, "Notes on ..."), not from =citar-vulpea=, which only makes a title from =citar-vulpea-note-title-template=. So the backfill was using citar's file source.

=#+print_bibliography:= is the Org-cite marker that prints the bibliography of the works cited in that note. A litnote cites nothing, so it is not needed.

**** What changes
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what-changes
:END:
- The backfill makes each note with the =citar-vulpea= notes source when it is registered, whatever =citar-notes-source= is.
- Each new note is tidied afterwards: a =Notes on ...= title is replaced and =#+print_bibliography:= lines are removed. A title that does not start with "Notes on" is left alone.
- New option =sp-litnotes-meta-new-title=: =title= (default, the BibTeX title alone, as asked) or =standard= ("Last (Year) Title", what =sp-litnotes-titles-convert= writes).
- Literate doc updated; one new ERT test.

**** Testing
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: testing
:END:
- =sp-litnotes-meta= ERT tests pass (14/14, Emacs 29.3, stubbed citar and Vulpea); =tools/check-tangle.sh= passes.
- Not run with the real citar-vulpea on the real vault. The cause (citar's file source being used) is inferred from the "Notes on" title and the citar-vulpea source code; the tidy step fixes the result either way.

** Description
Adds =gh-pr-pdf=, a command that turns the pull requests of a GitHub repository (and optionally its Discussions) into searchable org files and one paginated PDF, so a codebase's history can be studied as plain text.

#+begin_example
gh-pr-pdf siainbuletin/dotfiles
#+end_example

**** Changes
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: changes
:END:
- New Stow package =gh-pr-pdf/=: the script at =gh-pr-pdf/.local/bin/gh-pr-pdf= (links to =~/.local/bin/gh-pr-pdf=) and =gh-pr-pdf/README.org= (usage, needs, safety, "Not run"; Stow's default ignore list skips the README).
- The script wraps =github-backup= for the raw JSON (description, conversation, reviews, inline review comments, commits), writes =org/pr-NNNNN.org= per pull request in number order plus =org/all.org=, then =pandoc -t typst= and =typst compile= make the PDF.
  - Each org file has a property drawer (=:PR_NUMBER:=, =:STATE:=, =:AUTHOR:=, =:URL:=) for org-ql, and every commit is a link to =github.com/OWNER/REPO/commit/<sha>=.
  - Options: =--discussions=, =--skip-fetch=, =--no-pdf=, =--per-pdf N=, =--reverse=, =--private=, =-o DIR=.
  - Pull request text comes from strangers, so raw HTML is dropped, =pandoc= runs with =--sandbox=, and lines starting with an org directive (=#+INCLUDE:= and so on) become literal text. Checked with an injected =#+INCLUDE: "/etc/passwd"=.
- =stow-migration/packages.tsv=: one row (=gh-pr-pdf    all .local/bin/gh-pr-pdf=) so the package is in the list =migrate.sh= derives for each machine. It matches no file in =$HOME=, so it should not change what the migration moves.

**** Not run
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-run
:END:
Written in a container without Typst or network access to GitHub's API. Run on made-up JSON: the org and Typst-source output, including headings inside bodies, empty bodies, numeric ordering, =--per-pdf= and the Discussions renderer. Not run:

- =typst compile=: the PDF itself has not been seen. Try =gh-pr-pdf siainbuletin/dotfiles= and open the PDF; without =typst= it stops after writing the =.typ= file and says so.
- =github-backup= on a real repository. The JSON key names the script reads (=comment_regular_data=, =comment_data=, =review_data=, =commit_data=) are from memory. If a pull request reports commits but no commit list is found, the script warns and prints the keys it saw; the fix is the key names in =render_pr=.
- The Discussions fetch (=gh api graphql=), which reads up to 100 comments and 50 replies per discussion and warns on more.
- =stow gh-pr-pdf= (no Stow in the container): expect =~/.local/bin/gh-pr-pdf= as a symlink into =~/dotfiles/gh-pr-pdf/.local/bin/=.

No CHANGELOG edit, per the nightly-tidy rule.

:PROPERTIES:

- Merge commit :: [[https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/commit/f918373b7be767719264b439bc5bfd95eec1809d][f918373b7b]]
- Labels :: bugfix, correction

** Description
Follows #340. =typst compile= on the PDF from =gh-pr-pdf= failed on a pull request whose title contains =@key=:

#+begin_example
error: label `<key>` does not exist in the document
= PR \#190: ✨ Show the reference of @key links on hover
#+end_example

Typst reads =@name= in text as a reference, and the same happened on the matching commit line. The first version relied on =pandoc= escaping it, which it does in 3.1.3 (the version in the container, where I could not reproduce the error) but evidently not in the version used for the failing run.

**** Changes
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: changes
:END:
- =gh-pr-pdf/.local/bin/gh-pr-pdf=: =@=, =$= and =<= in pull request text are swapped for placeholder characters before =pandoc= sees them and turned into =\u{40}=, =\u{24}= and =\u{3c}= in the Typst source afterwards. That form is valid in running text and inside string arguments such as link targets, so it does not depend on how a given =pandoc= version escapes. Fenced code blocks and inline code keep the real characters.
  - =$...$= is the same kind of clash (Typst math), and =<key>= in text is a label.
- Same file: the Markdown stage no longer reads =$...$= as math (=tex_math_dollars= off). Before, a plain =$HOME/$PATH= in a pull request body was rewritten to a math fragment, which was wrong in the org files too.
- Same file: the script warns with line numbers if an unescaped =@name= is still in the Typst source.
- =gh-pr-pdf/README.org=: the "Safety" section describes the escaping, and "Not run" now says what the failed first run was.

**** Not run
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-run
:END:
=typst compile= (not installed in the container). Checked on made-up JSON modelled on the report: the =@key= title and commit line, =$HOME and $PATH=, =<key>=, an email address, =[cite:@key]=, a table, fenced code (including a nested four-backtick fence), inline code, link targets and a private-use character. The output has no leftover placeholders, the leak scanner finds no unescaped =@name=, and code stays literal. Six unit checks on the escaping function pass. To verify: run =gh-pr-pdf siainbuletin/dotfiles --skip-fetch= again and compile.

Unchanged and worth knowing: Markdown text like =<key>= (outside code) is still dropped, because GitHub's own renderer treats it as an HTML tag and the script removes raw HTML for safety. Put it in backticks and it is kept.

No CHANGELOG edit, per the nightly-tidy rule.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW27ctbJ968Ep7DYfsGqXU6xM][project thread]]/

Follow-up to #335 and #338.

**** Problem
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: problem
:END:
Notes made by the backfill had no Vulpea =:ID:=, no =:CREATED:=, no BibTeX metadata, and the =collection-query-table= block in the book/collection note stayed empty. The likely common cause: the backfill went through =citar-create-note=, and when the =citar-vulpea= source is not the active one citar writes a plain file itself. Such a file never passes through =vulpea-create=, so the =sp-notes= advice (=:CREATED:=) and Vulpea's ID/indexing never ran. The metadata fill and the database update also looked the note up by key instead of by its file, so a miss was only a message.

**** What changes
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what-changes
:END:
- New =sp-litnotes-meta-create-note= (option =sp-litnotes-meta-create-function=): makes the note with =vulpea-create= (ID, =litnote= tag, =ROAM_REFS=, =<key>.org= in the litnotes folder, =:CREATED:=), with the title of =sp-litnotes-meta-new-title=.
- Each note is then filled with =sp-litnotes-meta-fill=, given its file explicitly (authors, title, year, =bib-parent=, =bib-project=, read-status, relevance, priority) and tidied.
- The files are put in the Vulpea database one by one, then the table is created or refreshed. If the query table module does not load, that is now reported instead of skipped.
- Literate doc updated (bullets); three new ERT tests.

**** Testing
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: testing
:END:
- =sp-litnotes-meta= ERT tests pass (16/16, Emacs 29.3, stubbed =vulpea-create=, Vulpea database and author notes). One test runs the real fill and tidy on a stub-made file and checks the ID, =:CREATED:=, title, =pub-author=, =pub-year= and =bib-parent=, and that the file was passed to =vulpea-db-update-file=. =tools/check-tangle.sh= passes.
- Not run with the real Vulpea, citar or vault, and the real table module was not loaded. The cause above is inferred from the symptoms.

**** What is in it
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what-is-in-it
:END:
- =sp-cite-match= (=docs/tangles/academic/sp-cite-match.org=):
  - normalises text and BibTeX fields (accents, casing, ligatures, line-end hyphens);
  - scores surname, year, title and journal, with a DOI shortcut; returns =accept=, =ambiguous= or =none=;
  - splits a selected Bibliography into entries;
  - writes a =Cited works= section between markers (idempotent, shows which works have litnotes);
  - ~org-protocol://sp-cite-match?file=NAME~ handler.
- =sp-reading= (=docs/tangles/academic/sp-reading.org=): citekey to DEVONthink record, open at a page, or index the PDF / open in Preview.
- =hammerspoon/.config/hammerspoon/cite-match.lua=: hotkey (Ctrl+Shift+K) that copies the selection and calls =emacsclient=; loaded from =init.lua= inside a =pcall=.
- ERT tests: =tests/sp-cite-match-test.el= (12), =tests/sp-reading-test.el= (7); all pass on Emacs 29.3 in batch.

- The AppleScript in =sp-reading= (search, =index path ... to=, bulk =uuid of every item=) was written from memory of the dictionary. The module doc lists what to check by hand first.
- The litnote lookup through =citar-has-notes= / =citar-get-notes= with =citar-vulpea=.

:CUSTOM_ID: what-changes

  - lists the citation keys of =ROAM_REFS= as =sp-bib:= links; RET or a click opens the entry in the =.bib= file (=citar-open-entry=);
  - =embark-act= on a key offers the citar actions (entry, files, notes, links, copy reference) through a new embark target finder returning a =citar-key= target; it requires =citar-embark= when embark loads (=sp-citations= already installs it with =:ensure=).
- =:dt-page= column ("DT page"):
  - takes the =crossref= root of each key, its file (=citar-get-files=), and that file's DEVONthink record (same single JXA lookup as =:devonthink=, only when DEVONthink is running);
  - links to ~x-devonthink-item://UUID?page=N~, text "p. 41"; =N= is the first number of =pub-pages= plus an offset, counted from 0 (same convention as =sp-reading= in #343);
  - offset: option =sp-collec-query-dt-page-offset= (default 0), overridden by a =pdf-offset= meta key on the book/collection note;
  - a roman-numeral =pub-pages= links to the PDF ("open").

**** Problem
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: problem
:END:
- BibTeX author =Arthur, Christopher J.= gave the title =J. Arthur (2022) Capital as...= instead of =Arthur (2022) ...=.

**** Cause
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: cause
:END:
- =sp-litnotes-titles--split-name= is the one function that finds the surname. The backfill (=sp-litnotes-meta--new-title=), titles report/convert and the BibTeX-authors path all call it.
- Names are flipped to =First Last= before it runs, so it used its "particle" rule: lower-case words before the last word belong to the surname.
- That test ran with =case-fold-search= on, so the initial =J.= counted as a lower-case particle and went into the surname.

**** Change
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: change
:END:
- Particles are matched case-sensitively, and only whole lower-case words (=van=, =de la=) count.
- Commas are split outside braces only: ={Smith, Jones}, Ann= has surname =Smith, Jones=; =Last, Jr., First= has surname =Last=.
- ={World Bank}= stays one surname; no comma and one word stays as is.
- Tests (=tests/sp-litnotes-titles-test.el=, =tests/sp-litnotes-meta-test.el=): the forms above, =case-fold-search= on and off, BibTeX authors, and the backfill title. 34/34 pass on Emacs 29.3 batch.
- No CHANGELOG edits.

**** Not tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-tested
:END:
- Not run on the real vault; existing litnotes already titled =J. Arthur (...)= are not renamed by this PR (re-run the titles convert/report to fix them).
