- Merged :: 2026-11-09 15:16
- Branch :: =350-gh-pr-pdf-incremental= → =main=
- Merge commit :: [[https://github.com/siainbuletin/dotfiles/commit/7c288277b665a4620cfb3dee8d25c33026a57a2a][7c288277b6]]
- Labels :: enhancement, needs-further-testing

** Description
Follows #340 and #341. =gh-pr-pdf= fetched every pull request again on every run. After the first run it now asks =github-backup= for only what changed.

**** Changes
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: changes
:END:
All in =gh-pr-pdf/= (script and =README.org=, which has a new "Running it again" section).

- Fetching: the script always passes =github-backup -i=. The first run has no checkpoints, so it fetches everything and =github-backup= writes them. Later runs request only new data since the last successful backup.
- =backup/.gh-pr-pdf-state.json= records the last full fetch, the options it used and a hash per rendered pull request. A failed fetch does not move it forward.
- A full fetch is forced:
  - when no earlier one is recorded, or with =--full=;
  - when the options differ from the last run, because =-i= does not backfill a flag that is new;
  - when the last full fetch is older than =--full-every DAYS= (30 by default, 0 turns it off). The =github-backup= documentation warns that a failed earlier run can leave a gap in an incremental backup; this is the cure.
  - A full fetch first deletes =github-backup='s own checkpoint files (=last_update=, =reviews_last_update=) in =backup/=, so it is not cut short by an older checkpoint.
- Rendering: an org file is rebuilt only when the JSON of its pull request changed (or the renderer did), since =pandoc= runs several times per pull request. Org files of pull requests that vanish from the backup are removed. The PDF is still built from all the org files, a local step that does not use the API.
- Discussions stay a full fetch each time (one query per 25 discussions).
- The progress line says which mode ran and why, for example =fetching pull requests: incremental (last full fetch 3 days ago, ...)=.

**** Not run
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-run
:END:
=github-backup= is not installed in the container and there is no way to install it, so the incremental mode was run against a stand-in that logs how it is called and writes checkpoint files the way its documentation describes. Covered: first run, an unchanged rerun (0 rendered, 3 unchanged), one changed pull request (1 rendered), =--full= (checkpoints deleted first), changed options, a 40-day-old state against 29 days, =--full-every 0=, a failed fetch (state unchanged), a pull request that vanishes, and a corrupt state file.

Not seen, and worth checking on a real run:

- How =github-backup= applies =-i= to pull requests, and whether it fetches the comments and commits of one that changed (the PyPI page only says that it requests new data since the last successful backup).
- That it fetches everything when it finds no checkpoint, which the first run and every full fetch rely on.
- Quick check: compare the API requests of the second run with the first (=gh api rate_limit= before and after).

=typst compile= is still not run in the container either (see #341).

No CHANGELOG edit, per the nightly-tidy rule.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW25KWiJPRkGcgDQT8pc4YUMR][project thread]]/

Follows #352 (merged). Sia listed three fixes but said "two buttons"; I made three.

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
- The lint report (=sp-bibtex-lint-dryrun=) has one button per fix, each with the number of entries it would change. A button is a =sp-bibtex-lint:KIND:FILE= Org link, so =RET= runs it.
- Three commands, one per fix (one =.bib= file, batches of =sp-bibtex-lint-batch-size= = 50, apply/skip/quit per batch, backup before the first write, nothing written without an answer):
  - =sp-bibtex-lint-fix-order=: fields in the order of =sp-bibtex-field-order=; values untouched.
  - =sp-bibtex-lint-fix-indent=: every entry laid out by =bibtex-fill-entry=, the =bibtex-mode= standard.
  - =sp-bibtex-lint-fix-authors=, three steps:
    1. names that are not =Last, First= are rewritten
    2. names one typo away from an author note
    3. names with the surname of an author note (below)
  - For steps 2 and 3, per batch: =n= normalises the name in the BibTeX field to the note's name, =l= adds the name as a vulpea alias of the note (the =.bib= is not changed), =e= asks for each name, =s= skips, =q= quits.
- Surname matches (step 3), a kind of match of its own:
  - the report lists them in their own section with their own count, so they do not bury the typos
  - same surname, and given names that fit the note's name by name: =TW Adorno=, =T. W. Adorno= and =Theodor Adorno= fit =Theodor W. Adorno=; =Michael Smith= is not =John Smith=, and =W Adorno= or =Theodor L. Adorno= are not =Theodor W. Adorno=
  - several notes with the surname: those with as many given names as the BibTeX name are preferred (=TW Adorno= is =Theodor W. Adorno=, not =Tamara Adorno=); if more than one is left (=T Adorno=) the name is ambiguous, listed in its own section with the candidates, and never changed or aliased
  - a name that is a typo of a note stays a typo match; a name that is a note's name or alias is not flagged

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
Improves #280: when the =crossref='ed entry has no literature note, =bib-parent= is no longer left out. The note is made and linked.

- The parent is matched by its citation key (the =ROAM_REFS= key), never by title.
- A missing parent is made without asking, by =sp-litnotes-meta-create-function=, the same path =sp-litnotes-meta-backfill-children= and =-all-children= use:
  - =vulpea-create= with an ID, =:CREATED:=, =ROAM_REFS=, the =litnote= tag and the BibTeX type tag (=sp-bibtex-types=)
  - filled from its own BibTeX entry, given a plain title, and put in the Vulpea database
- =sp-litnotes-meta-fill= (single) and =sp-litnotes-meta-fill-all-convert= (batch from #348) both do this.
- Batch: each missing parent is made once, however many notes cross-reference it (=sp-litnotes-meta--made-parents=). It is counted in the one-time questions and in the final message.
- Dry run: new "Parent notes to make" section (each parent once, with the notes that link it), a count line, and "(new note)" on the =bib-parent= lines.
- Deep chains are flagged and avoided:
  - A normal crossref is =child -> parent= and the parent has no crossref. =child -> parent -> grandparent= (loops and self-references included) is flagged.
  - For such a note the fill and the batch convert nothing: no =bib-parent=, no parent note, even if the parent already has a note.
  - The dry run has a count line and a section "Crossref chains deeper than two levels" listing each chain; the single command prints a message.
  - New =M-x sp-litnotes-meta-fill-deep-chain= converts one flagged note on purpose: it shows the chain, asks once, fills the note and links or makes its direct parent. The parent is filled by the normal rules, so a loop is cut there. There is no batch version.
- A parent key with no BibTeX entry is left out with a message.
- =sp-litnotes-meta-offer-parent= became =sp-litnotes-meta-create-parent= (default t, old name kept as an obsolete alias). Set it to nil to get the old "leave it out" behaviour. The =y-or-n-p= question and the =citar-create-note= route are gone.

:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tests
:END:
- 37 tests in =tests/sp-litnotes-meta-test.el= pass in Emacs 29 (the old "offer to create" test was replaced by new ones):
  - parent made silently and filled, linked, not made again on a second run
  - existing parent not made; option off leaves the line out
  - deep chains (loop, self-reference, parent with a note) make nothing; detection of one-hop chains
  - the dry run lists a parent once for two children and flags a chain; the convert makes a parent once and converts nothing for a chain
  - =sp-litnotes-meta-fill-deep-chain=: declined, converted (makes =b= then =c=), loop cut at the parent, refuses a normal note

- New module =sp-backup-lookup= (doc =docs/tangles/funct/sp-backup-lookup.org=, tests tangled from it).
- =sp-backup-lookup-list FILE=: finds the backups of a file in every module's backup folder, newest first.
- =M-x sp-backup-open=: pick a backup of the current file and open it read-only.
- =M-x sp-backup-diff=: diff a backup against the file (prefix: Ediff).
- In batch reports: =b= opens and =D= diffs a backup of the file linked on the line at point.

**** Why one lookup
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: why-one-lookup
:END:
- Each module keeps its own backup folder and layout (=STAMP/name=, =name.STAMP=, =STAMP/full/path=, =STAMP/files/...=).
- Modules are unchanged; the lookup reads all of them through =sp-backup-lookup-directories= (BibTeX lint, litnote titles/meta/refs, meta order, footnote lint, author notes, notes filing).
- Backups with only a name (=STAMP/name=) cannot be told apart by folder, so same-named notes are all listed.

- 7 ERT tests on fake backup folders in each layout (Emacs 29.3), plus the existing batch-report tests.

- Batch fill (=-fill-all-dryrun= / =-convert=): a quoted title is its own category ("Quoted pub-title", counted and listed with old -> new). Convert removes the quotes with the existing backup, batch of 50, pick/choose and drop-and-stash handling. =sp-litnotes-meta-fill= (single note) does it too.
- The BibTeX title is read without enclosing quotes (={"Title"}=), so the changed-field update from #361 cannot reintroduce them.
- New =M-x sp-litnotes-meta-title-lint-dryrun= / =-convert= (on =sp-batch-report=, like the bib-parent lint) also reach notes with no citation key or no .bib entry.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW28CHnH1Ew1Kqrdet3ZGPrWT][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
New module =sp-see-also= (academic): reads the "see also" reminders I leave in litnotes as inline footnotes, =[fn::[[id:...][Concept]]]=, and ranks them. Literate doc: =docs/tangles/academic/sp-see-also.org=.

- *Scanner* (=sp-see-also-parse-buffer=): finds inline footnotes with an =id:= link and records the context of each: =quote= or =prose=, and the open question heading above it (keywords come from =sp-org-keywords-research=, so =QUESTION SCOPING READING SYNTHESIZING REVIEW= are open; =STABLE ANSWERED DROPPED= are closed).
- *No buffers visited*: files are read with =insert-file-contents= into a temp buffer in =fundamental-mode= (no hooks, no =org-mode=, no =org-element=). A test checks its footnote ranges against =org-element=. Unsaved open buffers are read from the buffer.
- *Cache*: per file, keyed by mtime and size, kept in =var/cache/see-also-index.eld=; reset when the keywords change. Vulpea gives the litnote list, the titles, and (via =vulpea-db-query-links-to=) the files that link to a concept, so a concept lookup reads only those. The whole-vault index is the fallback.
- *Priority*: two replaceable functions, =sp-see-also-concept-score-function= and =sp-see-also-question-priority-function=. Default: mention weight (prose 1, quote 2, plus the keyword weight when under an open question), times =1 + ln(1 + other litnotes)=.
- *Dashboards*: a =see-also= vulpea-ui widget (concepts by score, then open questions) and a =concept-usage= widget plus =#+BEGIN: concept-usage= dynamic block (litnote, where, under, context).

**** Measured
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: measured
:END:
Synthetic vault of 300 files (about 100 KB each), Emacs 29.3 batch: cold 0.65 s, warm from the disk cache 0.02 s.

**** Tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tested
:END:
17 ERT tests (=tests/sp-see-also-test.el=, all pass): context classification, org-element agreement, cache hit/miss/keyword reset, unsaved buffers, no buffer left behind, scoring, hook replacement, dblock output.

**** Not tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-tested
:END:
- The vulpea-ui widgets (no =vui= in the cloud container; the file only reads cleanly) and the real =vulpea-db-query-links-to= shape.
- Anything against the real vault.
- The original "General academic system" conversation could not be opened from this project, so the design is built from the request.

**** Notes for the sidenote PR
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: notes-for-the-sidenote-pr
:END:
=sp-see-also-parse-buffer= is the shared footnote parser (=:beg :end :label :text :links= plus context). =sp-reading-mode= / ox-tufte should call it rather than parse footnotes again.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2WiuK3EYFXxFgYTNmw2q6y3][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
New module =sp-reading-sidenotes= (ui), doc =docs/tangles/ui/sp-reading-sidenotes.org=, tests =tests/sp-reading-sidenotes-test.el=.

- In =sp-reading-mode=, each see-also footnote (=[fn::[[id:...][Concept]]]=) shows as a small number in the text and as a Tufte-style sidenote in the right margin. The file is not changed (overlays only).
- Footnotes come from =sp-see-also-parse-buffer= (#366), no second parser.
- The note starts on the line of its number, wraps in the margin (=sp-reading-sidenote-margin=, 30 columns), and moves down if it would overlap the previous one. It is redone on window changes, text scale and edits (idle timer).
- Turns on/off with =sp-reading-mode= (=sp-reading-sidenotes=), or alone with =C-c w s=. The right margin is widened while it is on and restored afterwards. Narrow windows keep the plain footnotes.
- =M-x sp-reading-sidenotes-export= exports the note with =ox-tufte= (installed via =use-package= + Elpaca =:ensure=) and opens the HTML.

**** Notes
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: notes
:END:
- *Stacked on #366* (base branch =claude/project-thread-7yi4nb=); retarget to =main= after it merges.
- =ox-tufte= is an export backend, so it cannot draw in an Emacs window: the on-screen sidenotes use the Emacs margin display, and ox-tufte makes the matching HTML. It turns every inline footnote into a sidenote, not only see-also ones.
- The frame is not resized for the wider margin; the text column narrows instead.
- No CHANGELOG edits (nightly tidy).

**** Tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tested
:END:
- 13 ERT tests (Emacs 29.3 batch, all pass): scanning through the parser, link text, margin line wrapping, overlay creation/removal, no overlap, narrow window, margin set/restore, following reading mode.
- A manual ox-tufte export of a footnote produced a =sidenote-number= label.
- Not seen in a real GUI frame: the actual look, wrapping, and =vertical-motion= placement on screen are untried. The vault and DEVONthink are not involved.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2Db7bsg1hCv2KPFwMY6tc5L][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
- =org-semantic-binary-install= failed with =Wrong type argument: number-or-marker-p, "Killed: 9"=.
  - macOS SIGKILLed the freshly copied binary when the installer ran =--version=.
  - =process-file= returns a string on a signal, and the package calls =zerop= on it.
- =sp-semantic.el= now:
  - deletes the old binary before an install, so the new copy gets a fresh inode;
  - wraps =org-semantic-binary-version=: on that error it removes the quarantine flag, signs ad hoc (=codesign --force --sign -=), and retries once;
  - installs the binary under =var/org-semantic/= (git-ignored) instead of the top of the config.
- The 40 MB binary was tracked in the repo and symlinked by Stow, so installs wrote through the symlink into the repo. It is deleted from the tree here.
- Doc updated in =docs/tangles/academic/sp-semantic.org= (bullet list) with the tangled =.el=.

**** After merging
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: after-merging
:END:
- Remove the dangling symlink =~/.config/emacs-modular/org-semantic/org-semantic= (and the empty dir), restow, then run =M-x org-semantic-binary-install=.

**** Not tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-tested
:END:
- Emacs and macOS are not available in the container, so none of this was run.
- The upstream bug (=zerop= on =process-file=) is in alberti42/org-semantic and is only worked around here.

No CHANGELOG edits (nightly tidy).

- Branch :: =371-bibtex-name-prefixes= → =main=

- Labels :: correction

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2TfB2nqvpwE54WgLSuyy8aW][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
An old Zotero export wrote names with a prefix as =biblatex= key=value text, e.g. ~family=Hayek given=Friedrich given=Friedrich ..., given=Friedrich A., prefix=von useprefix=false~. This adds a separate operation to =sp-bibtex-lint= that fixes them.

- New command =sp-bibtex-lint-fix-prefixes=, also in =sp-bibtex-lint-convert= (as "name prefixes") and as a button in the dry-run report. =sp-bibtex-lint-dryrun= now lists these entries (with links to the file lines) and counts them.
- Key=value names (~family=~, ~given=~, ~prefix=~, ~suffix=~, ~useprefix=~), also wrapped in braces and in any order:
  - become the lint's own form, =von Hayek, Friedrich A.= (the module standard is =Last, First=; the existing author fix would turn =Friedrich A. von Hayek= into that anyway)
  - repeated ~given=~ parts are merged; a part that fits a longer one (=Friedrich=, =F.= for =Friedrich A.=) is dropped and the fullest stays
  - =useprefix= is ignored, =suffix= goes in the middle (=Smith, Jr., John=)
  - names it cannot read (no ~family=~, two different families, given names that do not fit) are reported and left as they are
- Misplaced prefixes in names that already have a comma move in front of the last name: =Hayek, Friedrich A. von=, =Hayek von, Friedrich=, =Hayek, Friedrich A., von= give =von Hayek, Friedrich A.=; =de la= moves together. Only lower-case particles of =sp-bibtex-name-particles= move and one given name always stays (=Li, Bin= is untouched).
- Same pattern as the other fixes: backup before the first write, batches of =sp-bibtex-lint-batch-size= (50) with apply / skip / drop some / bring back / quit, and now =g= (apply this and all later batches, as in #368). =g= also works in step 1 of the author-name fix. Dropped entries stay out of a global run.
- Literate doc updated in =docs/tangles/academic/sp-academic.org= (bullet lists) and the =.el= tangled from it.

**** Tests
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tests
:END:
- 12 new ERT tests in =tests/sp-bibprocess-lint-test.el=: the Hayek example, parts parsing, given-name merging, suffix, particles, field linting, the dry-run report, convert with a backup, batches with =g=, drops. The whole file passes (52/52) on Emacs 29.3 with stubs.
- Not run on the Mac or on the real =.bib= files; try =M-x sp-bibtex-lint-dryrun= first.

No CHANGELOG edits (nightly tidy).

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2PP5G5M6XUy3ezceVz378Pm][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
A separate fix in =sp-bibtex-lint= for attachment paths: =M-x sp-bibtex-lint-fix-files=, a button in =sp-bibtex-lint-dryrun= (section "Attachment paths") and an entry in =sp-bibtex-lint-convert=.

- BibDesk =bdsk-file-N= fields (base64 bookmark) become one ~file = {...}~ field; several files are joined with =;=, an existing plain =file= field is extended.
  - The bookmark's old relative path gives a file name, looked up anywhere below =sp-literature-dir= (case and accents ignored); it must match exactly one file.
  - Otherwise the only PDF whose name, minus BibDesk's trailing digit, equals the citekey is used.
  - Entries that cannot be resolved keep their fields and are listed as problems.
- Absolute =~/Documents/literature/...= paths (typos of =Documents= accepted) become relative to =sp-literature-dir=; a path whose file is elsewhere in the library is pointed at it.
- Same pattern as the other fixes: whole file, one question, backup first, only the attachment fields change.
- =sp-bibtex-files-flatten= (default nil) also moves the files to the top of the library and writes the bare name.
- =sp-bibtex-files-devonthink-tool= (default nil): path of the new =tools/devonthink-move.py=. With it, the move goes through DEVONthink (one call per fix), so records keep their UUID, tags and annotations and =x-devonthink-item://= / =#+devonthink:= links keep working. If the tool stops, the =.bib= file is not written.

**** New: tools/devonthink-move.py
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: new-toolsdevonthink-movepy
:END:
- =move= (dry run unless =--apply=): =--library DIR --flatten SUBDIR...= or =--moves FILE= (FROMTO pairs, the format =sp-bibtex-files= logs). Each file is moved with DEVONthink's own =move=; afterwards the record is read back and the run stops at the first one whose UUID or path is not as expected. Files DEVONthink does not index are left alone, or renamed with =--plain-rename=. A manifest of the moves goes to =~/.local/state/devonthink-move/=.
- =check NOTES_DIR...=: lists the UUIDs in notes (=x-devonthink-item://=, =devonthink:=, =#+devonthink:=) that DEVONthink does not know; run it before and after.
- Literate doc =docs/tangles/academic/devonthink-move.org= (bullet lists), tangled to the tool and =tests/test_devonthink_move.py=.

**** Tests
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tests
:END:
- =tests/sp-bibprocess-lint-test.el=: 49/49 on Emacs 29.3 (bookmark decoding also checked against two real bookmarks; flatten with rename and with a faked tool, including the tool stopping).
- =python3 -m unittest tests/test_devonthink_move.py=: 13 tests with DEVONthink faked.

**** Not tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-tested
:END:
- =devonthink-move.py= has not been run against DEVONthink. The JXA calls (=lookupRecordsWithPath=, =getRecordWithUuid=, =move=) and the assumption that moving an indexed record into the group of another folder of the same indexed hierarchy moves the file on disk are unverified. Try =check=, then =move ... --apply --limit 1=, then =check= again. If the file does not move, the read-back fails and the run stops with the file where it was.
- Nothing was run on the Mac or on the real =.bib= files; try =M-x sp-bibtex-lint-dryrun= first.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW26Aw8C4fzJzTVx3iwKGHPXu][project thread]]/

**** Cause
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: cause
:END:
- The message =None of the files for 'KEY' exist; check 'citar-library-paths'...= comes from =citar-file--parse-file-field= (it is a =message=, not a raised error). The =file= field points to =~/Documents/literature/KEY.pdf=, but the PDF is somewhere else below the library (e.g. =inbox/mac-bibdesk/=), so citar finds nothing and the table's PDF column and =citar-open= come up empty.

**** Changes
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: changes
:END:
- New parser =sp-citations-parser-library=, added to =citar-file-parser-functions= (in the =citar= =:config=):
  - for each name in the =file= field that does not exist (absolute, or relative to =sp-literature-dir=), it looks for a file of the same name below =sp-literature-dir= (case and accent insensitive);
  - names that exist are left to citar's own parsers.
- Index of =sp-literature-dir= is built on first use and rebuilt (at most every =sp-citations-library-index-ttl= = 60 s) when a name is not found. Hidden folders and the backup folder are skipped.
- This replaces my first attempt (a try/catch fallback in the query tables), which is reverted. =citar-open=, =citar-get-files= and the =:pdf= column now all find the same files.
- Doc: =sp-academic.org= (sp-citations section).

**** Not verified
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-verified
:END:
- Tried the parser alone in Emacs 29 with citar's default parser stubbed (finds =inbox/mac/Foo-2001.pdf= for =~/Documents/literature/foo-2001.pdf=; ignores existing and truly missing names); the tangle check passes. Not run with real citar or on the vault.
- Does not fix the paths in the =.bib= files; =sp-bibtex-lint-fix-files= (#372) does.

** Description
Adds a macOS Stow package =devonthink-open=.

- =dt-open= looks each PDF up in every open DEVONthink database (=lookup records with path=, as in the DT forum threads) and opens the =x-devonthink-item://= link; PDFs that are not indexed go to a fallback viewer (Preview, configurable) and never to DEVONthink.
- =dt-open-install= builds =DT Open PDF.app= (an applet that calls =dt-open=), registers it for =com.adobe.pdf= and makes it the default PDF viewer, so Finder double-click and Alfred's file picker both use it. =--uninstall= restores the previous default.
- Not run on a Mac. Tested here: bash syntax and =dt-open='s decisions against stand-ins for =osascript=/=open=. Untested: the AppleScript lookup, =osacompile=/=PlistBuddy=/=codesign=, and LaunchServices registration.

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
Authors or editors that are organisations (e.g. the Endnotes collective, technically anonymous) were read as =Last, First= personal names. Now:

- A BibTeX name in double braces, ={{Endnotes}}=, is an organisation, in =.bib= files and in =pub-author= / =pub-editor= values.
- New defcustom =sp-author-notes-organisations=: names that are organisations even without braces (ignoring case and accents).
- An organisation is never flipped from =Last, First=, so ={{Doe, Roe Press}}= keeps its comma.
- =and= and =;= inside braces no longer split a name (={{Marx and Engels Institute}}=), in both =sp-author-notes= and =sp-author-notes-bibtex=.
- An organisation matches BibTeX authors by its whole name only, not by last name and initial.
- The note made for an organisation gets the =person= tag plus the =institution= tag (already in =sp-org-tag-registry=; setting =sp-author-notes-organisation-tag=), so Works tables and BibTeX commands keep working.
- A note tagged only =institution= is found and linked as an author note.
- The code lives in =docs/tangles/funct/sp-org-lint.org=; the =.el= files are re-tangled from it.

**** Tests
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tests
:END:
- New ERT tests for braces, splitting, cleaning, parsing, note creation and BibTeX matching.
- All 52 tests in the two author-notes test files pass (Emacs 29.3).

**** Notes

:CUSTOM_ID: notes
:END:
- Not run on the real vault.
- CHANGELOG not edited (nightly tidy writes it).
- The branch could not be renamed with the PR-number prefix from the cloud session.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2BwDJuqNETEyCwswgX8zTyT][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
- =sp-litnotes-meta-backfill-all-children= already inserted a =collection-query-table= block for a book or collection; it now also picks the right view for a reference work or an encyclopedia (by the BibTeX type tag, =sp-litnotes-meta-parent-views=).
- New command =M-x sp-litnotes-meta-refresh-all-tables= refreshes every chapter table in the vault in one go:
  - Syncs the Vulpea database first (=sp-litnotes-meta-refresh-sync=), since the DB can lag.
  - Parents are found from the chapters: every =bib-parent= of a note tagged =booksection=, =incollection=, =inreference= or =encyclopedia=. So an encyclopedia article whose parent is tagged =encyclopedia= or =collection= gets its table in either case.
  - A parent without a block gets one above its first heading; a tagged note with no chapters and no block is left alone.
  - =C-u= is a dry run. A summary buffer lists tables added, changed, unchanged, failures, and =bib-parent= ids missing from the database.
- New built-in views =reference-entries= and =encyclopedia-articles= (sorted by title; entries have no pages).
- =sp-bibtex-types-tag-alist= now maps =inreference=, =reference=, =mvreference=.
- =sp-collec-query-check-rules= takes a list of parent tags per child tag, with rules for =inreference= (reference or book) and =encyclopedia= (encyclopedia or collection), so the =:check= column does not flag them.

**** Assumptions to confirm
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: assumptions-to-confirm
:END:
- A reference manual is tagged =reference= (or =book=) and its entries =inreference=; an encyclopedia is tagged =encyclopedia=. All configurable via the options above.

**** Tests
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tests
:END:
- New ERT tests (Emacs 29.3): check rules, and refresh-all with stubbed Vulpea (dry run, insert, update, missing parent, second run unchanged). All 56 litnotes-meta and 32 query-table tests pass.
- Not run on the real vault. Docs are in =sp-litnotes-meta.org=; =.el= files re-tangled from the docs.
- CHANGELOG not edited (nightly tidy writes it).

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2TznfzA82m9ah28peK3HRxx][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
- A heading titled =See also= (any case), with its subtree, is now a see-also section.
- Every =id:= link in it is a mention of that concept, in list items or plain text.
- Mentions have =:where= = =section= (weight 1.5, in =sp-see-also-where-weights=).

**** Scope
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: scope
:END:
- The scope is the parent of the section: the nearest ancestor with an =:ID:=.
- At the bottom of the file (no ID'd ancestor) it belongs to the file.
- An =:ID:= on the =See also= heading itself is ignored.
- The open question above it counts, as for footnotes.

**** How
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: how
:END:
- Reuses the footnote scanner: =sp-see-also-parse-buffer= gains an optional =SECTIONS= argument.
- =sp-see-also-mentions-in-buffer= (cache and index) passes it, so =sp-see-also-show=, =sp-see-also-show-concept=, and the widgets and =concept-usage= block show them.
- The sidenote renderer is unchanged: it calls the parser without =SECTIONS=.
- Links already read as footnotes inside a section, and links in source/comment blocks, are not counted twice or at all.
- Cache version 3, so files are re-read; editing a section re-reads only that file.
- Literate source =sp-see-also.org= updated and re-tangled (new section "See also" sections, weights, tests).

**** Tests
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tests
:END:
- 5 new ERT tests on fixtures; 25/25 pass in batch on Emacs 29.3.
- *Not run on the real vault* or in a GUI/vulpea-ui.
- Known limit: a heading in all capitals (=SEE ALSO=) is not matched (the existing title parser reads the first capital word as a keyword).
- Branch is not number-prefixed: the number was unknown before creating the PR and the rename API is blocked.

** Description
Requested: PDFs should open in a separate DEVONthink window instead of the small viewer beneath the database view, and several PDFs must be possible at once.

- =openInDatabases= now calls DEVONthink's =open window for record= and =activate=, instead of =open location= with the =x-devonthink-item://= link (which replaced the previous PDF in the main window's viewer).
- Several PDFs: a Finder selection sent in one event is handled one after the other, each getting a window.
- =DT_OPEN_MODE= (window/reveal) is removed from the code, the config and the docs.
- Handlers renamed: =openInDEVONthink=, =findAndOpen=, =openInDatabases= (true/false instead of a link).
- Not run on a Mac. Not checked: what DEVONthink does when a window for that record is already open.

**** Cause
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: cause
:END:
- =sp-collection-query-book.el= ran =(with-eval-after-load 'vulpea-ui (require 'sp-collection-query-book-widget))= *before* its own =(provide ...)=.
- =sp-org-ext= loads =vulpea-ui= before =sp-collection-query=, so the =with-eval-after-load= body ran immediately.
- The widget file requires =sp-collection-query-book=, which was not yet provided, so the require recursed.

**** Fix
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: fix
:END:
- Move =(provide 'sp-collection-query-book)= above the =with-eval-after-load= block.
- Same change in the literate source =docs/tangles/funct/sp-collection-query.org=, with a bullet explaining why.

**** Checked
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: checked
:END:
- All =require=/=provide= names in the =sp-collection-query*= modules match their file names; no old =vulpea-collection= module names remain in them.
- No other cycle in the require graph.

**** Not tested
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-tested
:END:
- No Emacs in the cloud container, so the modules were not loaded in batch. Please start Emacs once to confirm =sp-org-ext= loads.

** Description
/Requested by *Sia* · [[https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2SRHUWz5F2if6VxPkp4VonS][project thread]]/

**** What
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what
:END:
- =gh-pr-pdf= now starts every PR on a new page in the PDF.
- It no longer fails to build the PDF on PR text where inline code is followed by =.name=.

**** Cause
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: cause
:END:
- The committed =.typ= (366 PRs, pandoc and Typst 0.15) compiles with every PR, so the org files and that snapshot are fine.
- A fresh re-render of the same backup with pandoc 3.9 failed in =typst compile= with =raw does not have field "el"=.
  - pandoc writes inline code as =#raw("...")=.
  - Typst reads =#raw("...").el= as field access, not as text.
  - PRs #64, #93, #176 and #271 trigger it: their source has nested backticks, so pandoc leaves =.el= or =.gitignore= right after the span.
- The failed compile left the previous PDF in place, so the PDF looked current but lacked the newer PRs, and compiling again fails the same way.
- I could not see Sia's PDF, so this is the cause I reproduced, not a proven match for their exact output.

**** Changes
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: changes
:END:
- =harden_typst= puts a zero-width space after =#raw(...)= when =.letter= follows. Only =#raw= calls are touched (table code such as =(auto, auto).at(col)= needs its dot).
- The preamble gets =#show heading.where(level: 1)= with a weak =pagebreak=: one PR (or discussion) per page.
- The old PDF is deleted before =typst compile=, so a failure cannot leave a stale one.
- =README.org= documents the three points as bullets.

**** Checked
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: checked
:END:
- Re-rendered all 366 PRs from the committed backup with pandoc 3.9 and Typst 0.15: PDF builds, 507 pages (was 294), all 366 PR headings present, each starting its own page.

**** Not checked
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: not-checked
:END:
- Not run on Sia's Mac, so their pandoc and Typst versions were not tried.
- With pandoc 3.1.3 the Typst build fails with =expected colon=, with or without this change. This is a separate pandoc-version problem, not touched here.
- No =CHANGELOG.org= change, per the rules.
- The branch name has no PR-number prefix (the branch is fixed by the environment).
